rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Definitions
rows.groupTitle: Agricultural land, registered agricultural land, and supporting defined terms
rows.groupReason: The two-prong test for agricultural land (currently used or regulation-designated as suitable) plus the shorter supporting definitions (registered agricultural land, drain, land use control law, local government, Minister, agricultural land owners association) form the remaining operative vocabulary.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two-prong test for agricultural land and identify the scope of each supporting defined term, including the section 8 registration link for registered agricultural land and the Community Planning Act instruments captured by land use control law.

evidenceText: "agricultural land" means (terre agricole) (a) land being used in an agricultural operation, or (b) land that is not being used in an agricultural operation but that meets the criteria set by regulation as land suitable for use in an agricultural operation
"registered agricultural land" means agricultural land that is registered by the Minister under section 8

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 1 contains two distinct recall tasks: the 14-category enumeration of 'agricultural operation' with its gain/reward requirement, and the set of supporting definitions (agricultural land two-prong test, registered agricultural land, drain, land use control law, local government, Minister) that establish the Act's remaining vocabulary.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Definitions
rows.groupTitle: Agricultural operation: definition and enumerated activities
rows.groupReason: The 14 enumerated activity categories (clearing through prescribed activities) plus the overarching gain/reward requirement form one large, independently recallable definition that drives the scope of the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the gain-or-reward requirement and the 14 enumerated categories (a) through (n) that define an agricultural operation, including the regulatory catch-all in (n).

evidenceText: "agricultural operation" means an agricultural operation that is carried on for gain or reward or in the hope or expectation of gain or reward, and includes
(n) any other agricultural activity or process prescribed by regulation
that is carried on for gain or reward or in the hope or expectation of gain or reward

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 1 contains two distinct recall tasks: the 14-category enumeration of 'agricultural operation' with its gain/reward requirement, and the set of supporting definitions (agricultural land two-prong test, registered agricultural land, drain, land use control law, local government, Minister) that establish the Act's remaining vocabulary.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Application for letters of incorporation
rows.groupTitle: Formation and incorporation application for agricultural land owners associations
rows.groupReason: Subsections 2(1) and 2(2) together state the permission to form the association and the regulatory application requirement for letters of incorporation; they answer a single recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the permissive basis for forming an agricultural land owners association and the regulatory application required before letters of incorporation may be issued.
rows.sourceMapReason: The two subsections form one coherent incorporation mechanism: the permissive basis for forming an agricultural land owners association and the application-based trigger for issuing letters of incorporation.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Certificate constituting letters of incorporation
rows.groupTitle: Minister's registration, certification, and the certificate as letters of incorporation
rows.groupReason: The three subsections form one sequential incorporation mechanism ending in the certificate's legal effect as letters of incorporation and conclusive evidence.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the Minister's duties on registration and issuance of the certificate, and state that the certificate constitutes the letters of incorporation and is conclusive evidence of compliance with incorporation requirements.

evidenceText: the Minister shall register the application for letters of incorporation
the Minister shall issue a certificate to the effect that the agricultural land owners association is incorporated under this Act and the regulations

shall constitute the letters of incorporation of that agricultural land owners association and shall be conclusive evidence that all the requirements of this Act and the regulations respecting incorporation have been complied with

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 3 is a short, self-contained incorporation mechanism: the Minister's sequential duties to register and issue a certificate, plus the certificate's legal effect as letters of incorporation and conclusive evidence. The three subsections form one interdependent procedural chain best recalled as a single unit.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Objects and purposes of an agricultural land owners association
rows.groupTitle: Objects and purposes of an agricultural land owners association
rows.groupReason: All four purposes define the single operative scope of the association and are best recalled together.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the four objects and purposes of an agricultural land owners association, including the residual clause authorizing activities directed by the Lieutenant-Governor in Council.

evidenceText: to promote and facilitate the stewardship, protection and improvement of agricultural land

to facilitate the provision and distribution of water sources and supply systems for irrigation for agricultural land and to manage the construction, operation and maintenance of water supply and distribution
to carry out such other activities or duties as may be authorized or required under this Act or as the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may direct

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 4 is a short, cohesive enumeration of the objects and purposes of an agricultural land owners association; all four items answer the same recall question and should be learned as one unit.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Powers of an agricultural land owners association
rows.groupTitle: Legal capacity of an agricultural land owners association
rows.groupReason: One coherent rule: the association has natural-person capacity, scoped to its objects and purposes and subject to the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an agricultural land owners association has the capacity and the rights, powers, and privileges of a natural person, in respect of its objects and purposes and subject to this Act.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 5 is a single, self-contained capacity clause granting the association the rights, powers, and privileges of a natural person, limited to its objects and purposes and subject to the Act.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: By-laws
rows.groupTitle: By-law making power and Regulations Act exclusion for agricultural land owners associations
rows.groupReason: The by-law power and its Regulations Act carve-out are inseparable: recalling one without the other gives an incomplete picture of the association's internal governance authority.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an agricultural land owners association may make by-laws for the control and management of its business and affairs, and that the Regulations Act does not apply to such by-laws.

evidenceText: An agricultural land owners association may make by-laws for the control and management of the business and affairs of the agricultural land owners association.
The Regulations Act does not apply to a by-law made under subsection (1).

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 6 grants a specific by-law making power to agricultural land owners associations and excludes the Regulations Act from those by-laws; the two subsections are tightly interdependent and form one small recall unit.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Advisory functions of agricultural land owners association
rows.groupTitle: Advisory functions of agricultural land owners association (s. 7)
rows.groupReason: The four advisory permissions form one recall unit: the scope of the association's advisory role to local government and the Minister.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the four advisory functions an agricultural land owners association may perform and the actor(s) it advises in each case.

evidenceText: advise a local government on the installation of facilities or services on or near registered agricultural land
advise the Minister and local government on acceptable management practices for agricultural operations

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 7 is a short, single-modality permission provision: an agricultural land owners association may advise specified actors on four parallel agricultural/land-use topics. All items share one legal operation and answer one recall question.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Registration of agricultural land
rows.groupTitle: Minister's duty to maintain the agricultural lands registry
rows.groupReason: Covers the Minister's two-part duty to maintain the registry and to register or remove agricultural lands, both subject to regulations.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Minister's statutory duty to establish, maintain, register, and remove agricultural lands from the registry, and note that the duty operates in accordance with the regulations.

evidenceText: The Minister shall, in accordance with the regulations, (a) establish and maintain a registry of agricultural lands, (b) register agricultural lands and remove agricultural lands from the registry.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 8 states the Minister's statutory duty to establish and maintain the agricultural lands registry and to register or remove lands, in accordance with regulations. It is a short, single-actor duty provision with modest but independent recall value as the foundation of the registration scheme.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Application for registration of agricultural land
rows.groupTitle: Application to register agricultural land
rows.groupReason: Establishes the applicant's standing (ownership of the land) and the regulatory framework governing the application process.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may apply to register agricultural land and the regulatory basis for making the application.
rows.sourceMapReason: Short permission provision establishing that only an owner may apply to register agricultural land, subject to regulations; minimal but operative legal rule with an ownership prerequisite.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Recommendation by the Minister
rows.groupTitle: Minister's power to recommend agricultural land for land use control
rows.groupReason: One discretionary power with defined actor, recipients, conditions, and purpose forms a single coherent recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Minister's power to recommend that unregistered agricultural land deemed suitable be considered for inclusion in a land use control law, and identify the permitted recipients and the two qualifying conditions (not registered under section 8; suitable as agricultural land in the Minister's opinion).

evidenceText: The Minister may recommend to the Minister of Local Government or a local government that agricultural land that is not registered under section 8 but that is, in the opinion of the Minister, suitable as agricultural land be considered for inclusion in the appropriate land use control law.

rows.sourceMapReason: A single-sentence discretionary power provision with one recall task: the Minister's authority to recommend unregistered, suitable agricultural land for inclusion in a land use control law.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Construction of ditches and drains
rows.groupTitle: Application for drainage permission and deposit requirement
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) form a rule/condition pair: who may apply, the triggering necessity condition, and the deposit prerequisite before the Minister may grant permission and the obligation to pay it out.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may apply for permission to construct a ditch or drain through adjacent property, the necessity condition for application, and the deposit requirement that must be met before the Minister may grant permission.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 12 contains two independently recallable concepts: the application right with its deposit prerequisite (12(1)–(2)) and a substantial seven-item list of Minister's powers (12(3)). A learner would reasonably be tested on the who/when/conditions for applying separately from the enumerated Minister's powers.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Construction of ditches and drains
rows.groupTitle: Minister's powers in ditch and drain construction
rows.groupReason: The seven enumerated powers in 12(3) answer a distinct recall question about the scope of the Minister's authority in the drainage process, including the power to construct unilaterally and to assess benefited landowners.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the seven powers the Minister may exercise for purposes of a ditch or drain application under section 12(1) or (2), including the power to construct without an agreement and to assess benefited landowners for cost.

evidenceText: investigate the need for the ditch or drain;
construct the ditch or drain whether or not the Minister obtains an agreement;
assess each owner of the benefited land for the cost of construction.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 12 contains two independently recallable concepts: the application right with its deposit prerequisite (12(1)–(2)) and a substantial seven-item list of Minister's powers (12(3)). A learner would reasonably be tested on the who/when/conditions for applying separately from the enumerated Minister's powers.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Respecting minors, mentally incompetent persons and non-residents
rows.groupTitle: Judicial protection order for minors, mentally incompetent persons, and non-residents in ditch and drain proceedings
rows.groupReason: One unified concept: the trigger conditions, the applying party, the competent court, the power conferred, and the fairness standard all interdepend to define a single judicial protection mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the three classes of affected landowners, the applicant, the competent court, the types of orders available, and the standard the judge applies.

evidenceText: If the person entitled to land through which any ditch or drain is proposed to be constructed is a minor, a mentally incompetent person or a non-resident of the Province, a judge of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick may, on the application of the person desiring the construction of the ditch or drain, make an order for the service of the person or the protection of the person's interests as the judge may deem fair and reasonable.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13 is a short, self-contained judicial protection mechanism for vulnerable or absent landowners in ditch and drain proceedings, forming one coherent recall unit.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Prohibition respecting placing of impediments in drain
rows.groupTitle: Prohibition on Impeding Shared Ditches and Drains
rows.groupReason: Applicability condition, prohibition, and consent carve-out are interdependent and form one recallable rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the condition under which the impediment prohibition applies, what it prohibits, and the consent required before placing anything in a shared ditch or drain.

evidenceText: the owners of land traversed by the ditch or drain shall not place any impediment in that ditch or drain that will interfere with the passage of water without first obtaining the consent of all owners served by that ditch or drain

rows.sourceMapReason: One self-contained conditional prohibition: owners of land traversed by a jointly funded shared drain may not impede water passage without prior consent of all served owners.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Maintenance and repair of ditches and drains
rows.groupTitle: Joint responsibility for shared ditch and drain maintenance
rows.groupReason: A single substantive duty with specific triggering conditions (shared use, provincial or joint funding, applicable statutes or mutual consent).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which adjacent owners are jointly responsible for maintaining and repairing a shared ditch or drain on agricultural land.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 15 contains three distinct recall tasks: a joint maintenance duty (s.15(1)), a Ministerial application-and-deposit procedure (s.15(2)–(3)), and the Minister's enumerated powers (s.15(4)).

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Maintenance and repair of ditches and drains
rows.groupTitle: Ministerial application and deposit for repair permission
rows.groupReason: Tightly interdependent procedural sequence: the trigger for applying to the Minister and the financial precondition the Minister must find sufficient before granting permission.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an agricultural land owners association or owner may apply to the Minister for repair permission and what deposit must be made before the Minister may grant that permission.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 15 contains three distinct recall tasks: a joint maintenance duty (s.15(1)), a Ministerial application-and-deposit procedure (s.15(2)–(3)), and the Minister's enumerated powers (s.15(4)).

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Maintenance and repair of ditches and drains
rows.groupTitle: Minister's enumerated powers in the repair process
rows.groupReason: Six distinct enumerated powers (investigate, estimate, determine damage, seek agreement, carry out repair, assess owners) form a separate recall task from the application procedure.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: List the six powers the Minister may exercise for the purposes of subsections (2) or (3) of section 15, including the power to carry out repair and to assess owners of benefited land.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 15 contains three distinct recall tasks: a joint maintenance duty (s.15(1)), a Ministerial application-and-deposit procedure (s.15(2)–(3)), and the Minister's enumerated powers (s.15(4)).

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Application for review of amount of damages
rows.groupTitle: Referral of damages amount to the Court of King's Bench
rows.groupReason: The provision creates one procedural review path: who may refer, the triggering determination (Minister under s. 12 or 15), and the designated forum with its Expropriation Act framework.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may refer a Minister's damages determination under section 12 or 15, the trigger for referral, and the designated court and legislative framework for the review.

evidenceText: the person may refer the matter to The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick or any judge thereof acting under Part II of the Expropriation Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16 states a single, self-contained review right: a person dissatisfied with a Minister's damages amount under section 12 or 15 may refer the matter to The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick or a judge thereof under Part II of the Expropriation Act. One actor, one trigger, one forum — one recall task.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Costs respecting construction or repair by Province
rows.groupTitle: Crown recovery of ditch and drain construction or repair costs
rows.groupReason: Both subsections state the debt, the recovery action, and the court-costs rule for that action as a single cost-recovery mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State how costs incurred by the Minister under s.12 or 15 become a debt on the assessed owner, the means of recovery, and the court's power to order litigation costs in that action.

evidenceText: The cost of the construction or repair of any ditch or drain incurred by the Minister under section 12 or 15 shall constitute a debt due to the Crown in right of the Province from the person or persons assessed for the cost by the Minister under section 12 or 15 and may be recovered by action in the name of the Crown in any court of competent jurisdiction.
The court may make an order as to the costs of such action in favour of or against the Crown.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 17 creates a debt obligation on the assessed owner for Minister-incurred ditch/drain costs and provides the Crown's court recovery mechanism, including a narrow court-costs order in that action; both subsections form one coherent cost-recovery concept.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Offences
rows.groupTitle: Offence for regulatory non-compliance and category designation
rows.groupReason: Both subsections state one rule: regulatory violations are offences processed under Part II of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act, defaulting to category B unless regulations prescribe otherwise.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that a person who violates or fails to comply with a regulation under the Act commits an offence, identify the default category B designation and the procedural vehicle (Part II of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act), and explain how subsection (2) allows regulations under paragraph 20(l) to prescribe a different category.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18 is a short, self-contained offence provision: subsections (1) and (2) are tightly interdependent (default category B, subject to regulatory override), forming one coherent recall unit on liability for regulatory non-compliance.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Administration
rows.groupTitle: Ministerial Administration and Delegation
rows.groupReason: Both subsections state the Minister's administrative responsibility and delegation authority as a single institutional rule set.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Minister as the administering authority for the Act and regulations and recognise the power to designate persons to act on the Minister's behalf.
rows.sourceMapReason: Two short subsections assign the Minister responsibility for administering the Act and regulations and grant a delegation power; they form one tightly linked institutional recall unit with no further substantive content to split.

rows.documentTitle:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act
rows.heading: Regulations
rows.groupTitle: Scope of Regulatory Authority (s. 20)
rows.groupReason: All fourteen paragraphs express one delegation of power; a learner recalls the full scope of regulatory authority as a single concept.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the enumerated matters on which the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations under the Agricultural Land Protection and Development Act, including land suitability criteria, association incorporation, land registry, agricultural practices, offence categories, and appeals.

evidenceText: respecting the criteria for determining whether land that is not in use in an agricultural operation is suitable for use in an agricultural operation
prescribing an agricultural activity or process for the purposes of the definition
prescribing, in relation to offences under the regulations, categories of offences for the purposes of Part II of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 20 is a single delegation of regulatory authority to the Lieutenant-Governor in Council covering fourteen enumerated topics; the recall task is identifying the full scope of matters subject to regulation under the Act.

rows.heading: Definitions
rows.groupTitle: Air Space Act defined terms
rows.groupReason: All operative definitions in section 1 form the shared vocabulary for the Act and are best recalled as a single definitional set.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Define the key terms of the Air Space Act, including the meaning of an air space parcel, the requirements of an air space plan, and the technical definition of orthometric height (CGVD2013, benchmark approved by the Director of Surveys).
rows.sourceMapReason: Short definitions section establishing the Act's vocabulary; terms are interdependent and collectively needed to understand the air space mechanism. The technical 'orthometric height' definition is only two sub-clauses and fits naturally within the overall definitional framework.

rows.heading: Air space as land
rows.groupTitle: Air space as land
rows.groupReason: One sentence establishing the legal character of air space as land and its susceptibility to the same dealings as land.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that under the Air Space Act, air space constitutes land and may be dealt with as land.
rows.sourceMapReason: Single foundational rule establishing that air space constitutes land and may be dealt with as land; one unified legal characterization with no internal division.

rows.heading: Creation of air space parcel
rows.groupTitle: Creation of air space parcels by filing
rows.groupReason: Single permission rule identifying the eligible estate owner, the filing mechanism, and the resulting volumetric parcels separated by surfaces.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the eligible owner (freehold or leasehold estate holder), the required mechanism (filing an air space plan in the registry office), and the form of the resulting parcels.
rows.sourceMapReason: Short self-contained provision stating who may create air space parcels, the filing mechanism, and the form of the result; one recallable concept, no split needed.

rows.heading: Requirements of air space plan
rows.groupTitle: Mandatory requirements of an air space plan
rows.groupReason: All subsections (a)–(e) specify interdependent content and geometric constraints for the same plan document; they form one recallable requirement set for surveyors preparing air space plans.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the five mandatory requirements an air space plan must satisfy, including identification of the parent parcel, boundary geometry, orthometric heights, and the required plot and paraline drawing with dimensioning rules.

evidenceText: identify the parcel of land of which the air space parcel is part and shall indicate that the plan is a subdivision of the whole or part of that parcel of land

have noted on it the orthometric height of one corner of the ground surface of the parcel of land referred to in paragraph (a) and the orthometric height of every corner or angle of the air space parcel

a three-dimensional paraline drawing of the air space parcel contained between the planes or arcs, and, if the surfaces of the air space parcel are both horizontal and vertical the plan shall so state, otherwise all boundaries of the air space parcel shall be fully dimensioned for length and direction

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 4 is a single coherent specification of mandatory content requirements for an air space plan; all five paragraphs answer the same recall question and should be studied together as one document-requirement set.

rows.heading: Filing of air space plan
rows.groupTitle: Filing prerequisites for an air space plan
rows.groupReason: Both subsections state conditions the registrar must verify before accepting an air space plan for filing, forming one procedural gate.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the three standard filing requirements in 5(1) and the additional development-officer certification required under 5(2) when the land is affected by a subdivision by-law or regulation under the Community Planning Act.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 5 sets out one coherent filing gate: three base conditions in 5(1) plus a conditional additional certification in 5(2), all answering the same recall question of what the registrar requires before accepting an air space plan.

rows.heading: Conveyance of air space parcel
rows.groupTitle: Conveyance of air space parcel
rows.groupReason: The three subsections together state the full conveyance regime: like-land treatment, what the conveyance excludes, and residual ownership of surrounding air space.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State how an air space parcel may be conveyed, what a conveyance does not include, and which air space remains with the transferor unless expressly conveyed.

evidenceText: An air space parcel shall devolve and may be conveyed or otherwise dealt with in the same manner and form as other land.
A conveyance of an air space parcel does not convey an easement of any kind, or imply a covenant restrictive of use or a covenant to convey another portion of the transferor's land.
Unless expressly conveyed, the title to the air space above the upper limits and below the lower limits of an air space parcel remains in the transferor.

rows.sourceMapReason: All three subsections form one coherent conveyance rule: general devolution rule (6(1)), exclusions from the conveyance (6(2)), and residual transferor ownership (6(3)). Recalling them separately would fragment a single short conveyance mechanism.

rows.heading: Assessment and taxation
rows.groupTitle: Air space parcel as real property for assessment and taxation
rows.groupReason: One sentence, one rule: the separately-owned condition and the real-property classification for assessment and taxation form a single recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the condition under which an air space parcel constitutes real property and for what purposes that classification applies.

evidenceText: An air space parcel, if separately owned, constitutes real property for the purposes of assessment and taxation.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 7 states a single, clear legal classification: a separately owned air space parcel is real property for assessment and taxation. This is one independently recallable rule with practical consequence, suitable as one StudyUnit.

rows.heading: Regulations
rows.groupTitle: Director of Surveys regulatory power
rows.groupReason: One clause, one actor, one permissive regulatory power with two defined subject matters — naturally one recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify that the Director of Surveys holds a permissive regulatory power under s. 8 and the two subject matters it may cover: standards of survey and content of an air space plan.
rows.sourceMapReason: A single short clause delegating a specific regulatory power to the Director of Surveys over survey standards and air space plan content; one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Definitions
rows.groupTitle: Core Aquaculture Activity and Biological Definitions
rows.groupReason: These terms define the regulated activity and the organisms/conditions it governs; each carries substantive scope content (e.g., farming's enumerated interventions, hazard's eight categories, land's overlying water column inclusion for 'water').
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the substantive content of key biological and activity definitions, including what 'farming' encompasses, the categories comprising a 'hazard,' what qualifies as 'aquatic organisms,' and the defining features of an 'invasive species' and a 'strain.',
rows.sourceMapReason: The definitions section contains 35 terms spanning substantially different recall domains: substantive biological/activity definitions, land-authorization instrument definitions, and institutional/cross-reference definitions. Each domain creates distinct recall tasks a learner would encounter separately on an exam.

rows.heading: Definitions
rows.groupTitle: Institutional Actors, Health Reporting, and Cross-Reference Definitions
rows.groupReason: These terms identify the institutional actors, the health-reporting trigger (reportable condition), and terms defined by cross-reference to other statutes; they provide the supporting vocabulary for the operational provisions.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which bodies and officers are defined (including that 'Minister' includes designated delegates and 'person' includes Cooperatives Act cooperatives), the dual basis for a 'reportable condition,' and the terms defined solely by reference to the Right to Information and Protection of Privacy Act or the Provincial Offences Procedure Act.
rows.sourceMapReason: The definitions section contains 35 terms spanning substantially different recall domains: substantive biological/activity definitions, land-authorization instrument definitions, and institutional/cross-reference definitions. Each domain creates distinct recall tasks a learner would encounter separately on an exam.

rows.heading: Definitions
rows.groupTitle: Land, Area, Site, and Authorization Instrument Definitions
rows.groupReason: These terms define the regulatory geography and the three authorization instruments (lease, permit, licence) with their issuing sections, creating a coherent recall unit on how aquaculture land is designated, allocated, and occupied.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how 'land' is defined (including overlying water column), what constitutes a 'site' versus 'aquaculture land,' the requirements embedded in a 'fallow period,' and which section authorizes each of the three instruments (lease s.16, permit s.26, licence s.36).
rows.sourceMapReason: The definitions section contains 35 terms spanning substantially different recall domains: substantive biological/activity definitions, land-authorization instrument definitions, and institutional/cross-reference definitions. Each domain creates distinct recall tasks a learner would encounter separately on an exam.

rows.heading: Application
rows.groupTitle: Application and Regulatory Exemptions of the Aquaculture Act
rows.groupReason: The general rule, the exemption categories, and the condition on exempted persons are tightly interdependent and answer one scope question.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the general scope of the Aquaculture Act, the five categories of persons, lands, sites, aquatic organisms, or activities subject to regulatory exemption, and the compliance obligation imposed on an exempted person.
rows.sourceMapReason: General scope rule, five-category regulatory exemption mechanism, and compliance duty on exempted persons form one interdependent applicability framework.

rows.heading: Agreements
rows.groupTitle: Minister's Agreement-Making Power for Aquaculture
rows.groupReason: The general enabling power, its specific joint-program and committee applications, and the confirm/ratify/alter/amend authority are facets of one ministerial agreement power.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which the Minister may enter agreements for aquaculture administration, identify the permitted counterparties, and describe the joint-program and intergovernmental-committee applications in subsection (2).
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 4 grants the Minister a single coherent agreement-making power for aquaculture administration; 4(2) elaborates 4(1) without limiting it, so the general power, joint-program application, and committee-establishment power form one recallable concept.

rows.heading: Advisory Committees
rows.groupTitle: Advisory Committee Establishment, Mandate, and Service Terms
rows.groupReason: All seven subsections form one advisory-committee governance unit covering who establishes it, how it is composed, when it meets, what it advises on, and how members are compensated.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister's power to establish and appoint to advisory committees, the committee's duty to consult and advise on administrative, regulatory, and legislative aquaculture matters when requested, and the member service terms of no salary, possible Minister-set allowance, and Treasury Board expense entitlements.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 5 is a short, coherent institutional provision establishing the advisory committee framework—Minister's power to establish, composition, meeting trigger, advisory mandate scope, and member service terms. All subsections describe one governance mechanism best recalled as a single unit.

rows.heading: Policies, standards, procedures and guidelines
rows.groupTitle: Ministerial policies, standards, procedures and guidelines
rows.groupReason: The three subsections together define one instrument category: the Minister's power to issue it, its registry publication duty, and its exclusion from the Regulations Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Minister's power to establish provincial policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines related to aquaculture, their requirement to be published in the registry, and the inapplicability of the Regulations Act to them.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 6 establishes a distinct ministerial-instrument category (policies, standards, procedures, guidelines) with its own publication duty and a carve-out from the Regulations Act; the three subsections form one coherent recall task on the legal character of these instruments.

rows.heading: Aquaculture management areas
rows.groupTitle: Designation of Aquaculture Management Areas
rows.groupReason: The designation power, the five enumerated order-content powers, and the mandatory registry notice-of-intent form one interdependent mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister's power to designate aquaculture management areas (whether in water or inland), the five categories of matter a designation order may address, and the requirement to publish a notice of intent in the registry before making the order.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 7 is a short, self-contained designation mechanism; the Minister's power, the order's permissible contents, and the pre-designation notice are tightly interdependent and form one coherent recall unit.

rows.heading: Aquaculture land
rows.groupTitle: Designation of Aquaculture Land

rows.heading: Real property assessment notice
rows.groupTitle: Occupier's right to a copy of the assessment notice
rows.groupReason: Subsection 21(2.1) creates the Director's duty to provide a copy to the user or occupier on written request, and 21(2.2) preserves the registered owner's tax liability under the Real Property Tax Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the occupier's right to request a copy of the assessment notice and confirm that providing the copy does not affect the assessed person's tax liability.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 21 contains four independently recallable concepts: the Director's core notice obligation and content, delivery/service mechanics, occupier access to a copy, and a standalone no-exemption-for-errors rule.

rows.heading: Definition of “error”
rows.groupTitle: Definition of "error" for section 22 correction
rows.groupReason: One tight definitional rule with a two-part inclusion/exclusion boundary (factual information error vs. valuation determination) scoped to section 22.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State what constitutes an "error" in the real property assessment list for purposes of section 22 and identify what is excluded from that definition.

evidenceText: "error" means an error in any part of the real property assessment list that is the result of incorrect factual information about the real property, and not in the determination of the real and true value of the real property.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single definitional provision drawing the legal boundary between factual-information errors and valuation errors for section 22 correction purposes.

rows.heading: Errors in real property assessment list
rows.groupTitle: Director's duty to correct errors in the real property assessment list
rows.groupReason: The provision sets out the Director's mandatory correction procedure and the two required notifications that follow any assessment correction.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Director's obligation to correct an error in the real property assessment list and the two notifications (amended notice to the person assessed and amendment to the local government or taxing authority under section 13) that follow.

evidenceText: the Director shall correct the error and alter the list accordingly, and on correcting or altering any assessment, the Director shall deliver or transmit to the person assessed an amended real property assessment notice, and shall furnish the appropriate local government or other taxing authority with an amendment to the portion of the real property assessment list under section 13

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 22 imposes a single, tightly linked procedural duty on the Director: upon discovering an error in the real property assessment list, correct it, notify the person assessed, and furnish the local government or taxing authority with the amendment. One actor, one trigger, one sequential obligation — a coherent standalone study unit.

rows.heading: Omissions from real property assessment list
rows.groupTitle: Rectifying omissions from the real property assessment list
rows.groupReason: Subsection (1) sets a single mandatory rectification duty with four linked steps (assess, enter, notify, furnish local government) triggered by omission of property from the list.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Director's mandatory steps when real property has been omitted from the real property assessment list, including the notice and local-government furnishing requirements under section 13.

evidenceText: the Director shall make any assessment necessary to rectify the omission and shall enter the real property on the real property assessment list

rows.sourceMapReason: The two subsections address distinct triggers and modalities: mandatory rectification of general omissions versus a specific permissive power over Real Property Tax Act property with an override of sections 21 and 22.

rows.heading: Omissions from real property assessment list
rows.groupTitle: Director's assessment power over Real Property Tax Act property
rows.groupReason: Subsection (2) grants a permissive reassessment power over paragraph (b.1) property tied to a Real Property Tax Act tax event, with an explicit override of sections 21 and 22 and mandatory entry and notice steps.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions under which the Director may assess or reassess real property under paragraph (b.1) of the definition of real property despite sections 21 and 22, and the mandatory entry and mailing steps that follow.

evidenceText: the Director may assess or reassess, despite sections 21 and 22, the real property any time for the 1977 taxation year and subsequent years

rows.sourceMapReason: The two subsections address distinct triggers and modalities: mandatory rectification of general omissions versus a specific permissive power over Real Property Tax Act property with an override of sections 21 and 22.

rows.heading: Time for assessment
rows.groupTitle: Annual assessment revision and applicability year
rows.groupReason: Establishes the Director's duty to revise all real property assessments each year and that the revised assessment is the assessment for the following year.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Director's annual assessment revision duty and identify which taxation year the revised assessment applies to under s. 23(1).
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 23 pairs a distinct annual revision timing rule (sub 1) with separate list-maintenance, content, and public-access provisions that form independent recall tasks for an assessment or surveying learner.

rows.heading: Time for assessment
rows.groupTitle: Real property assessment list: maintenance, content, and public access
rows.groupReason: Covers the Director's duty to maintain the list, its prescribed content, public inspection of the list and the section 13 portion, and the Director's discretionary information-release power.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Director's duty to maintain the real property assessment list, the requirement that its content be prescribed by regulation, the public inspection rules for the list and the section 13 portion, and the Director's power to release list information to any person or body.

evidenceText: The Director shall maintain a real property assessment list of all real property in the Province.
The real property assessment list shall be open to public inspection in the form and manner that the Director considers appropriate and may be available electronically.
The Director may release information contained in the real property assessment list to any person or body that the Director considers appropriate.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 23 pairs a distinct annual revision timing rule (sub 1) with separate list-maintenance, content, and public-access provisions that form independent recall tasks for an assessment or surveying learner.

rows.heading: Request for review of assessment to Director
rows.groupTitle: Effective date, list-change timeline, and scope limitation of the decision
rows.groupReason: The January 1 effective date, the 30-day list-change deadline, and the rule that one property's change does not affect other assessments are the operative effects and scope limits of the Director's decision.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that the decision takes effect from January 1 of the assessment year, that list changes must be made within 30 days of the decision, and that a change to one assessment does not affect any other assessment unless separately reviewed or appealed.

evidenceText: The decision of the Director under this section has effect from the first day of January in the year for which the assessment referred to in subsection (1) was made and any changes required to be made in the real property assessment list as a result of that decision shall be made within 30 days after the Director has made the decision

A change in an assessment arising out of a decision of any request for review of assessment or appeal under this Act shall not affect any other assessment unless that other assessment is itself changed as a result of a request for review of assessment or appeal under this Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 25 contains three independently recallable concepts: the requester's right and filing requirements, the Director's decision and notification duties, and the effective date and scope limitation of the decision. Each creates a distinct recall task for a learner studying assessment review procedure.

rows.heading: Request for review of assessment to Director
rows.groupTitle: Director's duty to reconsider, decide, and notify
rows.groupReason: The Director's register duty, reconsideration obligation (vacate/confirm/vary), required notice to the person with Review Register entries and appeal form, and notification to the local government or taxing authority form the Director-side procedural duties.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Director's obligation to reconsider and vacate, confirm, or vary the assessment, the contents of the mailed decision notice (Review Register entries plus appeal form), and the duty to notify the local government or other taxing authority.

evidenceText: The Director shall reconsider an assessment referred to in subsection (1) and shall vacate, confirm or vary the assessment, then send a notice to the person of his or her decision by mailing to the person a copy of all entries in the Review Register pertaining to the request for review of assessment together with a copy of the form for giving notice of appeal to the Board
the Director shall notify the local government or other taxing authority of the decision

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 25 contains three independently recallable concepts: the requester's right and filing requirements, the Director's decision and notification duties, and the effective date and scope limitation of the decision. Each creates a distinct recall task for a learner studying assessment review procedure.

rows.heading: Request for review of assessment to Director
rows.groupTitle: Right to request review and required contents of the request
rows.groupReason: Who may request, the 30-day deadline, and the mandatory contents of the request form one coherent filing-requirements recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may request a review, the 30-day deadline from mailing, and the four required contents of the request (name, address with postal code, telephone number, full and detailed reasons).

evidenceText: may request that the Director, by a request for review of assessment, review the real property assessment if the request is made within 30 days after the real property assessment notice or the amended real property assessment notice is mailed
shall set out in the request his or her full name, address including postal code and telephone number and provide full, complete and detailed reasons for objecting to the assessment

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 25 contains three independently recallable concepts: the requester's right and filing requirements, the Director's decision and notification duties, and the effective date and scope limitation of the decision. Each creates a distinct recall task for a learner studying assessment review procedure.

rows.heading: Review Registers
rows.groupTitle: Review Registers: Required Entries, Signature, and Public Inspection
rows.groupReason: All four subsections describe one administrative system — the Review Register — and a learner would recall the required entries, signature, and inspection access as a single procedural concept.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the entries the Director must record in a Review Register (request description, decision, and reasons), the signing requirement, and the public inspection provision.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 26 is a short, coherent procedural provision establishing the Review Register system: what must be recorded, the signing requirement, and public inspection. It forms one recallable concept within the assessment review process.

rows.heading: Appeal to Board
rows.groupTitle: Appeal to the Board – Right and Time Limits
rows.groupReason: The appeal right, forum, remedy, and both alternative deadlines are interdependent and answer one procedural question about exercising the appeal.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which a person may appeal to the Board after a Director review under section 25, identify the forum and available remedies, and apply the two alternative time limits for filing the appeal.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 27 grants the right to appeal an assessment to the Board after a Director review and sets two alternative filing deadlines; the right, forum, remedy, and temporal conditions form one recall unit.

rows.heading: Appeal to Board by local government or other taxing authority
rows.groupTitle: Local government or other taxing authority appeal to the Board (s. 28)
rows.groupReason: Defines the specific actor, the s. 25(5) notice trigger, the 21-day deadline, and the limited scope (variation of assessments within the authority's boundaries affected by the review) of this appeal right.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the trigger event, the 21-day deadline, and the scope of a local government's or other taxing authority's right to appeal an assessment to the Board under section 28.

evidenceText: Within 21 days after the Director mails a notice to a local government or other taxing authority under subsection 25(5), the local government or other taxing authority may appeal to the Board for the local government or other taxing authority to vary the assessment of real property located within its boundaries and affected by the request for review of assessment.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single short provision granting a local government or other taxing authority a time-limited right to appeal an assessment to the Board; trigger, deadline, and scope form one coherent procedural rule.

rows.heading: Notice of Appeal
rows.groupTitle: Instituting an appeal and required contents of the notice
rows.groupReason: The method of instituting the appeal and the mandatory contents of the notice are interdependent and answer a single recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State how an appeal to the Board is instituted and identify the three required contents of the notice of appeal.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 29 contains two distinct procedural stages with different actors: instituting the appeal and specifying notice contents, versus post-service distribution of copies and the resulting right to appear.

rows.heading: Notice of Appeal
rows.groupTitle: Service of copies of the notice of appeal and right to appear
rows.groupReason: Distinct actors with mandatory copy-service duties under different triggers, plus a separate permissive right to appear, form a second recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who must serve copies of the notice of appeal, on whom, under what conditions, and the right of a served person to appear at the hearing.

evidenceText: the Chairperson shall serve in accordance with the regulations a copy of the notice of appeal on
the local government or other taxing authority shall serve in accordance with the regulations a copy of the notice of appeal on the person in whose name the real property is assessed
A person served with a copy of a notice of appeal may appear at the hearing of the appeal.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 29 contains two distinct procedural stages with different actors: instituting the appeal and specifying notice contents, versus post-service distribution of copies and the resulting right to appear.

rows.heading: Service of notice of appeal
rows.groupTitle: Facsimile service requirements and validity
rows.groupReason: Cover-page contents, the 14-day original-substitution rule, the date-of-service rule, and the deemed-not-served conditions form one interdependent facsimile procedure.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the required facsimile cover-page contents, the fourteen-day original-service deadline, the date-of-service rule, and the conditions under which facsimile service is deemed not to have been served.

evidenceText: the original of the notice of appeal shall be served on the Chairperson in accordance with paragraph (1)(a), (b) or (d) within fourteen days after service by telephone transmission
A notice of appeal served by telephone transmission shall be deemed not to have been served
the date of service of the notice of appeal shall be the date shown by the date received stamp placed on the facsimile of the notice of appeal at the office of the Chairperson

rows.sourceMapReason: The four general service methods in (1) are independently recallable from the facsimile-specific technical requirements in (2)–(4), which form a self-contained sub-procedure.

rows.heading: Service of notice of appeal
rows.groupTitle: Permitted methods of service of notice of appeal
rows.groupReason: The four enumerated service methods are a self-contained procedural rule a learner recalls as one list.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the four statutory methods for serving a notice of appeal on the Chairperson under s. 29.1(1).

evidenceText: A notice of appeal shall be served on the Chairperson
by telephone transmission producing a facsimile of the notice of appeal at the office of the Chairperson as stated in the notice of appeal

rows.sourceMapReason: The four general service methods in (1) are independently recallable from the facsimile-specific technical requirements in (2)–(4), which form a self-contained sub-procedure.

rows.heading: Jurisdiction of Board
rows.groupTitle: Board's jurisdiction over questions of fact and assessment disputes
rows.groupReason: The two sentences state one interdependent jurisdictional scope: the Board's power over all questions of fact and its residual authority over disputes not otherwise addressed in the Act or regulations.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the scope of the Board's authority to hear and determine questions of fact and to deal with disputes under the Act not already provided for in the Act or the regulations.

evidenceText: The Board has the authority to hear and determine all questions of fact and may deal with any dispute as to any matter included within the provisions of this Act not already provided for in the Act or in the regulations.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 29.2 is a single, self-contained jurisdictional grant establishing the Board's authority over questions of fact and assessment disputes not otherwise provided for. It forms one coherent recall unit.

rows.heading: Conduct of hearing before Board
rows.groupTitle: Consequences of appellant non-appearance and failure to provide required information
rows.groupReason: Subsections 32(7) and (8) set out two distinct adverse consequences for the appellant: mandatory dismissal for non-appearance and discretionary refusal to hear for failure to provide section 8 and 9 information.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Distinguish the mandatory dismissal consequence for appellant non-appearance from the discretionary refusal to hear when the appellant fails to provide information required under sections 8 and 9.

evidenceText: Where the party appealing does not appear at the time and place set for the hearing of an appeal, the Board shall dismiss the appeal.
Where the party appealing, having been required to provide information under sections 8 and 9, fails to provide such information, the Board may refuse to hear the appeal.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 32 contains three distinct recall concepts: hearing procedure and evidence rules, the Director's specific filing duty with evidentiary effect, and consequences of appellant non-compliance. 32(5) is repealed and excluded.

rows.heading: Conduct of hearing before Board
rows.groupTitle: Director's filing obligation and evidentiary effect at hearing
rows.groupReason: Subsection 32(4) imposes a specific duty on the Director to file the assessment notice, review request, and Review Register, and confers an evidentiary effect on those filings.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State what the Director must file with the Board at the hearing of an appeal and the evidentiary effect those filings carry.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 32 contains three distinct recall concepts: hearing procedure and evidence rules, the Director's specific filing duty with evidentiary effect, and consequences of appellant non-compliance. 32(5) is repealed and excluded.

rows.heading: Conduct of hearing before Board
rows.groupTitle: Hearing procedure and evidence rules before the Board
rows.groupReason: Subsections 32(1)–(3) and (6) together establish the procedural framework: procedure set by regulation, permitted evidence forms, oath dispensation, and the Board's power to require appellant document filings.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the regulation-based procedural basis for Board appeals, the permitted forms of evidence, the oath dispensation rule, and the Board's power to require the appellant to file documents it intends to rely on.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 32 contains three distinct recall concepts: hearing procedure and evidence rules, the Director's specific filing duty with evidentiary effect, and consequences of appellant non-compliance. 32(5) is repealed and excluded.

rows.heading: Appeal record
rows.groupTitle: Board's appeal record duty and required contents
rows.groupReason: The 'shall keep a record' duty and its three enumerated content requirements are inseparable for recall: the duty is meaningless without its contents and vice versa.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Board's duty to keep a record of each appeal and identify the three categories that must constitute that record under s. 33(2).
rows.sourceMapReason: 33(1) imposes the Board's duty to keep an appeal record and 33(2) specifies its mandatory contents; the two subsections form one coherent procedural recall concept.

rows.heading: Powers of Board
rows.groupTitle: Board's disposal powers on assessment appeal
rows.groupReason: All four disposal options (refuse, dismiss, allow with direction, refer back) are one actor exercising one procedural power at a single stage.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the four ways the Board may dispose of an assessment appeal and the condition in subsection (a) tying refusal to hear to the appellant's failure to provide information required under sections 8 and 9.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 34(1) is a single enumeration of the Board's four disposal options for an assessment appeal, forming one coherent recall task for the same actor at one procedural stage.

rows.heading: Effect of decision of Board
rows.groupTitle: Effect and Implementation of Board Decision
rows.groupReason: Covers the retroactive effective date of a Board decision and the prompt-update duty for the assessment list as one practical rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State when a Board decision takes effect and what must be done to the real property assessment list as a result.

evidenceText: The decision of the Board has effect from the first day of January in the year for which the assessment appealed from was made
any changes required to be made in the real property assessment list as a result thereof shall be made as soon as possible after the Board has made its decision

rows.sourceMapReason: Single short section stating when a Board decision takes effect (retroactive to January 1 of the assessment year) and the duty to update the real property assessment list; the two clauses form one coherent recall unit.

rows.heading: Appeal to Court of King’s Bench
rows.groupTitle: Right to appeal Board decisions, filing procedure, and stay effect
rows.groupReason: The scope of appeal (questions of law), the Notice of Application filing method with the 60-day deadline, and the stay effect are the initiating steps a learner must recall as one coherent filing task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the scope of appeal from a Board decision, the Notice of Application filing requirements and 60-day deadline, and confirm that filing the appeal stays the Board's order, ruling, or decision.

evidenceText: An appeal lies to a judge of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick from an order, ruling or decision of the Board on any question of law.

An appeal under subsection (1) shall be made by Notice of Application which shall be served by the party appealing, in accordance with the Rules of Court, on the Board and on the other parties within 60 days of the mailing of the Board's decision under subsection 72(2) of the Local Governance Commission Act.
An appeal under subsection (1) stays the application of the order, ruling or decision in respect of which the appeal is made.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 37 establishes a complete appellate procedure with distinct actors (appealing party, Board, King's Bench judge, Court of Appeal) and separate recall tasks: the right and filing method, the record mechanism, and the judge's disposition powers plus further appeal.

rows.heading: Appeal to Court of King’s Bench
rows.groupTitle: Judge's disposition powers, Rules of Court application, and further appeal
rows.groupReason: The judge's three disposition options, the general application of Rules of Court, and the right of further appeal to the Court of Appeal form the concluding disposition and review pathway.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the judge's three disposition options on an assessment appeal, note the limited application of the Rules of Court, and identify the right to further appeal the judge's decision to the Court of Appeal.

evidenceText: After hearing the appeal, the judge may allow the appeal and set aside the order, ruling or decision or may dismiss the appeal or substitute his own ruling, order or decision for that of the Board.

There shall be an appeal from a decision of the judge to the Court of Appeal and the rules governing appeals to that Court from a decision of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick apply to appeals under this subsection.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 37 establishes a complete appellate procedure with distinct actors (appealing party, Board, King's Bench judge, Court of Appeal) and separate recall tasks: the right and filing method, the record mechanism, and the judge's disposition powers plus further appeal.

rows.heading: Appeal to Court of King’s Bench
rows.groupTitle: Board's record delivery duty and scope of appellate hearing
rows.groupReason: The Board's duty to deliver the section 33 record and the court's obligation to hear only on that record form one tightly linked procedural concept about the scope of the appellate hearing.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Describe the Board's duty to deliver the section 33 record and a copy of its decision to the Court of King's Bench clerk, and confirm that the appeal is heard and determined solely on the evidence and proceedings in that record.

evidenceText: Upon service under subsection (2), the Board shall deliver to the clerk of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick for the judicial district in which the appeal is to be heard the record referred to in section 33 and a copy of the order, ruling or decision of the Board.
The appeal shall be heard and determined upon the evidence and proceedings before the Board as contained in the record referred to in section 33.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 37 establishes a complete appellate procedure with distinct actors (appealing party, Board, King's Bench judge, Court of Appeal) and separate recall tasks: the right and filing method, the record mechanism, and the judge's disposition powers plus further appeal.

rows.heading: Regulations
rows.groupTitle: Scope of delegated regulatory power under s. 40
rows.groupReason: One delegated-power concept: the enumerated areas in which the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations, from Director-designated officers through farmland, heritage, mobile homes, exemptions, and the general carry-out power in paragraph (f).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the principal areas in which the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations under the Assessment Act, including specific parameters for definitions, exemption criteria, assessment procedures, and the general carry-out power in paragraph (f). P3 priority reflects that this is structural context for how substantive rules are made rather than a directly applied rule.

evidenceText: The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations

prescribing for the purpose of the Director's determination whether real property is in actual and bona fide use as farmland, the minimum gross revenue per hectare that must be derived from farming if the real property is to be assessed as farmland
generally to carry out the purposes and provisions of this Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 40 contains two distinct recall tasks: the scope of delegated regulatory power (40(1) and its paragraphs) and the separate rule permitting retroactive operation of specific regulations (40(1.1)–(1.28)). Each answers a different exam question.

rows.heading: Regulations
rows.groupTitle: Retroactive operation of specific regulations (s. 40(1.1)–(1.28))
rows.groupReason: Separate legal rule: each subsection identifies a specific regulatory paragraph that may operate retroactively and the earliest date to which retroactivity extends, forming a distinct recall task from the scope of delegated power.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State which regulatory paragraphs under s. 40(1) may operate retroactively and the applicable earliest retroactive date for each, from January 1, 2000 (assessment rate schedules) through January 1, 2018 (Minister of Agriculture criteria). P4 priority reflects that these are specific administrative date boundaries rather than core practice rules.

evidenceText: A regulation under paragraph (1)(e.41), (e.5), (e.6), (e.7) or (e.8) may be retroactive in its operation.
A regulation under paragraph (1)(e.3) may be retroactive in its operation to January 1, 2000, or to any date after January 1, 2000.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 40 contains two distinct recall tasks: the scope of delegated regulatory power (40(1) and its paragraphs) and the separate rule permitting retroactive operation of specific regulations (40(1.1)–(1.28)). Each answers a different exam question.

rows.heading: Confession of judgment as preference
rows.groupTitle: Confession of Judgment as Void Preference
rows.groupReason: Triggering conditions (insolvency, voluntary/collusive act, intent to prefer or defeat), the three covered instrument types, and the dual consequence (void as against creditors; invalid to support judgment or writ) are interdependent parts of one rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the circumstances, covered instruments, and legal effect when a person in insolvency gives a confession of judgment, cognovit actionem, or warrant of attorney to prefer or delay creditors.

evidenceText: If a person, being at the time in insolvent circumstances or unable to pay his debts in full, or knowing himself to be on the eve of insolvency, voluntarily or by collusion with a creditor or creditors, gives a confession of judgment, cognovit actionem, or warrant of attorney to confess judgment, to defeat or delay his creditors wholly or in part, or with intent thereby to give one or more of his creditors a preference over his other creditors

every such confession, cognovit actionem, or warrant of attorney to confess judgment, is void as against the creditors of the party giving the same, and is invalid and ineffectual to support any judgment or writ of execution

rows.sourceMapReason: One self-contained voidness rule: the triggering circumstances, covered instruments, and legal consequence of a preferential confession of judgment form a single recallable unit.

rows.heading: Transfers of property as preference
rows.groupTitle: Preference voidness: fraudulent transfer and unjust preference
rows.groupReason: Two parallel voidness rules sharing the same insolvency trigger and property scope but requiring different intents (defeat/delay/prejudice vs. unjust preference), best studied and recalled together as the core s.2 prohibition pair.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the insolvency trigger and the two distinct intent requirements (defeat/delay/prejudice creditors vs. give an unjust preference to one creditor) that render a transfer void under s.2(1) and s.2(2), and note the added 'postponed' creditor category in s.2(2).

evidenceText: with intent to defeat, delay or prejudice his creditors, or any one or more of them, is void, as against a creditor injured, delayed or prejudiced
to or for a creditor with intent to give such creditor an unjust preference over the other creditors, or over any of them, is void, as against a creditor injured, delayed, prejudiced or postponed

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 2 contains three independently recallable concepts: the dual voidness rules for fraudulent transfers and unjust preferences, the evidentiary presumption with its 60-day limitation, and the separate surety/indorser extension. Subsection 2(4) is a pure repeal with no operative content.

rows.heading: Transfers of property as preference
rows.groupTitle: Presumption of preference and 60-day limitation
rows.groupReason: The evidentiary presumption and the 60-day limitation for impeachment are a separate recall task from the substantive voidness rules, applying regardless of voluntary or pressured transactions.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the 60-day time limit for bringing a suit to impeach a preference and identify what is presumed (the intent and unjust-preference character) once a transaction gives a creditor a preference over others.

evidenceText: it shall, with respect to any suit or proceeding that, within sixty days thereafter, is brought to impeach or set aside such transaction, be presumed to have been made with the intent aforesaid, and to be an unjust preference within the meaning hereof, whether the same is made voluntarily or under pressure

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 2 contains three independently recallable concepts: the dual voidness rules for fraudulent transfers and unjust preferences, the evidentiary presumption with its 60-day limitation, and the separate surety/indorser extension. Subsection 2(4) is a pure repeal with no operative content.

rows.heading: Transfers of property as preference
rows.groupTitle: Conveyance to surety or indorser as preference
rows.groupReason: Extends the preference voidness rules to a distinct actor (surety or indorser who would become a creditor on payment), creating a separately recallable trigger and condition.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when a transfer to a surety or indorser of a promissory note or bill of exchange is void as a preference, and the condition that the surety or indorser would become a creditor upon payment.

evidenceText: is made to or for any surety or indorser of any promissory note or bill of exchange, who would upon payment by him of the debt, promissory note, or bill of exchange, in respect of which such suretyship was entered into, or such indorsement given, become a creditor of the person giving the preference

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 2 contains three independently recallable concepts: the dual voidness rules for fraudulent transfers and unjust preferences, the evidentiary presumption with its 60-day limitation, and the separate surety/indorser extension. Subsection 2(4) is a pure repeal with no operative content.

rows.heading: Valid assignments
rows.groupTitle: Matters to which the Act is inapplicable
rows.groupReason: Sets out four distinct inapplicability rules: Wage-earners Protection Act wage payments, creditor who lost valuable security, good-faith substitution of security, and security for a pre-existing debt securing a bona fide advance.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify each matter to which the Act does not apply under 3(6), including wage payments under the Wage-earners Protection Act, security given up in good faith, substitution of security, and security for pre-existing debt with a bona fide advance.

evidenceText: Nothing herein contained affects the Wage-earners Protection Act, or prevents a debtor providing for payment of wages due by him

nor does anything herein contained invalidate a security given to a creditor for a pre-existing debt, where on account of the giving of the security, an advance of money is made to the debtor by the creditor in the bona fide belief that the advance will enable the debtor to continue his trade or business and pay his debts in full

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 3 contains four operative subsections (3(1), 3(2), 3(5), 3(6)) addressing distinct legal rules with different actors, triggers, and modalities, each forming an independently recallable concept; four subsections (3(3), 3(4), 3(7), 3(8)) are repealed and carry no operative content.

rows.heading: Valid assignments
rows.groupTitle: Purchaser's payment to vendor's creditor void as to creditor
rows.groupReason: Creates a specific voidness rule where a purchaser's payment to the vendor's creditor is void as to the creditor even though valid as to the purchaser, triggered by circumstances that would render a direct debtor payment void.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State when a purchaser's payment of the purchase price to the vendor's creditor is void as respects the creditor and the conditions that trigger the rule.

evidenceText: the payment or transfer, even though valid as respects the purchaser, is void as respects the creditor to whom the same is made

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 3 contains four operative subsections (3(1), 3(2), 3(5), 3(6)) addressing distinct legal rules with different actors, triggers, and modalities, each forming an independently recallable concept; four subsections (3(3), 3(4), 3(7), 3(8)) are repealed and carry no operative content.

rows.heading: Valid assignments
rows.groupTitle: Creditor's right to security restoration on void payment
rows.groupReason: Grants a creditor whose valuable security was given up in connection with a void payment the right to have the security restored or its value made good as a condition of returning the payment.

if the money paid, or the goods or other property sold or delivered, bear a fair and reasonable relative value to the consideration therefor

rows.heading: Effect of Bankruptcy Act

evidenceText: The provisions of this Act apply only in so far as they are not inconsistent with the Bankruptcy Act, chapter B-3 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1970.

rows.heading: Definitions

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 1 defines 23 terms spanning three distinct recall domains: the regulated resource and its products, the operational instruments and economic thresholds, and the spatial units and institutional holders. rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what 'bituminous shale production operations' encompasses, what makes a quantity a 'commercial quantity,' and which section grants each of the three instruments (licence to search, development permit, lease).
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 1 defines 23 terms spanning three distinct recall domains: the regulated resource and its products, the operational instruments and economic thresholds, and the spatial units and institutional holders. A learner would be tested on each cluster as a separate recall task.

rows.heading: Definitions
rows.groupTitle: Resource and product scope definitions
rows.groupReason: These terms define the substance regulated by the Act and the products it yields, establishing what falls within the Act's subject matter.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify what substances constitute 'bituminous shale,' distinguish 'oil' from 'natural gas' under the Act, and define 'synthetic crude oil' and 'bituminous shale products.'
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 1 defines 23 terms spanning three distinct recall domains: the regulated resource and its products, the operational instruments and economic thresholds, and the spatial units and institutional holders.
