rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Minister's authority to assess a franchise renewal fee and require the renewed gas distributor to pay it.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 11 contains three independently recallable concepts: the Board's substantive renewal power with its scope and exclusion, the procedural proceeding/continuation requirement, and the Minister's separate fee-assessment power.

rows.heading: Renewal of general franchise agreement by Minister
rows.groupTitle: Minister's power to renew or extend a general franchise agreement
rows.groupReason: The discretionary renewal power, the mandatory renewal obligation triggered by a holder's exercised contractual right, and the associated renewal-fee power form one interdependent recall unit on the Minister's general franchise renewal authority.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the Minister may renew a general franchise agreement, when the Minister is obliged to renew, the required Lieutenant-Governor in Council approval, and the Minister's power to assess a franchise renewal fee.

evidenceText: the Minister, with the approval of the Lieutenant-Governor in Council, may renew a general franchise agreement or extend its term at any time during the term of the agreement
the Minister shall renew the general franchise agreement or extend its term, as the case may be, for the term specified in the general franchise agreement
The Minister may assess a franchise renewal fee for a renewal under subsection (1) and require the gas distributor whose general franchise is renewed to pay it

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 11.1 contains a short, tightly interlocked rule: the Minister's discretionary renewal power (s.1), the mandatory renewal duty when the holder exercises a contractual right (s.1.1), and the associated fee-assessment power (s.3). Together they form one coherent recall task on the Minister's general franchise renewal authority.

rows.heading: Renewal of single end use franchise agreements
rows.groupTitle: Single end use franchise renewal: power, term, and fee
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1)–(3) form one interdependent renewal mechanism: the Lieutenant-Governor in Council's renewal power, the mandatory 20-year minimum term, and the attendant fee power are inseparable for recall.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may renew a single end use franchise agreement, when renewal may occur after December 31, 2014, the minimum renewal term of 20 years, and the renewal fee power.
rows.sourceMapReason: Self-contained renewal framework for single end use franchise agreements: renewal power, mandatory 20-year minimum term, and associated fee-assessment power form one coherent recall unit.

rows.heading: Application and fee for single end use franchise
rows.groupTitle: Board-era single end use franchise application, conditions, and fee
rows.groupReason: Three tightly linked subsections covering the temporal application process, the Board's two grant conditions, and the CPI-adjusted fee still owed by pre-2015 franchisees form one coherent recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Board's two grant conditions for a single end use franchise (area not actually serviced; economic infeasibility for the general franchise holder) and the $50,000 annual CPI-adjusted fee (1999 base) applicable to franchisees granted on or before December 31, 2014.

evidenceText: Between February 1, 2000, and December 31, 2014, both dates inclusive, subject to subsection (1.1), an application for a single end use franchise made to the Board under subsection 5(1) shall be decided by the Board
the franchise applied for is in an area not actually serviced by the general franchise holder

the holder of a single end use franchise shall pay a franchise fee of fifty thousand dollars to the Minister of Finance and Treasury Board on or before December 31st of the year in which the franchise is granted, and thereafter shall pay an annual franchise fee of fifty thousand dollars, adjusted annually by the latest change in the New Brunswick consumer price index, using 1999 as a base year

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13 sets out the 2000–2014 Board application and grant conditions for single end use franchises; subsection (2) remains operative for legacy franchisees via s. 13.1(3).

rows.heading: Granting, renewing or extending single end use franchise, fee
rows.groupTitle: Single end use franchise granting threshold and exception
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) form a rule-and-exception pair setting the five-million-gigajoule capacity threshold on the Lieutenant-Governor in Council's power and carving out pre-2015 franchises.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the installed consumption capacity threshold required for the Lieutenant-Governor in Council to grant, renew, or extend a single end use franchise and identify the exception for franchises granted or renewed on or before December 31, 2014.

evidenceText: may grant, renew or extend a single end use franchise only if the industrial facility for which the application is made has an installed consumption capacity of at least five million gigajoules per year

The installed consumption capacity requirement in subsection (1) does not apply to an industrial facility for which a single end use franchise was granted, renewed or extended on or before December 31, 2014

rows.sourceMapReason: The section divides into three independently recallable concepts: the Lieutenant-Governor in Council granting threshold with its pre-2015 exception, the two fee rate regimes by cohort, and the payment schedule plus annual adjustment for the post-2014 fee.

rows.heading: Granting, renewing or extending single end use franchise, fee
rows.groupTitle: Single end use franchise fee rates by cohort
rows.groupReason: Subsections (3) and (4) assign different franchise fees depending on whether the franchise was granted or renewed on or before or after December 31, 2014.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the franchise fee applicable to a single end use franchise holder whose franchise was granted or renewed on or before December 31, 2014 versus after that date.

evidenceText: The holder of a single end use franchise granted or renewed after December 31, 2014 shall pay a franchise fee calculated at a rate of ten cents per gigajoule of gas consumed per year by the industrial facility

rows.sourceMapReason: The section divides into three independently recallable concepts: the Lieutenant-Governor in Council granting threshold with its pre-2015 exception, the two fee rate regimes by cohort, and the payment schedule plus annual adjustment for the post-2014 fee.

rows.heading: Granting, renewing or extending single end use franchise, fee
rows.groupTitle: Payment schedule and annual adjustment of the post-2014 franchise fee
rows.groupReason: Subsections (6) and (7) specify the payee, quarterly remittance dates, the transmission-line-owner certification requirement, and the annual April 1 regulatory adjustment for the fee under subsection (4).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Describe to whom the ten-cents-per-gigajoule franchise fee is payable, the quarterly remittance dates, the required written certification, and the annual adjustment mechanism effective after March 31, 2021.

evidenceText: shall be remitted in quarterly payments on January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1 of each year
After March 31, 2021, a franchise fee imposed under subsection (4) shall be adjusted as of the first day of April each year in accordance with the formula prescribed by regulation

rows.sourceMapReason: The section divides into three independently recallable concepts: the Lieutenant-Governor in Council granting threshold with its pre-2015 exception, the two fee rate regimes by cohort, and the payment schedule plus annual adjustment for the post-2014 fee.

rows.heading: Natural Gas Distribution Fund
rows.groupTitle: Natural Gas Distribution Fund: establishment, custody, flow-through, and application rules
rows.groupReason: One coherent fund mechanism: purpose, custodian, funding sources, 30-day disbursement trigger, and the general franchise holder's duty to apply amounts to the following year's revenue requirement.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the purpose of the Natural Gas Distribution Fund, identify its custodian, describe which fees and interest flow in, and recall the 30-day disbursement rule and the general franchise holder's obligation to apply received amounts to its revenue requirement for the following year.

evidenceText: There is established a fund called the Natural Gas Distribution Fund.
Within 30 days after a fee is paid into the Fund under subsection (5), the fee and any interest accrued shall be paid to the general franchise holder.
The general franchise holder shall apply any amount received under subsection (7) to its revenue requirement for the year following the year the amount is received.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13.2 is a self-contained fund mechanism: establishment, custody, funding sources, 30-day disbursement, and application rules all interlock as one recallable mechanism for the Natural Gas Distribution Fund.

rows.heading: A gas distribution system is a public utility and a gas distributor is a common carrier of gas
rows.groupTitle: Legal status of gas distribution system and gas distributor under s. 14
rows.groupReason: Both subsections are single-sentence deeming provisions that together state the core legal classification of the gas distribution regime and the resulting regulatory hook and duty.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that a gas distribution system is deemed a public utility subject to Part 3 of the Energy and Utilities Board Act (where consistent with the Act) and that a gas distributor is deemed a common carrier of gas with an affirmative duty to act as one.

evidenceText: A gas distribution system owned or operated by a gas distributor is deemed to be a public utility and is subject to Part 3 of the Energy and Utilities Board Act so far as it is consistent with this Act.
A gas distributor is deemed to be a common carrier of gas and shall act as a common carrier of gas.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 14 establishes two foundational legal characterizations (gas distribution system as public utility subject to EUBA Part 3; gas distributor as common carrier with an affirmative duty) that together define the regulatory nature of the gas distribution regime in one compact, interdependent unit.

rows.heading: Gas distribution and provision of customer service
rows.groupTitle: Gas distributor's distribution duty and Board ordering power
rows.groupReason: Covers the distributor's mandatory connection duty upon written request and the Board's complementary power to order or cease gas distribution and customer service.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the gas distributor's obligation to distribute gas to a building upon written request from the owner, occupant, or other person in charge, and the Board's power to order a distributor to provide or cease gas distribution or customer service upon application.
rows.sourceMapReason: Both subsections address the gas distribution obligation: the distributor's mandatory duty to connect upon written request and the Board's power to order or cease service. Together they form one coherent service-obligation concept.

rows.heading: Prohibition against disposal of a gas distribution system, or sale or merger of a gas utility, without leave of the Board
rows.groupTitle: Board leave application and amalgamation voidness
rows.groupReason: The application procedure and the distinct voidness consequences for amalgamation agreements and certificates form a separate procedural-and-consequence recall task from the underlying prohibitions.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that leave applications are made to the Board which may grant or refuse, and that an amalgamation agreement is void if the Board refuses leave and a certificate of amalgamation is void if issued before leave is granted.

evidenceText: An application for leave under this section shall be made to the Board, which may grant or refuse leave

An amalgamation agreement between corporations proposing to amalgamate is void if the Board refuses to grant leave under this section, even if it has been adopted in accordance with section 122 of the Business Corporations Act
A certificate of amalgamation issued under section 124 of the Business Corporations Act is void if issued before the Board grants leave for the amalgamation

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 27 contains two independently recallable concepts: the substantive prohibitions and security carve-out (different actors, different triggers) and the Board application procedure with amalgamation voidness consequences (different modality and legal effect).

rows.heading: Prohibition against disposal of a gas distribution system, or sale or merger of a gas utility, without leave of the Board
rows.groupTitle: Prohibited transactions and security exception
rows.groupReason: Covers the full scope of prohibited transactions (disposal of system, public-serving parts, amalgamation, 20% acquisition) and the security-interest carve-out as one recallable prohibition set.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify each transaction prohibited without prior Board leave (disposal of the distribution system or public-serving parts, amalgamation by a sole corporation, acquisition of 20% or more beneficial ownership) and the mortgage/charge exception.

evidenceText: Without first obtaining an order from the Board granting leave, no gas distributor shall
no person shall acquire directly or indirectly 20 per cent or more of the beneficial ownership of a gas distributor
This section does not apply to a mortgage or charge to secure any loan or indebtedness or to secure any bond, debenture or other evidence of indebtedness

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 27 contains two independently recallable concepts: the substantive prohibitions and security carve-out (different actors, different triggers) and the Board application procedure with amalgamation voidness consequences (different modality and legal effect).

rows.heading: A gas distributor must be authorized to do business in New Brunswick
rows.groupTitle: Legal form and provincial authorization requirement for a gas distributor
rows.groupReason: One rule with two recall elements: permitted organizational forms and the provincial business-authorization requirement.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the three permitted legal forms (corporation, partnership, limited partnership) and the requirement that a gas distributor be authorized by the laws of the Province to carry on business in the Province.

evidenceText: A gas distributor shall be a corporation, partnership or limited partnership authorized by the laws of the Province to carry on business in the Province.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single operative rule specifying the permitted legal forms and provincial authorization requirement for a gas distributor; independently recallable and self-contained.

rows.heading: Prohibition against injecting gas into an underground storage facility without authorization
rows.groupTitle: Prohibition on injecting gas into an underground storage facility without a storage lease
rows.groupReason: The prohibition and its sole lease-holder exception are interdependent and answer one recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the prohibition on injecting gas for storage into an underground storage facility and identify the sole condition that authorizes the injection.

evidenceText: No person shall inject gas for storage into an underground storage facility unless he or she is a holder of an underground storage lease issued under the Underground Storage Act.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single prohibition with one tightly coupled exception condition; forms one recallable legal rule.

rows.heading: Authorization of use of underground storage facilities
rows.groupTitle: Board authorization for underground storage use
rows.groupReason: The Board's power to authorize, the scope of authorized activities, and the physical-integrity condition are one recall task centred on the Board's discretion.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the scope of activities the Board may authorize by order under s. 48(1) and the terms it may impose regarding physical integrity of the facility.

evidenceText: the Board may by order authorize a person to inject gas into an underground storage facility, store gas in it and remove gas from it, and to enter into and upon the land in the area and use the land for that purpose

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 48 contains two independently recallable concepts: the Board's authorization power and conditions (different actor, power modality) and the compensation duties with their exclusive dispute-resolution path (different actor, duty modality, procedural mechanism).

rows.heading: Authorization of use of underground storage facilities
rows.groupTitle: Compensation duties and dispute resolution for authorized storage
rows.groupReason: The compensation owed to right-holders and landowners, the 'just and equitable' standard, the exclusion of ordinary actions, and the Court of King's Bench determination path form one coherent compensation-and-remedy concept.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the two categories of just and equitable compensation owed by persons authorized under s. 48(1), the prohibition on separate actions for that compensation, and the exclusive Court of King's Bench determination under the Expropriation Act.

evidenceText: shall make to the owners of any gas or oil rights or of any right to store gas in the area just and equitable compensation

No action or other proceeding lies for compensation payable under this section and failing agreement, the amount shall be determined by the Court of King's Bench under Part 2 of the Expropriation Act.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 48 contains two independently recallable concepts: the Board's authorization power and conditions (different actor, power modality) and the compensation duties with their exclusive dispute-resolution path (different actor, duty modality, procedural mechanism).

rows.heading: Shared use of underground storage facilities
rows.groupTitle: Board power to direct shared use of underutilized underground storage
rows.groupReason: Distinct Board power with specific trigger, condition, and scope that a learner must recall independently of the agreement-approval rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the trigger, the condition on the facility, the scope of the Board's direction, and who sets the terms when the Board directs shared use of an underground storage facility to a gas distributor.

evidenceText: the Board may direct a person having an underground storage facility that is not in full use to provide all or part of the facility to the applicant, upon such terms and conditions as the Board may determine

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsection 49(1) creates a Board power to direct compulsory sharing of underutilized storage; 49(2) imposes a separate prohibition requiring Board approval for gas storage agreements. Different actors, modalities (power vs. prohibition), and recall tasks justify two units.

rows.heading: Shared use of underground storage facilities
rows.groupTitle: Board approval required for gas storage agreements
rows.groupReason: Separate prohibition with three enumerated approval elements that forms its own recall task distinct from the Board's directional power in 49(1).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the prohibition on entering or renewing a gas storage agreement without Board approval and list the three elements that must be approved: the parties, the period, and the storage subject.

evidenceText: No person shall enter into an agreement or renew an agreement with any other person for the storage of gas unless the Board has approved
the parties to the agreement or renewal
the period for which the agreement or renewal is to operate
the storage that is the subject of the agreement or renewal

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsection 49(1) creates a Board power to direct compulsory sharing of underutilized storage; 49(2) imposes a separate prohibition requiring Board approval for gas storage agreements. Different actors, modalities (power vs. prohibition), and recall tasks justify two units.

rows.heading: Licences relating to wells
rows.groupTitle: Licence procedure for wells in underground storage facilities
rows.groupReason: The four subsections form one procedural sequence: Minister's referral duty, Board's hearing triggers, the report's legal character as a deemed order with service on parties, and the Minister's obligation to decide in accordance with the report.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the referral, hearing, reporting, and decision steps for a well licence in an underground storage facility, including the two hearing triggers and the report's status as a deemed order of the Board.

evidenceText: The Minister shall refer to the Board every application for granting a licence under the Oil and Natural Gas Act relating to a well in an underground storage facility

If the applicant does not have authority to store gas in the underground storage facility or, in the Board's opinion, the special circumstances of the case require a hearing, then the Board may hold a hearing before reporting to the Minister
that report shall be deemed to be an order of the Board
The Minister shall grant or refuse to grant the licence under the Oil and Natural Gas Act in accordance with the report

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 50 is a short, self-contained procedural flow for well licences in underground storage facilities: referral, optional hearing, report-as-deemed-order, and Ministerial decision. The four subsections are tightly interdependent stages of one workflow and form a single coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Regulation of sale of gas by gas distributors
rows.groupTitle: General franchise holder's gas selling authority and conditions
rows.groupReason: The GFRH's selling permission and its two qualifying conditions form a tightly interdependent rule-and-conditions structure answering one recall question.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions under which the general franchise holder may sell or offer to sell gas to a customer, including the requirement to follow prescribed terms and conditions and the exemption from a Board certificate under section 61.

evidenceText: The general franchise holder may sell gas or offer to sell gas to a customer.
shall do so in accordance with the terms and conditions prescribed by regulation, and
may do so without a certificate issued by the Board under section 61.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 51 contains two distinct recall tasks: the GFRH's selling permission with its conditions, and the separate operational duties on gas distributors and their associates regarding supplier-of-last-resort status, gas acquisition, and affiliate selling restrictions.

rows.heading: Regulation of sale of gas by gas distributors
rows.groupTitle: Distributor supplier-of-last-resort duty and other sale-related obligations
rows.groupReason: These subsections impose distinct operational duties and a cross-reference restriction on gas distributors and their associates that are separate from the GFRH's direct selling authority.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the gas distributor's obligation to be or arrange a supplier of last resort, the regulatory conditions on acquiring gas for sale, and the restriction limiting associates and affiliates to selling gas only in accordance with section 58.

evidenceText: A gas distributor shall be a supplier of last resort or shall arrange for a supplier of last resort.
A gas distributor who acquires gas for sale shall do so in accordance with the terms and conditions prescribed by regulation.
An associate or affiliate of a gas distributor may only sell gas in accordance with section 58.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 51 contains two distinct recall tasks: the GFRH's selling permission with its conditions, and the separate operational duties on gas distributors and their associates regarding supplier-of-last-resort status, gas acquisition, and affiliate selling restrictions.

rows.heading: Regulation of rates and tariffs
rows.groupTitle: Rate-setting prohibition and Board authority
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1)–(4) and (6) establish the prohibition on unauthorized charges, the Board's power to approve or fix just and reasonable rates or substitute its own, its independence from distributor-customer contracts, and the permissible contents of a Board order.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prohibition on distributor charges without a Board order, the Board's power to approve or fix just and reasonable rates (or fix its own if satisfied the applied rates are not just and reasonable), its independence from distributor-customer contract terms, and the conditions, classifications, practices, and rate-calculation rules a Board order may include.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 52 pairs the core rate-setting prohibition and Board authority with a separate cluster of rules on how the Board must treat regulatory accounts and may choose its regulatory method.

rows.heading: Regulation of rates and tariffs
rows.groupTitle: Regulatory account treatment and rate-setting methods
rows.groupReason: Subsection (2.1) and 52(5)(a)–(f) set out how the Board must treat the regulatory deferral account (mandatory inclusion, no return, no financing costs), may treat the variance account and renewable gas infrastructure costs, and may adopt any method or alternative form of regulation.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Board shall include the regulatory deferral account in the revenue requirement but shall not permit a return on it or include related financing costs, may recognize a regulatory variance account and renewable gas infrastructure investment costs as part of regulated assets, and may adopt any method or technique including an alternative form of regulation in setting rates.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 52 pairs the core rate-setting prohibition and Board authority with a separate cluster of rules on how the Board must treat regulatory accounts and may choose its regulatory method.

rows.heading: Regulatory deferral account – 2017 to 2019
rows.groupTitle: Exclusion of regulatory deferral account from revenue requirement (2017–2019)
rows.groupReason: One short prohibition with a fixed 2017–2019 temporal scope; a single recall task (what restriction applied to the RDA in the revenue requirement and for whom).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the restriction that applied to the regulatory deferral account in the general franchise holder's revenue requirement during the period from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2019.

evidenceText: no portion of the regulatory deferral account shall be included in the revenue requirement of the general franchise holder

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 52.02 is a single, self-contained prohibition: for 2017–2019, no portion of the regulatory deferral account may be included in the revenue requirement of the general franchise holder. It states one rule with one actor, one restriction, and a fixed temporal scope, making it a natural standalone unit.

rows.heading: Return on equity – 2017 to 2019
rows.groupTitle: Excess return-on-equity allocation, 2017–2019
rows.groupReason: The entire subsection pair defines one tiered allocation formula for excess ROE: credits to the deferral account up to 200 basis points in full, half/half above that, with the excess half reducing rates for non-Small General Service customers.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the tiered allocation rule when the general franchise holder's actual return on equity exceeds 10.9% during 2017–2019, including the 200-basis-point threshold and the split between the regulatory deferral account and the following year's rate reduction.

evidenceText: no amounts shall be credited towards the balance in the regulatory deferral account except as provided for in this section
the amount that exceeds 10.9 per cent shall be allocated as follows

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 52.03 states one coherent allocation rule: during 2017–2019, excess returns on equity above 10.9% are split by tier between the regulatory deferral account and a future rate reduction. The prohibition in (1) and the tiered allocation in (2) are tightly interdependent and form a single recall task.

rows.heading: Recovery of balance
rows.groupTitle: Mandatory $100 million straight-line amortization rule
rows.groupReason: Subsection (3) imposes a specific mandatory rule that overrides the Board's general discretion in subsection (2), fixing the amount, method, and time frame for a defined portion of the balance.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the fixed recovery amount, amortization method, and applicable time period that the Board must authorize for the $100 million portion of the regulatory deferral account balance.

evidenceText: the Board shall authorize the recovery of $100 million of the balance in the regulatory deferral account on a fixed straight line amortization basis for the period commencing on January 1, 2020, and ending on December 31, 2045

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsections (1)–(2) form one coherent recovery mechanism (balance recovered through revenue requirement, Board discretion on manner and period), while subsection (3) is a distinct mandatory rule with its own fixed amount, method, and time frame that explicitly overrides subsection (2).

rows.heading: Recovery of balance
rows.groupTitle: Regulatory deferral account recovery mechanism and Board discretion
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) together state the general rule: the balance is recovered through the revenue requirement, and the Board determines the specific period and annual amounts on application under section 52.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the mechanism by which the regulatory deferral account balance is recovered and identify the parameters the Board may determine when authorizing that recovery.

evidenceText: the balance remaining in the regulatory deferral account after the amounts, if any, have been credited in accordance with section 52.03, shall be recovered by including in the revenue requirement of the general franchise holder

the Board shall authorize the recovery of the balance in the regulatory deferral account in any manner it considers appropriate, including determining the period during which the balance is to be recovered and the amounts to be included in the revenue requirement

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsections (1)–(2) form one coherent recovery mechanism (balance recovered through revenue requirement, Board discretion on manner and period), while subsection (3) is a distinct mandatory rule with its own fixed amount, method, and time frame that explicitly overrides subsection (2).

rows.heading: Return on equity
rows.groupTitle: Mandatory return on equity rate for gas rate orders
rows.groupReason: One operative rule: the Board shall permit a 10.9 per cent return on equity when approving or fixing rates and tariffs under sections 52.06 and 52.07.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the mandatory return-on-equity rate the Board must permit and identify the sections to which it applies.

evidenceText: the Board shall permit a return on equity of 10.9 per cent

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 52.05 is a single, self-contained mandatory rule fixing the return-on-equity rate at 10.9 per cent for Board rate and tariff decisions under sections 52.06 and 52.07. It forms one recall task and needs no split or combine.

rows.heading: Rates and tariffs freeze – 2017 to 2019
rows.groupTitle: Rates and tariffs freeze for five customer classes (2017–2019)
rows.groupReason: The freeze obligation, the five named customer classes, and the December 31 2019 expiry are one interdependent recall unit; separating classes from the freeze rule would fragment a single concept.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the five customer classes subject to the 2017–2019 rate freeze, the originating application date, the cross-referenced limiting provisions, and the expiry date of December 31, 2019.

evidenceText: the rates and tariffs approved or fixed by the Board with respect to the general franchise holder's application dated July 25, 2016, for the following classes of customers shall, in aggregate, be subject to a rates and tariffs freeze and shall remain in effect until December 31, 2019

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 52.07 is a single, self-contained time-limited rate freeze for five named customer classes (2017–2019); it forms one recall task but its fixed past period limits current study priority.

rows.heading: Burden of proof
rows.groupTitle: Burden of proof in gas distribution rates and tariffs applications
rows.groupReason: One procedural rule: identifies the actor (gas distributor) who must meet the burden of proof and the triggering context (application regarding rates and tariffs for gas distribution).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State which party bears the burden of proof in an application regarding rates and tariffs for gas distribution under the Gas Distribution Act.

evidenceText: the burden of proof is on the gas distributor

rows.sourceMapReason: Single-rule procedural assignment placing the burden of proof on the gas distributor in rates and tariffs applications; one clearly recallable concept.

rows.heading: Filing and inspection of schedules
rows.groupTitle: Filing and public inspection of approved rates and tariffs schedules
rows.groupReason: One recallable duty: the gas distributor must ensure approved rates and tariffs are publicly accessible both at the Board and at convenient locations in the Province, including providing copies on request.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State what a gas distributor must file with the Board and maintain at convenient locations in the Province regarding approved rates and tariffs, and the public inspection and copy-on-request obligations attached to each.

evidenceText: A gas distributor shall file with the Board schedules, which shall be open to public inspection, showing all rates and tariffs that the Board has approved

A gas distributor shall maintain at convenient locations in the Province, keep available for public inspection and make available to a member of the public who requests one, a copy of all rates and tariffs that the Board has approved

rows.sourceMapReason: Both subsections impose complementary public-access duties on the gas distributor regarding the same approved rates and tariffs, differing only in location (Board vs. convenient provincial locations) and form (filed schedules vs. maintained copies). They form one coherent transparency obligation best recalled together.

rows.heading: Change of rates and tariffs
rows.groupTitle: Board approval and filing requirement for rate or tariff changes
rows.groupReason: The prohibition, the Board proceeding condition, and the pre-effect schedule-filing duty form one recallable regulatory procedure for changing rates or tariffs.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions a gas distributor must satisfy before changing rates or tariffs and the filing obligation that applies to any approved change.

evidenceText: A gas distributor shall not make any change to its rates or tariffs for the distribution of gas except with the approval of the Board, after a proceeding determined by the Board
any approved change shall be plainly indicated on new schedules that shall be filed with the Board before the change comes into effect

rows.sourceMapReason: Single short provision stating one interdependent rule: no rate change without Board approval after a proceeding, plus a pre-effect filing duty for approved changes.

rows.heading: Safety and inspection of facilities
rows.groupTitle: Gas distributor safety and pre-distribution inspection duties
rows.groupReason: General safety standard and specific pre-distribution inspection procedure form one interrelated safety regime for the gas distributor.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the gas distributor's duty to furnish safe, adequate and proper service and the requirement to inspect building installations for statutory compliance and tightness before distributing gas.
rows.sourceMapReason: Both subsections impose interrelated safety duties on the gas distributor under one heading, forming a single recallable safety-and-inspection obligation.

rows.heading: Prohibition against marketing gas without a certificate
rows.groupTitle: Gas marketer certificate requirement and exemptions
rows.groupReason: Subsection 58(1) states the prohibition and 58(1.1) carves out five exemption categories; together they answer the single recall task of who must hold a certificate and who is exempt.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the four gas-marketing activities prohibited without a certificate and the five categories of persons exempt from the certificate requirement.

evidenceText: no person shall, unless the person holds a certificate, do any of the following
The following persons are exempt from the requirement to hold a certificate

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 58 contains two independently recallable rules: the certificate requirement with its exemptions (any person) and a separate name-matching restriction (certified gas marketers). Different actors, different legal questions, and distinct recall tasks justify two StudyUnits.

rows.heading: Prohibition against marketing gas without a certificate
rows.groupTitle: Name-matching restriction on certified gas marketers
rows.groupReason: Subsection 58(2) imposes a separate restriction on already-certified marketers regarding the trade name under which they may conduct marketing activities, distinct from the threshold certification question.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that a gas marketer must conduct marketing activities under the name in which it is certified unless the certificate authorizes another name.

evidenceText: in a name other than the one in which it is certified unless authorized to do so in the certificate

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 58 contains two independently recallable rules: the certificate requirement with its exemptions (any person) and a separate name-matching restriction (certified gas marketers). Different actors, different legal questions, and distinct recall tasks justify two StudyUnits.

rows.heading: Prices of gas and services may be fixed by order of the Board
rows.groupTitle: Board's Price-Regulation Power for Gas and Customer Services

rows.heading: Power to dispose of equipment, machinery or implements

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13 grants the Minister one coherent power to dispose of equipment, machinery or implements no longer required for highway purposes, spanning sale, lease, tender, and trade-as-credit in two tightly linked subsections.

rows.heading: Power to dispose of motor vehicles, trailers, towed equipment and industrial equipment

registered in the name of the Minister, or

rows.heading: Powers of Minister

may describe or re-describe any highway as a provincial highway or a provincial-municipal highway
may classify and reclassify any highway as an arterial highway, collector highway or local highway

rows.heading: Powers of Minister

rows.heading: Designation of road as highway

rows.sourceMapReason: All subsections serve one coherent mechanism: how the Minister designates, publishes, amends, and scopes a highway designation, forming a single recallable unit.

rows.heading: Development area
rows.groupTitle: Development area declaration: power and conditions
rows.groupReason: The declaration power and its two prerequisite conditions form a single threshold test for creating a development area under the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify which authority may declare a development area and the two Ministerial proposals that must be in place for the declaration to be made.

evidenceText: The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may declare an area of land to be a development area if the Minister proposes
to expend public money on the acquisition and development of that area of land for highway purposes
to acquire over a period of time all the lands in that area as they become available or are needed for highway purposes

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16 grants the Lieutenant-Governor in Council the power to declare a development area conditioned on two interdependent Ministerial proposals; one coherent recall unit with no need to combine or split.

rows.heading: Purchase and lease of land within development area
rows.groupTitle: Purchase, lease-back, and lease termination in a development area
rows.groupReason: All four subsections form one interdependent acquisition-to-termination mechanism that a learner must recall as a whole to understand how development-area land is obtained, leased back, and reclaimed.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Minister's power to acquire land in a development area, the duty to negotiate in good faith and lease back during a purchase, the lease-back power after expropriation, and the 30-day registered-mail termination procedure for those leases.

evidenceText: The Minister may acquire land within a development area by purchase or expropriation, when the land is required for and in connection with a highway

by giving the lessee 30 days' notice in writing to vacate and by sending that notice by registered mail to the lessee

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 17 presents one coherent acquisition-and-lease mechanism in a development area: the power to acquire by purchase or expropriation, the duty to negotiate in good faith and lease back during purchase, the parallel lease-back power after expropriation, and the 30-day registered-mail termination procedure. The four subsections are short, interdependent, and form a single recallable unit on how land is acquired and managed in a development area.

rows.heading: Request to Minister to purchase land within development area

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18 is a short, self-contained provision: 18(1) grants the owner a request right and 18(2) states the automatic consequence of the Minister's inaction. The two subsections are tightly interdependent and form one coherent recall concept.

rows.heading: Improvement on land within development area

evidenceText: No person shall construct an improvement or reconstruct or add to an improvement on any land within a development area except with the approval in writing of the Minister.

rows.sourceMapReason: One prohibition with a single dependent approval condition; no basis to split or combine.

rows.heading: Filings and notice of creation of development area

cause to be registered in the appropriate land registration office a notice to the persons who appear from the records of that office to be owners of the land in the development area that the land is subject to sections 16 to 22 and cause the notice to be sent by registered mail to those persons

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 20 sets out the complete ministerial filing, publication, registration, and mailing duties triggered when a development area is created under section 16, forming one coherent procedural unit.

rows.heading: Expropriation of land within development area

rows.heading: Interest in land within development area

evidenceText: Any person who holds or acquires an interest in land within a development area holds or acquires that interest subject to sections 16 to 21.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single clear rule binding every development-area land interest to sections 16–21; one actor, one legal effect, no internal complexity to split.

may enter upon any land for the purpose of making drains in which to carry off water from a highway and of keeping such drains in repair

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 23 grants the Minister six parallel powers targeting distinct objects (surveying, possession, materials, drainage, alteration, temporary detour). rows.heading: Compensation of landowner for injurious affection

rows.heading: Claim for compensation for injurious affection

rows.heading: Reasonable compensation for injurious affection

rows.sourceMapReason: Short provision establishing the Minister's duty to make a written compensation offer and give simultaneous notice of the court referral path when disagreeing with a claim.

rows.heading: Offer not accepted re injurious affection

rows.sourceMapReason: Operative provision creating a mandatory court-submission duty on the Minister for rejected injurious affection compensation; independently recallable from section 26's offer-and-notice requirement.

rows.heading: Powers of Minister, resistance or opposition

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 28 contains the Minister's enumerated removal, demolition, extraction, and entry powers in subsection (1) and a separate judicial warrant procedure for resistance to demolition in subsections (2) and (3), which are independently recallable.

rows.heading: Certificate of highway

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 29 grants the Minister a certification power over highways and assigns the certificate conclusive evidentiary weight; the power and its effect form one inseparable recallable rule.

rows.heading: Width of highway

rows.heading: Surrender of lease
