rows.groupTitle: Summons and Disclosure Protections for the Minister and Employees
rows.groupReason: Both subsections protect the Minister and employees in their official capacity—one limits court compulsion, the other restricts disclosure—forming one compact recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which the Minister or a Province employee may be compelled to appear or produce documents in court, and the circumstances in which an enforcement employee is prohibited from disclosing information obtained officially.

evidenceText: A summons to witness shall not issue out of any court requiring the attendance of the Minister or any employee of the Province in his official capacity
shall not disclose any information obtained by him in his official capacity that the Minister certifies is not in the public interest to be divulged

rows.sourceMapReason: Two short subsections forming a coherent set of official-capacity protections: a court-compulsion restriction (7(1)) and an employee non-disclosure duty (7(2)), both tied to the Minister's and employees' roles under the Act.

rows.heading: Right of entry – Crown land
rows.groupTitle: Right of Entry – Crown Land
rows.groupReason: Single conditional permission: Crown land entry for oil and natural gas exploration requires Minister's consent on terms the Minister prescribes, subject to the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which Crown lands may be entered and explored for oil and natural gas under section 8.

evidenceText: Crown lands may be entered upon and explored for oil and natural gas with the consent of the Minister upon such terms and conditions as he prescribes.

rows.sourceMapReason: Self-contained permission rule for Crown land entry conditioned on Minister's consent and prescribed terms; distinct from non-Crown land entry in s. 9 and independently recallable.

rows.heading: Right of entry
rows.groupTitle: Compensation liability for entry on Crown and non-Crown land
rows.groupReason: The parallel compensation provisions create distinct recall tasks on recipient, scope of compensable damage, application mechanism, and payment destination for each land category.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the compensation obligation, recipient, application mechanism, and payment destination for loss or damage caused by oil and gas entry operations on Crown land versus non-Crown land.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 9 contains three distinct recall tasks: the entry prohibition with its two methods and agent qualification, the scope limitation on surface rights, and the parallel compensation regimes for Crown and non-Crown land.

rows.heading: Right of entry
rows.groupTitle: Entry prohibition and methods on non-Crown land
rows.groupReason: The prohibition, the two entry methods (agreement or Minister's special order), and the agent qualification form one coherent lawful-entry recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the prohibition on entering non-Crown land for oil and gas operations, identify the two methods of obtaining right of entry, and state the qualification requirement for the person negotiating the agreement.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 9 contains three distinct recall tasks: the entry prohibition with its two methods and agent qualification, the scope limitation on surface rights, and the parallel compensation regimes for Crown and non-Crown land.

rows.heading: Right of entry
rows.groupTitle: Scope of surface use and possession rights
rows.groupReason: The 'necessary part of the surface' limitation for licence/lease holders versus geophysical licence holders is a distinct scope-of-right recall task separate from the entry requirement.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the 'necessary part of the surface' limitation on use and possession rights for holders of a licence to search, well licence, or lease versus holders of a geophysical licence.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 9 contains three distinct recall tasks: the entry prohibition with its two methods and agent qualification, the scope limitation on surface rights, and the parallel compensation regimes for Crown and non-Crown land.

rows.heading: Special order to enter and use land
rows.groupTitle: Special order application and grant procedure
rows.groupReason: These subsections form the complete trigger, notice precondition, hearing timeline, and sole-discretion decision procedure for obtaining a special order.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the eligible applicants, the five-clear-day notice precondition, the Minister's mandatory ten-clear-day hearing deadline, the sole-discretion grant-or-deny power, and the substituted-service accommodation for multiple owners.

evidenceText: may apply in writing to the Minister, for a special order to enter such land
served upon the owner, tenant or occupier of the land five clear days prior to the making of the application, written notice of the intention
shall fix a date for the hearing of the application which shall not be later than ten clear days
may in his sole discretion and without giving reasons therefor, grant or deny such special order

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 10 contains a coherent application-and-grant procedure (10(1)–(3), (6)) and a distinct post-grant compensation and security mechanism (10(4)–(5)) that raise independently recallable questions for a learner.

rows.heading: Special order to enter and use land
rows.groupTitle: Compensation referral and security for special order
rows.groupReason: The compensation-referral trigger and the security-before-entry requirement are interdependent post-grant rules distinct from the application procedure.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the trigger and forum for compensation referral under Part II of the Expropriation Act, the effective date of the special order, and the Minister's power to require section 54 security before entry.

evidenceText: the determination of the compensation shall be referred to The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick or any judge thereof acting under Part II of the Expropriation Act by either party

the special order is effective upon the date of issue, and the Minister may require the licensee, geophysical licensee, well licensee or lessee to give security in the form as prescribed in section 54

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 10 contains a coherent application-and-grant procedure (10(1)–(3), (6)) and a distinct post-grant compensation and security mechanism (10(4)–(5)) that raise independently recallable questions for a learner.

rows.heading: Termination of the special order
rows.groupTitle: Termination and continuation of a special order
rows.groupReason: One recall task: when does a special order terminate (two months, non-use or cessation of surface use) and how may the Minister continue it (indication to Minister, conditions warrant).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two-month non-use trigger for automatic termination of a special order, identify the affected license holders, and explain the Minister's power to continue the order.

evidenceText: If at any time after the expiration of two months from the date of a special order, the licensee, geophysical licensee, well licensee, or lessee has not commenced to use or ceases to use the surface of the land, or any part thereof, the special order terminates.
the Minister may, if in his opinion the conditions warrant, make an order continuing the special order.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 11 states one coherent rule: a special order auto-terminates after two months of non-use, and the Minister may continue it. Both subsections are tightly interdependent (11(2) directly responds to 11(1)) and form a single recallable concept.

rows.heading: Geophysical licence for exploration
rows.groupTitle: Geophysical Exploration Access Requirement
rows.groupReason: One prohibition with two dependent exceptions; recalling them separately would fragment a single authorization rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the prohibition on undertaking geophysical exploration and the two roles that authorize a person to do so.

evidenceText: No person, on his own behalf or for or on behalf of others, shall undertake geophysical exploration whether on land, water or by aircraft unless he is
(a) a geophysical licensee, or
(b) a permittee acting on behalf of a geophysical licensee.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single prohibition with two dependent exceptions forming one coherent recall task on who may undertake geophysical exploration.

rows.heading: Application for geophysical licence
rows.groupTitle: Application for and grant of geophysical licence
rows.groupReason: These subsections form one coherent application-and-grant concept: written application to the Minister, grant conditioned on regulatory terms and security under s.54, the Minister's ongoing power to add terms or require more security, and the exemption where security is already deposited.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the written application requirement, the conditions for the Minister to grant a geophysical licence (regulatory terms and security per s.54), the Minister's power to impose additional terms or require further security, and the exemption available when security is already on deposit with the Minister of Finance and Treasury Board.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13 covers the geophysical licence application/grant/security regime and a distinct refund-of-security procedure with separate recall tasks (how to obtain the licence versus how to recover the security deposit).

rows.heading: Application for geophysical licence
rows.groupTitle: Refund of geophysical licence security
rows.groupReason: The refund provision states a distinct procedural outcome with specific evidentiary conditions (compliance with Act and regulations, and submission of all required reports) that a learner recalls independently of the application process.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the two conditions the geophysical licensee must evidence, to the Minister's satisfaction, to obtain a refund of the security: that operations were conducted in accordance with the Act and regulations, and that all required reports and information have been submitted.

evidenceText: the security shall be refunded to the geophysical licensee upon evidence being furnished, to the satisfaction of the Minister, that the operations were conducted in accordance with this Act and the regulations and that all reports and information required under this Act and the regulations have been submitted.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13 covers the geophysical licence application/grant/security regime and a distinct refund-of-security procedure with separate recall tasks (how to obtain the licence versus how to recover the security deposit).

rows.heading: Transferability of geophysical licence
rows.groupTitle: Non-transferability of geophysical licence
rows.groupReason: One prohibition with a single consent condition; no separate actors, triggers, or modalities warranting a split.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the condition under which a geophysical licence may be transferred.

evidenceText: A geophysical licence is not transferable without the written consent of the Minister.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 14 states one clear prohibition — a geophysical licence is not transferable without the Minister's written consent — forming a single recallable rule with no internal subdivisions to split.

rows.heading: Cancellation of geophysical licence by Minister
rows.groupTitle: Cancellation of geophysical licence by Minister
rows.groupReason: One coherent procedural unit: ground for cancellation, notice-and-rectification safeguard with danger exception, and mandatory written acknowledgement after rectification.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the ground on which the Minister may cancel a geophysical licence, the notice and rectification procedure (including the danger-to-person-or-property exception), and the Minister's duty to issue written acknowledgement of satisfactory rectification.

evidenceText: The Minister may cancel a geophysical licence where the holder of such licence does not comply with a provision of this Act or the regulations.
the Minister shall not cancel a geophysical licence under subsection (1) until he has given the holder thereof thirty days notice, or such longer time as he deems advisable, to rectify the default
the Minister shall give the geophysical licensee written acknowledgement that the rectification is satisfactory and that he may continue operations

rows.sourceMapReason: All three subsections form one tight cancellation procedure: the ground (non-compliance), the notice-and-rectification safeguard with its danger exception, and the post-rectification acknowledgement duty. They are interdependent and short enough to recall as a single mechanism.

rows.heading: Exclusive right of licensee or lessee to do work
rows.groupTitle: Exclusive right of licensee or lessee and geophysical licensee exception
rows.groupReason: One coherent concept: the exclusivity rule, the geophysical licensee's permitted activities by depth and type, and the non-interference condition on those activities.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the exclusive right of a licensee or lessee to do geophysical and exploratory drilling work, the three categories of permitted geophysical licensee activities (testhole drilling to 150 m, testhole drilling to 450 m with written Ministerial approval, and other geological/geophysical exploration), and the prohibition on interfering with enumerated mining and other rights holders.

evidenceText: a licensee or lessee has the exclusive right to do geophysical work and geophysical exploration work and exploratory drilling for oil or natural gas, or both, within the boundaries of his licence to search or lease
carry out testhole drilling to a depth of one hundred fifty metres
A person who performs exploration activities as described in subsection (2) shall not interfere with the operations of any holder of a mining or mineral claim or mining lease under the Mining Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsections (1), (2), and (3) form a tight rule/exception/condition structure defining the exclusive right to do oil-and-gas work and the limits on the geophysical licensee's carve-out; they are needed together to recall the complete scope of the right.

rows.heading: Terms and conditions on a geophysical permit
rows.groupTitle: Minister's power to impose terms and conditions on a geophysical permit
rows.groupReason: One ministerial power with a defined standard ("what the Minister considers appropriate") forming a single recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Minister's authority to impose terms and conditions on a geophysical permit, the timing, and the standard applied.

evidenceText: The Minister may, at any time, impose any terms and conditions on a geophysical permit that the Minister considers appropriate.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16.01 states a single ministerial power to impose terms and conditions on a geophysical permit; one recallable concept with no internal sub-structure to split.

rows.heading: Abandonment of shotholes and testholes
rows.groupTitle: Plugging duty for shotholes and testholes and conflict resolution
rows.groupReason: The plugging duty, its two compliance mechanisms, and the Minister-method-prevails conflict rule are one interdependent recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the permittee's obligation to plug shotholes and testholes, the two compliance paths (regulations or Minister's method), and which prevails in a conflict.

evidenceText: A permittee shall plug a shothole or testhole in accordance with the regulations or with the method required by the Minister.
If a conflict exists between the regulations and the method required by the Minister, the method required by the Minister prevails.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16.02 is a short, tightly interdependent provision: subsection (1) imposes the plugging duty and its two compliance paths, and subsection (2) resolves conflicts between those paths. Together they form one recall task.

rows.heading: Granting of well licence
rows.groupTitle: Minister's power to grant a well licence and impose terms
rows.groupReason: Subsection (1) sets the two grant conditions (satisfaction with drilling program and compliance with s. 16.3); subsection (2) adds the Minister's terms-and-conditions power; together they define the licensing decision.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two conditions that must be met before the Minister may grant a well licence and identify the Minister's power to impose terms and conditions on the licence.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16.2 is a short, self-contained provision stating the Minister's discretionary power to grant a well licence and to impose terms and conditions; both subsections form one coherent licensing-grant concept.

rows.heading: Application for well licence
rows.groupTitle: Required components of a well licence application
rows.groupReason: All five items (form, fee, security deposit, $10,000,000 liability insurance proof, drilling program with completion program, and any prescribed information) form one coherent filing requirement for the applicant.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify every document and item that must accompany a well licence application under section 16.3, including the $10,000,000 liability insurance proof and the drilling program with completion program.

evidenceText: proof of liability insurance coverage in the amount of $10,000,000 for the applicant or his or her agents
the applicant’s proposed drilling program, which includes the completion program

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16.3 is a single procedural requirement listing all items that must accompany a well licence application; every item answers the same recall question and involves the same actor (the applicant).

rows.heading: Amendment of well licence
rows.groupTitle: Grounds and requirements for amending a well licence
rows.groupReason: Mandatory triggers, permissive right, form requirement, and fee rule form one short, recallable procedural concept for well licence amendment applications.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the three mandatory triggers and the permissive ground for applying to amend a well licence, and state the form and fee requirements that attach to such applications.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16.4 is a short, coherent procedural unit covering the mandatory and permissive grounds for amending a well licence plus the associated form and fee requirements; the pieces are tightly interdependent as one application mechanism.

rows.heading: Transfer of well licence
rows.groupTitle: Well licence transfer: Minister's approval and application requirements
rows.groupReason: Subsection (1) sets the approval requirement and (2) specifies the form and three accompanying items; together they answer the single recall task of what is needed to transfer a well licence.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that a well licence is not transferable without the Minister's written approval and identify the three items that must accompany the transfer application.

evidenceText: A well licence is not transferable without the written approval of the Minister.

An application to obtain the approval of the Minister to transfer a well licence shall be on a form provided by the Minister and shall be accompanied by the following: (a) the fee prescribed by regulation; (b) the security deposit prescribed by regulation; and (c) proof of liability insurance coverage in the amount of $10,000,000 for the person to whom the well licence is to be transferred.

rows.sourceMapReason: One coherent transfer mechanism: the prohibition on transfer without the Minister's written approval and the application requirements to obtain that approval form a single recallable procedural rule.

rows.heading: Liability insurance
rows.groupTitle: Well licensee liability insurance obligations
rows.groupReason: The maintenance duty ($10,000,000 coverage for the licensee or agents) and the notification duty (immediate notice to the Minister of any change or cancellation) are interdependent pieces of one insurance-compliance rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the required liability insurance amount a well licensee must maintain during the licence term and the immediate notification duty to the Minister upon any change in coverage, including cancellation.
rows.sourceMapReason: Two tightly linked duties (maintain $10M coverage; notify the Minister of any change or cancellation) form one recallable insurance-compliance obligation for well licensees.

rows.heading: Cancellation of well licence
rows.groupTitle: Cancellation of well licence: notice, compliance schedule, and post-cancellation liability
rows.groupReason: The three subsections form one sequential cancellation procedure: trigger and notice, cancellation for failure to remedy, and continuing liability after cancellation.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Minister's written notice and compliance-schedule requirement, the cancellation trigger when the violation is not remedied, and the licensee's continuing obligation after a well licence is cancelled.

evidenceText: the Minister may give written notice to the well licensee specifying the violation or non-compliance and setting out a schedule for compliance
the Minister may cancel the well licence
the well licensee continues to be liable for any obligation for which the licensee was liable under this Act or the regulations immediately before the cancellation

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16.6 is a single short procedural mechanism (violation notice → compliance schedule → cancellation → continuing liability) whose subsections are tightly interdependent and form one recallable cancellation procedure.

rows.heading: Return of security deposit
rows.groupTitle: Return of well licence security deposit
rows.groupReason: One short mandatory rule: the deposit shall be returned upon transfer or abandonment to the Minister's satisfaction.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the two triggers (transfer of a well licence or abandonment of a well to the Minister's satisfaction) that obligate return of the security deposit to the well licensee.

evidenceText: If a well licensee transfers a well licence or abandons a well to the satisfaction of the Minister, the security deposit shall be returned to that well licensee.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16.7 is a single, self-contained operative rule stating a mandatory return obligation triggered by transfer or abandonment of a well licence to the Minister's satisfaction. It forms one coherent recall task with no need to split or combine.

rows.heading: Licence to search
rows.groupTitle: Minister's power to grant a licence to search and terms authority
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (3) together define the scope of what may be granted and the Minister's authority to impose terms and conditions within the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the scope of the Minister's power to grant a licence to search for oil, natural gas, or both, and the authority to impose terms and conditions within the Act.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 17 contains three distinct recall tasks: the Minister's granting power and terms authority, a mandatory tender requirement with specific triggers, and exclusivity prohibitions on concurrent holdings.

rows.heading: Licence to search
rows.groupTitle: Tender requirement before granting a licence to search
rows.groupReason: Subsection (2) imposes a mandatory tender procedure triggered by land previously unlicensed or by expiry, cancellation, or surrender of a prior holding.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the circumstances in which the Minister must call for tenders before granting a licence to search and the prescribed manner requirement.

evidenceText: the Minister shall call for tenders for the purchase of such licence to search in a manner prescribed by regulation

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 17 contains three distinct recall tasks: the Minister's granting power and terms authority, a mandatory tender requirement with specific triggers, and exclusivity prohibitions on concurrent holdings.

rows.heading: Licence to search
rows.groupTitle: Exclusivity restrictions on licences to search
rows.groupReason: Subsection (4) states two prohibitions: no overlapping licences for the same area and no licence where a lease is already in force.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two exclusivity prohibitions: no more than one licence in force for the same area and no licence for land with a lease in force.

evidenceText: Not more than one such licence to search shall be granted and in force at the same time covering the same area or part of an area, nor shall any such licence to search be granted for land for which a lease is in force

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 17 contains three distinct recall tasks: the Minister's granting power and terms authority, a mandatory tender requirement with specific triggers, and exclusivity prohibitions on concurrent holdings.

rows.heading: Size of licence area
rows.groupTitle: Size limits of a licence area
rows.groupReason: Both the upper cap (one hundred sections) and the lower floor (special spacing area) answer the same recall question and belong in one unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the maximum and minimum size limits for a licence area contained in one licence to search under the Oil and Natural Gas Act.

evidenceText: A licence area contained in one licence to search shall not exceed one hundred sections and shall not be less than a special spacing area.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18 states a single, self-contained size rule for a licence-to-search area (maximum one hundred sections, minimum a special spacing area), forming one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: On-shore or off-shore licence
rows.groupTitle: Minister's duty to designate licence as on-shore or off-shore
rows.groupReason: One short designation duty on the Minister; a single recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Minister's obligation to designate a licence to search as on-shore or off-shore at the time of granting.

evidenceText: The Minister shall at the time of granting of the licence to search designate the licence as an on-shore or off-shore licence to search.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19 imposes a single, unambiguous 'shall' duty on the Minister to classify each licence to search as on-shore or off-shore at granting; it is one recallable procedural obligation.

rows.heading: Validity of on-shore and off-shore licences
rows.groupTitle: Off-shore licence to search – validity, renewal procedure, and deposit condition
rows.groupReason: Cohesive off-shore regime: staggered term structure, 30-day advance renewal application with fee and deposit, and the ongoing deposit-maintenance condition tied to the work requirement.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Describe the off-shore licence term structure (2 + 2 + up to 6 annual periods), the 30-day renewal application requirement with prescribed fee and deposit, and the deposit-maintenance condition on each renewal.

evidenceText: An off-shore licence to search is valid for an initial term of two years and may be renewed for a second period of two years and thereafter for a maximum of six consecutive annual periods
Every renewal of an off-shore licence is subject to the licensee maintaining a deposit with the Minister in an amount at least equivalent to the work requirement for the term of the renewal period.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 20 establishes two distinct licence regimes (on-shore and off-shore) with different terms, extension/renewal procedures, and conditions, forming two independently recallable concepts.

rows.heading: Validity of on-shore and off-shore licences
rows.groupTitle: On-shore licence to search – validity and extension
rows.groupReason: Cohesive rule-set: three-year base term plus the extension mechanism (application with stated reasons, Minister's satisfaction of circumstances, discretionary period).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the three-year term of an on-shore licence to search and the conditions under which the Minister may grant an extension.

evidenceText: An on-shore licence to search is valid for a term of three years.
If the Minister is satisfied that the circumstances justify the extension, the Minister may extend the on-shore licence to search for the period of time the Minister considers necessary.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 20 establishes two distinct licence regimes (on-shore and off-shore) with different terms, extension/renewal procedures, and conditions, forming two independently recallable concepts.

rows.heading: Work deposits
rows.groupTitle: Work deposit requirement and exploratory-work obligation under a licence to search
rows.groupReason: The licensee's duty to perform exploratory work and the Minister's duty to require a deposit at least equivalent to that work form one interdependent security mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the licensee's exploratory-work obligation during the term of a licence to search and the Minister's requirement to collect a security deposit before the licence is granted.

evidenceText: the licensee shall do or cause to be done on the area for which the licence to search was granted, exploratory work to the satisfaction of the Minister in an amount prescribed by regulation

Before a licence to search is granted, the Minister shall require the licensee to deposit with the Minister of Finance and Treasury Board an amount at least equivalent to the work requirement prescribed by regulation for the term of the licence to search

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 21(1) and (2) together form the work-deposit mechanism: the licensee's exploratory-work duty and the Minister's requirement for a security deposit measured against that work. They are tightly interdependent and constitute one recallable concept. Subsection (3) is repealed.

rows.heading: Redistribution of work requirements
rows.groupTitle: Redistribution of exploratory work expenditures
rows.groupReason: The three eligibility conditions and the Minister's redistribution power form one interdependent procedural mechanism best recalled together.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the three conditions a licensee must satisfy to apply for redistribution of exploratory work expenditures and describe what the Minister may redistribute on application.
rows.sourceMapReason: A short, self-contained provision setting out the conditions for a licensee to apply to redistribute exploratory work expenditures and the Minister's corresponding redistribution power.

rows.heading: Surrender of licence to search
rows.groupTitle: Surrender of Licence to Search
rows.groupReason: A single permission with one precondition forms one recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the condition that must be satisfied before a licence to search may be surrendered.

evidenceText: A licence to search may be surrendered if all work requirements for the term have been met.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 21.1 states one clear permission (surrender of a licence to search) with one precondition (all work requirements met); the repealed 'Grouping of Licences to Search' heading carries no operative content.

rows.heading: Application for lease
rows.groupTitle: Application for lease and Minister's mandatory grant
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) form a single application-and-grant transaction: the licensee's right to apply during the term and the Minister's duty to grant upon compliance are interdependent recall items.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State when a licensee may apply for a lease during the licence-to-search term and the Minister's obligation to grant the lease upon compliance with the Act and regulations.

evidenceText: The licensee, at any time during the continuance of the term of the licence to search may apply, in a manner prescribed by regulation, to the Minister for a lease.
The Minister upon receipt of an application under subsection (1) shall grant the lease subject to the terms and conditions he imposes if the licensee has complied with this Act and the regulations.

rows.sourceMapReason: The section contains two distinct procedural mechanisms with different triggers and conditions: an application during the licence term (26(1)–(2)) and an end-of-term conversion with surrender of unconverted areas (26(3), 26(5)).

rows.heading: Application for lease
rows.groupTitle: Conversion of licence to lease at term end and surrender of unconverted areas
rows.groupReason: Subsection (3) sets the end-of-term conversion condition (exploration commitments met in the Minister's opinion) and subsection (5) states the consequence for unconverted sections; together they form one complete conversion-and-surrender rule distinct from the during-term application.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the condition for converting a licence to search to a lease in its entirety at the end of the licence term and the disposition of licence-area sections not included in the conversion.

evidenceText: A licence to search may be converted to a lease in its entirety at the end of the licence term, if in the opinion of the Minister, all exploration commitments under the licence have been met.
Those sections within each licence area that are not included in the areas converted from licence to search to lease shall be surrendered to the Crown in right of the Province.

rows.sourceMapReason: The section contains two distinct procedural mechanisms with different triggers and conditions: an application during the licence term (26(1)–(2)) and an end-of-term conversion with surrender of unconverted areas (26(3), 26(5)).

rows.heading: Lease for oil and gas production rights
rows.groupTitle: Lease grant to a licence-to-search holder
rows.groupReason: Subsection 27(1) is a self-contained grant power: a single applicant class, a single trigger, and a discretionary outcome that a learner must recall as one unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may grant a lease only upon written application by the holder of a licence to search for the specific lands in question.

evidenceText: The Minister, upon written application, may grant a lease where the application is made by the holder of a licence to search for the lands for which the application is made.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 27 contains two distinct procedural mechanisms: (1) initial lease grant to a licence-to-search holder and (2) transfer of a lease area to a new lessee, explicitly carved out by 'notwithstanding.' They involve different applicants, different triggers, and separate legal modalities, making them independently recallable.

rows.heading: Lease for oil and gas production rights
rows.groupTitle: Transfer of lease area to another lessee
rows.groupReason: Subsection 27(2) operates notwithstanding 27(1), involving a different applicant (the lessee), a different scope (whole or part of the lease area), and a mixed modality (discretionary approval plus mandatory new-lease grant on prescribed terms).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may approve transfer of the whole or part of a lease area to another lessee and must, upon such transfer, grant a new lease to the transferee on terms and conditions prescribed by the Minister.

evidenceText: approve the transfer of the whole or part of the lease area to another lessee, and shall upon such transfer grant a new lease to such transferee upon such terms and conditions as are prescribed by the Minister.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 27 contains two distinct procedural mechanisms: (1) initial lease grant to a licence-to-search holder and (2) transfer of a lease area to a new lessee, explicitly carved out by 'notwithstanding.' They involve different applicants, different triggers, and separate legal modalities, making them independently recallable.

rows.heading: Call for tenders for lease
rows.groupTitle: Lease grant by call for tenders – conditions
rows.groupReason: Minister's power to grant a lease to a successful bidder conditioned on a compliant tender process and absence of overlapping licences or leases.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the two conditions that must both be met before the Minister may grant a lease to a successful bidder under section 27.1.

evidenceText: The Minister may grant a lease to a successful bidder
where a call for tenders for the purchase of the lease has been made in accordance with the regulations
where no other licence to search or lease is in force covering the same area or part of the same area

rows.sourceMapReason: One short provision stating a single ministerial power with two tightly interdependent conditions; one coherent recall task on tender-based lease granting.

rows.heading: Abandonment and release of lease
rows.groupTitle: Lessee's right to abandon and release part of the demised area
rows.groupReason: One permission (partial release to the Crown) and its operative effect (release from exploration/development duty for the released portion) form a single tightly interdependent recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the lessee's right to abandon and release any part of the demised area to the Crown and the effect on the lessee's obligation to explore or develop the released portion.

evidenceText: A lessee may, at any time, abandon and release to the Crown any part of the demised area and shall not thereafter be bound to explore or develop such portion of the area so released.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 28 grants a lessee a clear, self-contained right to partially abandon and release a demised area to the Crown, with a stated effect on exploration and development obligations. One actor, one permission, one consequence — a single recallable rule.

rows.heading: Surrender of lease
rows.groupTitle: Licensee's right to release part of demised area
rows.groupReason: Single right with its operative effect on exploration and development obligations, independently recallable as one concept.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the right a licensee has under section 28.1 to abandon and release part of the demised area to the Crown and the effect of that release on exploration and development obligations.

evidenceText: A licensee may, at any time, abandon and release to the Crown any part of the demised area and shall not thereafter be bound to explore or develop such portion of the area so released.

rows.sourceMapReason: Short, self-contained provision granting a licensee the right to release part of the demised area to the Crown with a clear legal consequence; forms one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Exclusive production rights
rows.groupTitle: Exclusive production right of licensee or lessee
rows.groupReason: One operative rule granting an exclusive production right tied to the respective licence or lease area.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who holds the exclusive right to produce or cause to be produced oil and natural gas and the area from which that right operates.
rows.sourceMapReason: A single, self-contained substantive right with one clear recall task; no structural basis to combine or split.

rows.heading: Term of lease
rows.groupTitle: Standard term of an oil and natural gas lease
rows.groupReason: One mandatory rule setting the five-year lease term; independently recallable as the standard lease duration under the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the mandatory term for which a lease under the Oil and Natural Gas Act shall be granted.

evidenceText: A lease shall be granted for a term of five years.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 30 states a single, clear mandatory rule: a lease shall be granted for a term of five years. This is a core operative lease-term requirement with independent recall value, best studied as one focused unit.

rows.heading: Extension of lease
rows.groupTitle: Extension of lease: application and Minister's discretion
rows.groupReason: Single recall task: what are the steps, requirements, and decision standard for extending a lease term under section 30.1.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the lessee's right to apply for a lease extension, the requirement to state reasons, and the Minister's discretionary standard and duration authority.

evidenceText: a lessee may apply, on a form provided by the Minister, for an extension of the term of the lease
The lessee shall set out in the application the reasons for the extension
If the Minister is satisfied that the circumstances justify the extension, the Minister may extend the lease for the period of time the Minister considers necessary

rows.sourceMapReason: Three short subsections form one tightly coupled lease-extension procedure: the lessee's right to apply, the required content of the application, and the Minister's decision standard.

rows.heading: Rental reductions
rows.groupTitle: Rental reduction: Minister's power, application conditions, and consolidated-lease exclusion
rows.groupReason: One recallable concept: the conditions, limits, and prohibition governing a pre-production rental-reduction application to the Minister.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the pre-production condition, the Minister's reduction cap, the three application requirements (30-day timing, affidavit contents, one-half annual cap), and the consolidated-lease prohibition under s. 31.

evidenceText: the Minister may, upon written application, order the reduction of the rental payable under lease by an amount not exceeding the allowable expenditures, as determined by the Minister, that have been made by the lessee on exploration work within the lease area during the previous year
A lessee may not make an application under subsection (1) with respect to a consolidated lease.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 31 is a single coherent mechanism: the Minister's pre-production rental-reduction power, its three application conditions, and the consolidated-lease exclusion. All pieces are needed to recall how rental reduction works.

rows.heading: Idem
rows.groupTitle: Rental Reduction Carry-Forward and Commercial Production Cutoff
rows.groupReason: 32(1) carries forward an unused section 31 reduction into a subsequent year's rental, and 32(2) terminates that carry-forward once commercial production has commenced; together they define the temporal scope of rental reductions.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the rule for carrying forward an unused section 31 rental reduction to a subsequent year and identify when that reduction mechanism ceases to apply.

evidenceText: the rental for any subsequent year shall be reduced subject to paragraph 31(c) by the amount of that part
the rental shall not be reduced pursuant to section 31 for any year following a year in which commercial production has commenced

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 32 contains a tightly coupled carry-forward rule (32(1)) and its directly dependent commercial-production cutoff (32(2)); the two subsections form one recall task on when unused rental reductions apply and when they stop.

rows.heading: Consolidated leases
rows.groupTitle: Consolidated lease: application, grant criteria, and pre-grant financial requirements
rows.groupReason: Application right, two grant criteria, and two mandatory pre-grant payments are one sequential mechanism best recalled as a unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State how a lessee applies for a consolidated lease, the two conditions under which the Minister may grant it, and the two financial requirements the Minister shall impose before granting.

evidenceText: A lessee may apply to the Minister in writing for a consolidated lease by which the lease areas included in more than one lease will be grouped as a single lease area.
The Minister may grant a lessee a consolidated lease if (a) the leases proposed to be consolidated are held by the same lessee, and (b) the lease areas are contiguous.

Before the Minister grants a consolidated lease, the Minister shall require the lessee to do the following: (a) deposit with the Minister of Finance and Treasury Board an amount at least equivalent to the work requirement prescribed by regulation for the first year of the term of the consolidated lease; and (b) pay to the Minister of Finance and Treasury Board the annual rent prescribed by regulation for the first year of the term of the consolidated lease, less any annual rent previously paid

rows.sourceMapReason: Three short subsections form one interdependent mechanism: application, grant criteria, and pre-grant financial requirements for a consolidated lease.

rows.heading: Forfeiture
rows.groupTitle: Forfeiture for Non-Payment of Deposit or Rental
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) form one interdependent trigger–notice–cancellation procedure specific to non-payment of deposit or rental, with a mandatory (shall) notice and a 30-day cure window.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the trigger (failure to make deposit or pay rental within 30 days), the Minister's mandatory written notice, and the 30-day cure period before the lease or licence to search is cancelled.

evidenceText: Where a lessee or licensee does not make the deposit or pay the rental required by regulation within thirty days from the date the deposit or rental is due, the Minister shall give written notice to the lessee or licensee as the case may be, specifying the default.

If the default referred to in subsection (1) is not remedied within thirty days of the date of the Minister's notice under subsection (1), the licence to search or lease, as the case may be, shall be cancelled by the Minister.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 34 contains two distinct forfeiture tracks with different triggers, different notice modalities (shall vs. may), and different cross-referenced scopes, each pairing a notice step with a mandatory cancellation consequence.

rows.heading: Forfeiture
rows.groupTitle: Forfeiture for Other Violations of the Act or Regulations
rows.groupReason: Subsections (3) and (4) form a separate procedural track covering all violations other than non-payment, with a discretionary (may) notice, a 'prepare to remedy' standard, and a regulation-eligible earlier cure period.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the scope (all violations other than non-payment), the Minister's discretionary written notice, the 30-day cure or prepare-to-remedy standard, and the mandatory cancellation of the lease or licence to search.

evidenceText: Where a lessee or licensee violates any provision of this Act or the regulations other than those referred to in subsection (1), the Minister may give written notice to the lessee or licensee, as the case may be, specifying the violation.

Unless the lessee or licensee, as the case may be, remedies or prepares to remedy the violation to the satisfaction of the Minister within thirty days from the date of the Minister's notice referred to in subsection (3), or such earlier time as is provided by regulation, the Minister shall cancel the lease or licence to search.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 34 contains two distinct forfeiture tracks with different triggers, different notice modalities (shall vs. may), and different cross-referenced scopes, each pairing a notice step with a mandatory cancellation consequence.

rows.heading: Surveys
rows.groupTitle: Survey System Requirement for Locations
rows.groupReason: Imposes a binding requirement that all locations under the Act conform to the regulatory survey system.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the survey-system conformity requirement that applies to locations under the Oil and Natural Gas Act.

evidenceText: a location shall be based on the survey system as set forth by regulation

rows.sourceMapReason: A single, self-contained shall-requirement: locations under the Act must be based on the survey system as set forth by regulation. One recallable rule, one actor, one modality.

rows.heading: Powers of the Minister
rows.groupTitle: Designation and operation of fields and pools
rows.groupReason: Paragraphs (a)–(c) form a coherent sub-concept: identifying a geological unit and deciding what it will produce.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Minister designates a field or pool (surface-area description, geological formation, zone) and determines whether it is operated for oil, natural gas, or both.

evidenceText: designate a field by describing the surface area thereof
determine whether a field or pool as described under paragraph (a) or (b) is to be operated for the production of oil or natural gas, or both

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 36 lists ten concurrent Ministerial powers spanning three distinct recall tasks: geological-unit designation and operation, production/water regulation, and spacing/paying-quantity rules. The thematic groupings create independently testable concepts.

rows.heading: Powers of the Minister
rows.groupTitle: Production control, allocation, and water disposal
rows.groupReason: Paragraphs (d)–(g) cover the Minister's operational toolkit: well-area allocation, production restriction/proration/prohibition, produced-water disposal, and water-covered-area drilling conditions.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister's powers to allocate well areas for allowable production, restrict/prorate/prohibit output of oil, natural gas, and water, require disposal of produced water, and prescribe drilling conditions in water-covered areas.

evidenceText: control and regulate the production of oil, natural gas, and water by restriction, proration, or prohibition
require the disposal into an underground formation or otherwise, in accordance with such terms and conditions as he prescribes, of any water produced
prescribe the conditions under which drilling operations are to be carried out in a water-covered area

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 36 lists ten concurrent Ministerial powers spanning three distinct recall tasks: geological-unit designation and operation, production/water regulation, and spacing/paying-quantity rules. The thematic groupings create independently testable concepts.

rows.heading: Powers of the Minister
rows.groupTitle: Spacing areas and paying quantity
rows.groupReason: Paragraphs (g.1), (h), and (i) address well-spacing determinations and the economic threshold of paying quantity, a distinct regulatory concept from production control.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister's powers to determine special spacing areas, prescribe non-normal spacing in a field or pool, and define paying quantity for any well in the Province.

evidenceText: determine special spacing areas
prescribe other than a normal spacing area in any field, pool, or other area
prescribe what constitutes paying quantity with respect to any well drilled within the Province

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 36 lists ten concurrent Ministerial powers spanning three distinct recall tasks: geological-unit designation and operation, production/water regulation, and spacing/paying-quantity rules. The thematic groupings create independently testable concepts.

rows.heading: Power of Minister to restrict oil or natural gas produced
rows.groupTitle: Minister's power to restrict oil and natural gas production
rows.groupReason: One Ministerial restriction power with four interdependent methods covering the oil allocation hierarchy and the separate natural gas pool-level limit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the four methods by which the Minister may restrict production: fixing a provincial allowable oil rate, allocating it among pools, distributing it among wells in a pool, and limiting natural gas output per pool for efficient use and reserve utilization.

evidenceText: fixing a Provincial allowable rate of production for oil not exceeding the market demand as determined by the Minister
limiting the total amount of natural gas that may be produced from any pool without waste, having regard to the market demand for natural gas

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 37 grants the Minister a single restriction power over oil and natural gas production, exercised through four enumerated methods forming one cohesive mechanism (a three-tier oil allocation cascade plus a gas pool-level limit). Short, unified, and independently recallable as one concept.

rows.heading: Powers of Minister to prevent waste
rows.groupTitle: Minister's powers to prevent waste (repressuring and gas disposition)
rows.groupReason: Both (a) pool-pressure powers and (b) gas-gathering/marketing powers are facets of the single waste-prevention authority and are best recalled together.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the two categories of measures the Minister may require to prevent waste: pool repressuring/recycling/pressure maintenance (including injection of substances) and gas gathering, processing, marketing, or storage.

evidenceText: In order to prevent waste, the Minister may
require the repressuring, recycling, or pressure maintenance of any pool or portion thereof

require that any natural gas be gathered and processed if necessary, and that the natural gas or liquid hydrocarbon extracted therefrom be marketed or injected into an underground reservoir for storage

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 38 is a self-contained ministerial power provision defining two interrelated waste-prevention orders (pool pressure maintenance and gas gathering/processing/marketing) under one purpose and actor. Both sub-powers share the same modality and context, forming one coherent recall unit.

rows.heading: Duty of Minister to approve schemes
rows.groupTitle: Ministerial approval requirement for field and gas schemes (s. 39)
rows.groupReason: The prohibition, its three scheme categories, and the Ministerial approval condition are interdependent and answer one recall question.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the three categories of schemes that require Ministerial approval by order and note that approval is upon terms and conditions the Minister prescribes.

evidenceText: No person shall proceed with a scheme for (a) repressuring, recycling, or pressure maintenance in any field or pool, (b) the processing, storage, or disposal of natural gas, or (c) the gathering, storage and disposal of water produced from any field or pool, unless the Minister, by order, has approved the scheme upon the terms and conditions the Minister prescribes.

rows.sourceMapReason: One coherent prohibition with three scheme categories defining scope and a Ministerial approval-by-order condition forming a single recallable rule.

rows.heading: Prevention of loss or damage
rows.groupTitle: Minister's power to control well escapes and uncontrolled water
rows.groupReason: One ministerial power with a disjunctive trigger and a single public-interest standard; no independent sub-concepts warrant separate recall.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the trigger conditions (unprevented escape of oil or natural gas, uncontrolled water flow) and state the Minister's discretionary power and the 'necessary or expedient in the public interest' standard for intervening.

evidenceText: If at any time an escape of oil or natural gas from a well is not prevented or if a flow of water is not controlled, the Minister may take such means as appear to him to be necessary or expedient in the public interest to control and prevent the escape of oil, natural gas, or water.

rows.sourceMapReason: A single, compact ministerial power with one trigger condition, one actor, and one standard; it forms one recallable concept without needing to split or combine.

rows.heading: Order to prohibit production or shut down, direction to discontinue operation
rows.groupTitle: Minister's inquiry-based well shut-in order and pre-inquiry emergency direction
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) are interdependent: (2) is an emergency direction pending the inquiry conducted under (1), sharing the same well-operation context and proceeding.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions for the Minister's post-inquiry shut-in order (contravention finding after notice) and the pre-inquiry emergency shutdown direction (waste, damage to property, or pollution prevention, with the inquiry held within fifteen days).

evidenceText: he may order that on and after a date to be fixed by him no production is to be permitted from the well and that it is to be shut in and kept shut in until such time as he directs to the contrary
he may direct that a well be shut down pending an inquiry under subsection (1), which shall be held within fifteen days of the making of the direction

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsections (1) and (2) form one interdependent inquiry-based shutdown mechanism, while (3) operates on a distinct trigger, scope, form, and resolution warranting a separate recall task.

rows.heading: Order to prohibit production or shut down, direction to discontinue operation
rows.groupTitle: Minister's oral direction to discontinue inadequate or hazardous operations
rows.groupReason: Subsection (3) has a distinct trigger (inadequate, improper, or hazardous method), broader operational scope, oral form confirmed in the daily drilling report, and a distinct resolution tied to adoption of approved methods.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the trigger, covered operation types, oral-and-note form, and resolution condition for the Minister's direction to discontinue a drilling, completion, suspension, abandonment, or production operation.

evidenceText: he may direct orally, confirmed by a note in the daily drilling report, that the operation be discontinued until methods approved by him are adopted

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsections (1) and (2) form one interdependent inquiry-based shutdown mechanism, while (3) operates on a distinct trigger, scope, form, and resolution warranting a separate recall task.

rows.heading: Power of Minister to close area
rows.groupTitle: Minister's area closure power and notice requirements
rows.groupReason: The closure power, its practicable-notice mechanism, and the mandatory advisory duty to the Minister of Transport of Canada form one interdependent recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the trigger (hazardous conditions in a field or at a well), the written-designation mechanism, the travel-permit prohibition, and the notice and advisory duties the Minister must observe when closing an area under section 42.

evidenceText: he may designate in writing the area to be closed prohibiting anyone from entering, travelling about, or remaining therein without a travel permit issued under his authority
the Minister shall advise an appropriate representative of the Minister of Transport of Canada of his action under this section

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 42 is a single, coherent emergency power: the Minister may close a hazardous area by written designation, with attached notice and advisory duties that are directly dependent on the closure act.

rows.heading: Power of Minister to do whatever is necessary, liability for cost of well control
rows.groupTitle: Minister's emergency entry and corrective-action power under s. 43(1)
rows.groupReason: Standalone operational power with its own trigger (non-compliance with a Ministerial direction) and scope (entry and any necessary corrective work).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the trigger condition, the actors who may exercise the power, and the scope of the Minister's entry and corrective-action authority under s. 43(1).

evidenceText: if in the opinion of the Minister, the control of a well or any completion, suspension, or abandonment is not in accordance with a direction, or requirement of the Minister, he, or any person duly authorized by him, shall have access to and may enter upon the well site or any structure thereon and do whatever the Minister deems necessary

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 43 contains two materially distinct recall tasks: the Minister's operational entry and corrective-action power (43(1)) and the security-deposit application and licensee cost-liability mechanism (43(2)–(4)). Different actors, different legal modalities, and independent exam questions support splitting.

rows.heading: Power of Minister to do whatever is necessary, liability for cost of well control
rows.groupTitle: Security deposit application and residual licensee liability for well control costs
rows.groupReason: Three interdependent financial rules (deposit application, no-relief on return, residual debt character) that together answer one recall question about the licensee's cost liability for well control work.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how the security deposit is applied to well control costs under s. 43(2), why its return does not reduce licensee liability under s. 43(3), and the legal character of any residual unpaid costs under s. 43(4).

evidenceText: The Minister of Finance and Treasury Board may use or expend all or any part of a security deposit furnished by the well licensee to defray the cost of, as determined by the Minister, or the cost incidental to the work of control, completion, suspension, or abandonment of the well
The return of the deposit or any part thereof, does not relieve the well licensee of liability for any cost of or the cost incidental to the control, completion, suspension or abandonment of a well

The cost incurred by the Minister under this section remaining unpaid after applying thereto the security deposit of the well licensee held by the Minister of Finance and Treasury Board is a debt payable by the well licensee to the Crown.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 43 contains two materially distinct recall tasks: the Minister's operational entry and corrective-action power (43(1)) and the security-deposit application and licensee cost-liability mechanism (43(2)–(4)). Different actors, different legal modalities, and independent exam questions support splitting.

rows.heading: Enforcement of direction, taking of possession, costs and expenses, net proceeds
rows.groupTitle: Costs, net proceeds, and security-deposit shortfall under section 44
rows.groupReason: Subsections (4) through (7) form a sequential financial mechanism: cost allocation by Ministerial discretion, payment from well proceeds, payment of net proceeds to the Court of King's Bench, and the shortfall backstop applying section 43 security-deposit provisions.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the Minister's discretion over costs, the permissible sources of payment from well proceeds, the destination of net proceeds, and how the section 43 security-deposit and liability provisions apply when proceeds are insufficient.

evidenceText: The costs and expenses of, and the costs and expenses incidental to, a proceeding taken by the Minister under this section are at the discretion of the Minister

The net proceeds of the oil and natural gas produced at the well remaining after the payment of the costs and expenses under subsection (5) shall be paid by the Minister into The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick

provisions of section 43 regarding the use of the security deposit and regarding the further liability of the well licensee with respect to the costs referred to in that section apply, mutatis mutandis

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 44 contains three materially distinct recall tasks: the Minister's enumerated enforcement powers, the legal effects of taking possession (duty to obey and Crown disposition of products), and the sequential financial mechanics of costs, net proceeds, and shortfall.

rows.heading: Enforcement of direction, taking of possession, costs and expenses, net proceeds
rows.groupTitle: Minister's enforcement powers under sections 42 and 43
rows.groupReason: Subsection (1) enumerates five distinct enforcement actions the Minister may take; recalling them as a set is a separate recall task from the downstream effects or financial rules.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Enumerate the specific actions the Minister may take to enforce a direction or requirement under sections 42 and 43, including possession, production control, plugging, and flow prevention.

evidenceText: forcibly or otherwise enter upon, seize, and take possession of any well, together with the whole or part of the movable and immovable property in, on, or about the well
either discontinue all production or take over the management and control of it
plug the well at any depth

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 44 contains three materially distinct recall tasks: the Minister's enumerated enforcement powers, the legal effects of taking possession (duty to obey and Crown disposition of products), and the sequential financial mechanics of costs, net proceeds, and shortfall.

rows.heading: Enforcement of direction, taking of possession, costs and expenses, net proceeds
rows.groupTitle: Duty to obey and Crown disposition of products during Minister's possession
rows.groupReason: Subsections (2) and (3) together state the immediate legal effects triggered by the Minister taking possession: a duty on licensee personnel and the Crown-property disposition of produced oil and gas.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the duty imposed on officers and employees of the well licensee during the Minister's possession and the Minister's power to deal with produced oil and natural gas as Crown property.

evidenceText: every officer and employee of the well licensee, his agent, or contractor shall obey the directions or requirements concerning the well given by the Minister
take, deal with, and dispose of all oil and natural gas produced at the well as if it were the property of the Crown, subject to the payment of the net proceeds

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 44 contains three materially distinct recall tasks: the Minister's enumerated enforcement powers, the legal effects of taking possession (duty to obey and Crown disposition of products), and the sequential financial mechanics of costs, net proceeds, and shortfall.

rows.heading: Savings
rows.groupTitle: Savings: remainder of licence or lease not invalidated by non-Crown inclusions
rows.groupReason: One operative savings rule protecting the remainder of a licence to search or lease when it includes non-Crown oil or natural gas; a single recallable validity concept.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the effect on the remainder of a licence to search or lease when it includes oil or natural gas that does not belong to or is not reserved to the Crown in right of the Province.

evidenceText: The inclusion in a licence to search or a lease of oil or natural gas that does not belong to or is not reserved to the Crown in right of the Province does not invalidate such licence to search or lease with respect to the remainder of the licence to search or lease.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 45 is a single, self-contained savings rule stating that inclusion of non-Crown oil or natural gas in a licence to search or lease does not invalidate the remainder. It has independent operative legal value as a validity-preserving rule for oil and gas instruments.

rows.heading: Unit agreement
rows.groupTitle: Minister's unitization agreement power and binding effect

rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the Minister's power to enter into a unitization agreement for the unitized operation of a field, pool, or any part thereof, and identify that the agreement is binding on all parties upon execution.

evidenceText: The Minister may enter into a unitization agreement for the unitized operation of a field or pool or any part thereof, and upon the execution of such agreement it is binding on all parties thereto.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 46 states a single ministerial power (unitization agreement), its scope (field, pool, or part thereof), and a binding legal effect, forming one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Notification of exploration work
rows.groupTitle: Notification requirement before exploratory work or production

rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the written-notification requirement that must be satisfied to the Minister before commencing exploratory work or production of oil or natural gas.

evidenceText: No person shall commence exploratory work or production of oil or natural gas until the person has notified the Minister in writing of the person's intention to do so.

rows.sourceMapReason: A single prohibition with one written-notification condition; the rule is self-contained and independently recallable as one legal duty.

rows.heading: Transfers and assignments

a copy of the instrument giving the security certified by an officer or employee of the bank to be a true copy.

rows.heading: Transfers and assignments

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 48 contains four distinct recall concepts: the transfer prohibition, the recording/effectiveness mechanism, bank-security registration, and valid self/co-holder transfers.

rows.heading: Transfers and assignments

rows.approximateLearningGoal: State what a licensee or lessee must not do without the Minister's approval regarding a licence to search or lease.

evidenceText: A licensee or lessee shall not assign, transfer, sublet or abandon the possession of the rights described in his licence to search or lease, or any part thereof without the approval of the Minister.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 48 contains four distinct recall concepts: the transfer prohibition, the recording/effectiveness mechanism, bank-security registration, and valid self/co-holder transfers.

rows.heading: Transfers and assignments

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 48 contains four distinct recall concepts: the transfer prohibition, the recording/effectiveness mechanism, bank-security registration, and valid self/co-holder transfers.

rows.heading: Confidential information
rows.groupTitle: Confidential information: public access and data restrictions
rows.groupReason: The three subsections form one access regime: general public inspection right, a confidential-data release restriction with designation and permission conditions, and a supremacy rule over RTIPPA.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which oil and natural gas title records are open to public inspection free of charge, what data the Minister may hold confidential and the conditions for its release, and that section 49 prevails over a conflicting provision of the Right to Information and Protection of Privacy Act.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 49 establishes a cohesive public-access and confidentiality regime in three interdependent parts (general inspection right, confidential-data release restriction, RTIPPA supremacy) that function as one recall unit.

rows.heading: Registration with Minister of address for service

rows.sourceMapReason: Single short duty provision imposing an address-for-service registration obligation on enumerated oil and gas stakeholders; one recallable concept.

rows.heading: Execution of licence to search and lease by Minister
rows.groupTitle: Execution and evidentiary effect of licences to search and leases
rows.groupReason: Covers the Minister's execution authority, the filing requirement, delivery of certified copies, and their court equivalence as one interdependent procedural mechanism.

evidenceText: The Practice Review Committee shall distribute a detailed list of possible course types, seminars, activities etc. to participating members.

Members required to participate in the program may recommend other courses, activities etc. to the Committee. These will be reviewed and, if deemed acceptable, will be included in the Mandatory Continuing Education Program.

rows.sourceMapReason: Short, self-contained procedural provision: the Committee's distribution duty and the member recommendation/inclusion process are interdependent parts of one recallable CE-program step.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18.1.7 states a single, simple institutional duty: the Association will maintain a current record of MCE points for each participating member. It creates a legal obligation but is narrowly administrative in scope, warranting one small StudyUnit.

rows.documentTitle: Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors Bylaws
rows.heading: Participating members shall report all MCE

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18.1.8 imposes a single clear annual reporting duty on participating members, specifying the instrument and deadline; it forms one recallable compliance concept.

rows.heading: The Practice Review Committee shall review

rows.sourceMapReason: Single-sentence governance duty assigning the Practice Review Committee an annual MCE Program review and report obligation to the Executive Council.

rows.documentTitle: Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors Bylaws

The Practice Review Committee shall review this request and make a recommendation to Council.

rows.sourceMapReason: A short, self-contained provision creating a member's right to apply for an MCE exemption, stating grounds, and fixing the PRC's review-and-recommend duty. All elements form one coherent procedural rule.

rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the consequence for a member who fails to comply with sections 18.1.2 and 18.1.8, and identify the two sections that qualify that consequence.
rows.sourceMapReason: Single operative rule stating the revocation consequence for continuing-education non-compliance, with two tightly interdependent carve-outs forming one recall concept.

rows.documentTitle: Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors Bylaws
rows.heading: Council, may, in its discretion and where

rows.heading: At least 30 days before revoking the right to

The means by which a member may apply to council for relief under 18.2.2

rows.sourceMapReason: One coherent procedural duty: the Secretary must deliver a 30-day notice with three specified contents before revoking a member's right to practice under section 18.2.1.

rows.heading: Requirement for Preparation of a Survey
