rows.groupTitle: Powers of the Chief Registrar of Deeds
rows.groupReason: All subsections state the supervisory, inspection, instruction, reporting, and seal powers of the Chief Registrar, with the limitation in (d) as an integral carve-out from the instruction power.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the specific powers vested in the Chief Registrar of Deeds (or a Service New Brunswick designee) over registry offices and state the limitation that a registrar need not follow instructions on matters of legal liability to the public or individuals.

evidenceText: make a personal inspection of the building in which any registry office is kept, and of the books, deeds, titles, and instruments in any registry office
the registrar is not bound to carry out instructions in reference to a matter involving a question of legal liability of the registrar to the public or to individuals

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 17 sets out a coherent set of oversight, inspection, and administrative powers of the Chief Registrar of Deeds, including a substantive limitation protecting the registrar from compelled instruction on legal-liability matters; the powers share one actor and one recall question.

rows.heading: Replacement of registrar by temporary officer
rows.groupTitle: Appointment of a temporary acting registrar
rows.groupReason: The triggers, the Chief Registrar's authorization duty, the acting registrar's recording and certification powers, and the temporal limit form one coherent contingency procedure.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions that trigger the Chief Registrar of Deeds to authorize a temporary acting registrar, the scope of that officer's recording and certification powers, and the duration of the appointment.

evidenceText: the Chief Registrar of Deeds shall authorize a suitable person to take possession thereof
such person may receive and record all instruments offered for registry, entering the same and certifying thereto in his own name as acting registrar
he shall continue so to act until order made to the contrary

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18 is a single, self-contained contingency procedure: it sets the triggers for vacancy or neglect, the Chief Registrar's mandatory duty to authorize a replacement, the acting registrar's limited recording powers, and the duration of that authority. All elements form one recallable procedural mechanism.

rows.heading: Registration of instruments
rows.groupTitle: Affidavit of transfer requirement and forwarding to assessment
rows.groupReason: Subsection (6) imposes a mandatory affidavit-of-transfer requirement with specified contents for deed registration, and (7) directs the registrar to forward (not record) the affidavit to the Executive Director of Assessment within thirty days; together they form one procedural requirement.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the contents and form of the affidavit of transfer required for registration of a deed, who must make it, and the registrar's duty to forward it to the Executive Director of Assessment.

evidenceText: No deed affecting the transfer of real property shall be registered unless accompanied by an affidavit of the transfer setting forth the true and actual consideration for which such property was acquired, the names of the parties, the location and description of real property and such other information prescribed by regulation

The registrar shall not record such affidavit but shall forward the same to the Executive Director of Assessment under the Assessment Act not later than thirty days after the date of registration of the deed

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19 contains four distinct recall tasks: the core registration rule with its two consequences and the lease exception; protective periods for official conveyances; the will registration period; and the affidavit-of-transfer requirement with its forwarding duty.

rows.heading: Registration of instruments
rows.groupTitle: Registration requirement, consequences of non-registration, and lease exception
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) state the general registration rule and its two distinct consequences (void against purchasers and against judgment creditors), while (3) carves out the short-lease exception; together they form the core registration requirement a learner must recall as one rule with its exception.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the registration requirement for instruments, the consequence of non-registration against subsequent purchasers for valuable consideration and against bona fide judgment creditors, and the conditions under which a short lease need not be registered.

evidenceText: if not so registered, shall, subject to the provisions of subsections (3), (4), (4.1) and (5), be deemed fraudulent and void against subsequent purchasers for valuable consideration whose conveyances are previously registered
No lease for a term not exceeding three years, where the actual possession goes along with the lease, need be registered

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19 contains four distinct recall tasks: the core registration rule with its two consequences and the lease exception; protective periods for official conveyances; the will registration period; and the affidavit-of-transfer requirement with its forwarding duty.

rows.heading: Registration of instruments
rows.groupTitle: Protective registration periods for official and sheriff's conveyances
rows.groupReason: Subsections (4) and (4.1) set a six-month protective registration period for conveyances executed in an official capacity (public auction) and for a sheriff's conveyance under the Enforcement of Money Judgments Act, respectively; (4.1) expressly extends (4) without limiting it.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the registration timeframes under which an official conveyance from a public auction and a sheriff's conveyance under the Enforcement of Money Judgments Act retain validity as if registered at the time of sale or execution.

evidenceText: the conveyance, if registered within six months of the day of such sale, shall, as against any subsequent purchaser or judgment creditor, be as valid as if registered at the time of sale

if a sheriff executes a conveyance of an interest in lands sold by the sheriff under the Enforcement of Money Judgments Act, the conveyance, if registered within six months after the day of its execution

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19 contains four distinct recall tasks: the core registration rule with its two consequences and the lease exception; protective periods for official conveyances; the will registration period; and the affidavit-of-transfer requirement with its forwarding duty.

rows.heading: Registration of instruments
rows.groupTitle: Protective registration period for wills
rows.groupReason: Subsection (5) sets a distinct location-based timeframe (six months in-province, one year out-of-province) for registering a will, applying the same validity-against-subsequent-parties effect as the official-conveyance periods but keyed to the testator's place of death.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the registration timeframes for a will depending on whether the testator died within or without the Province and the legal effect of registration within those periods.

evidenceText: A will registered within six months after the death of the testator if he died within the Province, or within one year after death if he died without the Province, shall as against subsequent purchasers or judgment creditors be as valid as if it had been registered immediately after the death of the testator

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19 contains four distinct recall tasks: the core registration rule with its two consequences and the lease exception; protective periods for official conveyances; the will registration period; and the affidavit-of-transfer requirement with its forwarding duty.

rows.heading: Instrument that may be submitted as a digitally scanned image
rows.groupTitle: Digital submission of instruments: permission, requirements, and who may submit
rows.groupReason: Covers the permission to submit digitally, the format and Service New Brunswick technology requirements, the identity-evidence duty, and the subscriber-only rule with the land surveyor exception for plans.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions under which an instrument may be filed or registered as a digitally scanned image, the format and technology requirements, the identity-evidence duty, and the limitation that only subscribers (or land surveyors with a Service New Brunswick agreement for plans of survey or subdivision plans) may submit such images.

evidenceText: all instruments that may be submitted to be filed or registered under this Act may be filed or registered by submitting a digitally scanned image of the instrument
shall be in a format that has been approved by the Chief Registrar of Deeds as being equivalent, when printed, in form and content to its counterpart prescribed by regulation
no person other than a subscriber shall submit a digitally scanned image of an instrument

A land surveyor who has entered into an agreement with Service New Brunswick may, in accordance with the agreement and this Act, submit a digitally scanned image of an instrument that is a plan of survey or a subdivision plan

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19.01 is a short, coherent provision governing digital submission of instruments: the permission and format/technology requirements, the identity-evidence duty, and the subscriber-only prohibition with the land surveyor exception. All five subsections operate on the single act of submitting a digitally scanned image, making one StudyUnit appropriate, though the prohibition/exception (s.4–5) could arguably stand as a separate recall task.

rows.heading: Authentication of digitally scanned image
rows.groupTitle: Authentication requirements for digitally scanned instruments
rows.groupReason: All four subsections together state the single authentication mechanism: the pre-submission requirement, the rule that authenticator and submitter may differ, the possession-and-completeness conditions, and the certification effect.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions a subscriber or land surveyor must meet to authenticate a digitally scanned image, the legal effect of that authentication as a certification, and the rule that the authenticator need not be the same person who submits the image.

evidenceText: A digitally scanned image of an instrument shall not be submitted by a subscriber or land surveyor for filing or registration unless the digitally scanned image has been authenticated in the manner established by Service New Brunswick.
A subscriber or a land surveyor shall not authenticate a digitally scanned image of an instrument unless
The authentication by a subscriber or land surveyor under subsection (3) is a certification by the subscriber or land surveyor that

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19.02 is a short, self-contained provision governing the authentication of digitally scanned images for filing or registration. Subsections (1)–(4) form one interdependent mechanism: the submission requirement, a clarifying rule that authenticator and submitter may differ, the conditions for authentication, and the certification character of the authentication. Splitting would fragment a single authentication concept.

rows.heading: Authorization to submit digitally scanned image
rows.groupTitle: Certification of authorization on digital submission
rows.groupReason: The provision assigns a specific legal characterisation (certification of authorization) to a specific act (submission to a registry office) by specific actors (subscriber or land surveyor).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that submitting a digitally scanned image to a registry office is a certification by the subscriber or land surveyor that he or she is authorized to submit it for registration or filing.

evidenceText: The submission of a digitally scanned image of an instrument by a subscriber or land surveyor to a registry office is a certification by the subscriber or land surveyor that he or she is authorized to submit the digitally scanned image of the instrument for registration or filing.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19.03 is a single, self-contained rule: it states that submitting a digitally scanned image to a registry office operates as a certification of the submitter's authorization. One actor set, one trigger, one legal effect — one recall task.

rows.heading: Effect of digitally scanned image of an instrument
rows.groupTitle: Legal effect of digitally scanned instrument
rows.groupReason: One unified rule: the image is exempt from writing and signature requirements and has the same legal effect as a traditional instrument.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the legal effect a digitally scanned image of an instrument has when received at a registry office, including the writing and signature requirements from which it is exempt and the overriding effect it has over other Acts and rules of law.

evidenceText: a digitally scanned image of an instrument that is received at a registry office is not required to be in writing or to be signed by the parties and has the same effect for all purposes as an instrument that is in writing and is signed by the parties

rows.sourceMapReason: Single self-contained rule establishing the legal effect of a digitally scanned image received at a registry office.

rows.heading: Subscriber or land surveyor agreement
rows.groupTitle: Digital submission agreement with Service New Brunswick
rows.groupReason: All three subsections establish one coherent access framework: the individual agreement and its required contents, plus the parallel professional-body prerequisite for both lawyers and land surveyors.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State what agreement a subscriber or land surveyor must enter into with Service New Brunswick to submit a digitally scanned image of an instrument, the three purposes that agreement must serve, and the institutional prerequisite (professional-body agreement covering eligibility certification and access revocation) that must exist before Service New Brunswick will enter into the individual agreement.

evidenceText: A member of the Law Society of New Brunswick or a land surveyor who wishes to submit a digitally scanned image of an instrument to a registry office shall enter into an agreement with Service New Brunswick

Service New Brunswick shall not enter into an agreement under subsection (1) with a member of the Law Society of New Brunswick unless there is in place an agreement between the Law Society of New Brunswick and Service New Brunswick

Service New Brunswick shall not enter into an agreement under subsection (1) with a land surveyor unless there is in place an agreement between the Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors and Service New Brunswick

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19.05 is a compact, self-contained mechanism: the individual's duty to contract with Service New Brunswick (s.1) and the institutional prerequisite for Service New Brunswick to do so (ss.2–3) are tightly interdependent and form one recallable framework for digital submission access.

rows.heading: Effect of registration in the Personal Property Registry
rows.groupTitle: Effect of PPR registration on registered-land dealings
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) together state one rule: PPR registrations do not affect registered-land dealings and knowledge is not fraud evidence under s.19(1).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the effect of a Personal Property Registry registration on dealings with registered land, including the s.49 PPSA saving and the s.19(1) fraud-evidence rule.
rows.sourceMapReason: Both subsections state one coherent rule that PPR registrations do not affect dealings with registered land, and they are tightly interdependent.

rows.heading: Contents of conveyance respecting intestacy
rows.groupTitle: Required contents of conveyance following intestacy
rows.groupReason: The provision sets out what an instrument must state when the grantor acquired the interest by devise or operation of law upon intestacy; the three particulars form one content requirement.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the particulars that a conveyance must include when the grantor acquired the affected interest by devise or operation of law upon intestacy, including the condition that date and place of decease need only be stated if known.

evidenceText: shall state the name of the person from whom the interest has devolved, together with the date and place of decease of such person, if known

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 20 imposes a single, self-contained content requirement on instruments where the grantor's interest arose by intestacy; the three required particulars answer one recall task and form one coherent unit.

rows.heading: Offences and penalty respecting false affidavit
rows.groupTitle: Offence of false affidavit in registration (s. 21)
rows.groupReason: Single prohibition with a defined penalty category; one independently recallable legal rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the offence created by s. 21 (knowing false statement in a s. 19 affidavit), the triggering condition, and the applicable penalty category under the Provincial Offences Procedure Act.

evidenceText: knowingly states anything false in the affidavit commits an offence punishable under Part II of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act as a category F offence

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 21 is a single, self-contained offence provision creating a category F penalty for knowingly making a false affidavit required under section 19. One recall task; no split or combine warranted.

rows.heading: Enlargement of time for registration of will
rows.groupTitle: Concealment or suppression of will – purchaser protection
rows.groupReason: Separate rule with a different actor (purchaser for valuable consideration), trigger (concealment or suppression), and deadline (three years after death) from the enlargement mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a purchaser for valuable consideration is protected from a concealed or suppressed will that is not registered within three years after the testator's death.

evidenceText: if there is any concealment or suppression of a will, no purchaser for a valuable consideration shall be disturbed or defeated by the will, unless it is registered within three years after the testator's death

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 22 contains two rules with different actors, triggers, and deadlines: the enlargement mechanism for the interested person and a separate concealment/suppression protection for purchasers for valuable consideration. Each supports an independent recall task.

rows.heading: Enlargement of time for registration of will
rows.groupTitle: Enlargement of time for will registration
rows.groupReason: Covers the conditions (unfaulted inability, memorial requirement), provincial and extra-provincial memorial timeframes, and the extended registration deadline.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the conditions, memorial timeframes (six months in-province / one year extra-provincial), and the six-month post-obtaining registration deadline that make a late will registration sufficient under the Act.

evidenceText: unable without his fault to exhibit the same for registry within the time before limited, and a memorial of such contest or cause is entered in the registry office within the space of six months after the decease of the testator if he died within the Province, or within the space of one year after his decease if he died without the Province
the registry of such will within the space of six months after obtaining the will or probate thereof or the removal of such cause shall be a sufficient registry within the meaning of this Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 22 contains two rules with different actors, triggers, and deadlines: the enlargement mechanism for the interested person and a separate concealment/suppression protection for purchasers for valuable consideration. Each supports an independent recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of will in extra-provincial court, registration of notarial will
rows.groupTitle: Registration of extra-provincial will and no-probate affidavits
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) form an interdependent rule-and-condition pair defining acceptable documents, authentication, evidentiary effect, registration, and the additional witness/death affidavits required when no probate was granted.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the acceptable documents, required authentication, and additional affidavits (witness proof of execution and death of testator) for registering an extra-provincial will in a New Brunswick registry office.

evidenceText: a certified copy thereof, the probate of such will, or any letters of administration with the will annexed, purporting to be under the hand of the officer having the custody of the records of the court in which the original will was deposited and of the seal of the said court

Where a will referred to in subsection (1) has not been granted probate there shall be registered with the certified copy thereof an affidavit sworn by one of the witnesses to the will, either within or without the Province, proving the due execution thereof by the testator, together with an affidavit of the death of the testator.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 23 contains two distinct registration regimes: subsections (1)–(2) govern general extra-provincial wills (with a no-probate condition), while subsection (3) creates a separate procedure for notarial wills from Quebec or South Africa with different document and affidavit requirements.

rows.heading: Registration of will in extra-provincial court, registration of notarial will
rows.groupTitle: Registration of notarial wills from Quebec or South Africa
rows.groupReason: Subsection (3) creates a separate registration pathway for notarial wills from specific jurisdictions with its own document, affidavit, and authentication requirements distinct from the general extra-provincial will procedure.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the document and affidavit requirements, including the officer's affidavit of validity and the affidavit of death, for registering a notarial will executed under the laws of Quebec or South Africa in a New Brunswick registry office.

evidenceText: Where a will is a notarial will under the laws of the Province of Quebec or of South Africa, a notarial certified copy thereof with an affidavit of the officer, with whom such will is deposited, that such will is a valid and subsisting will under the laws of the province or country where the same was executed

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 23 contains two distinct registration regimes: subsections (1)–(2) govern general extra-provincial wills (with a no-probate condition), while subsection (3) creates a separate procedure for notarial wills from Quebec or South Africa with different document and affidavit requirements.

rows.heading: Registration of will probated in British Dominion
rows.groupTitle: Registration of a will probated in a British Dominion court
rows.groupReason: Documents required (Master in Chancery hand, court seal, Chief Justice certificate), the registration step, and the resulting legal effect are one interdependent mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the evidentiary requirements for registering a will probated in a British Dominion court and the legal effect of such registration in the registry office.

evidenceText: a copy of such will purporting to be under the hand of a Master in Chancery, or other officer of the court in which such will was proved and registered, and purporting to be authenticated by the seal of the court

may be registered in the registry office for any county of the Province as other conveyances are registered, and the same when so registered, shall have the same effect as if the original will had been registered therein

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 24 is a self-contained mechanism for registering a will probated in a British Dominion court: evidentiary requirements, registration permission, and legal effects form one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of unprobated will
rows.groupTitle: Delivery of a registered unprobated will for probate
rows.groupReason: Governs the registrar's duty to deliver the original will to a judge of probate upon a directed order, including the prior substitution of a certified examined copy and the filing requirements.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State what the registrar of deeds must do upon service of a judge of probate's order directing delivery of a registered unprobated will, including the substitution of an examined copy and what is retained on file.

evidenceText: the registrar of deeds, upon service on him of an order of a judge of probate having jurisdiction over the estate of the testator directing him to do so, shall deliver the original will to the judge of probate for the purpose of having the same probated

the registrar shall first substitute on the files in his office an examined copy of said will, certified as such by said registrar, and he shall retain and keep on file the examined copy of the will, together with the affidavits filed under this section, and the order of the judge of probate

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 25 contains two distinct procedural stages with different actors and triggers: the registration requirements (25(1)) and the delivery/substitution procedure when probate is later sought (25(2)). Section 25(3) is repealed.

rows.heading: Registration of unprobated will
rows.groupTitle: Registration requirements for an unprobated will
rows.groupReason: Sets the specific documentary requirements (original will, witness affidavit, death affidavit, or certified copy from another office) and the subsection 23(1)-(2) override for registering an unprobated will.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the documents required to register an unprobated will, including the witness affidavit, death affidavit, and the alternative certified-copy route when the will is already deposited in another registry office.

evidenceText: a will, probate of which has not been granted, may be registered by the deposit of the original will, with an affidavit sworn to by one of the witnesses to the will, either within or without the Province, proving the due execution thereof by the testator, together with an affidavit of the death of the testator
Subject to subsections 23(1) and (2)

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 25 contains two distinct procedural stages with different actors and triggers: the registration requirements (25(1)) and the delivery/substitution procedure when probate is later sought (25(2)). Section 25(3) is repealed.

rows.heading: Registration of probated will, registration of sealed will
rows.groupTitle: Registration of probated and sealed will documents without further proof
rows.groupReason: Covers the two registration paths—locally proved wills and foreign probate documents sealed under s. 73 of the Probate Court Act—as one registration-without-further-proof mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify which probate-related documents may be registered in a county registry office without further proof under s. 26(1) and 26(2), and state the sealing requirement for foreign probate documents under section 73 of the Probate Court Act.
rows.sourceMapReason: Both subsections apply the same registration mechanism—register without further proof, with the same effect as original registration—to locally proved wills and to foreign probate documents sealed by The Probate Court of New Brunswick.

rows.heading: Registration of foreign decree
rows.groupTitle: Registration of foreign decree – conditions and proof
rows.groupReason: The permission, the seal-or-judge-signature condition, and the affidavit or affirmation proof are one interdependent registration rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions an authenticated or certified copy of a foreign decree must satisfy (Court seal or judge's signature with no-seal certification) and the affidavit or affirmation proof before a section 47 authorized person required for registration in the registry office.

evidenceText: may be registered in the registry office for the county in which such lands are situate if the authenticated or certified copy of such decree, decretal or other order purports to be under the seal of the Court making the same
such seal, or the signature of such judge, shall be proved by affidavit or affirmation before an official or person authorized by section 47

rows.sourceMapReason: The section states a self-contained permission to register foreign decrees affecting NB land, with tightly interdependent conditions on the copy and a proof requirement, forming one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of corporate documents
rows.groupTitle: Registration of certified copies of corporate documents
rows.groupReason: One concept: which corporate documents qualify, the required certification, where they may be registered, and their legal effect upon registration.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State which corporate documents may be registered as certified copies, the required certification, the registration venue, and the legal effect of such registration under section 28 of the Registry Act.

evidenceText: A copy of letters patent, supplementary letters patent or other document of incorporation, amalgamation or change of name, certified as a true copy by the person having custody of the records of the agency issuing the original thereof, may be registered in the registry office for any county, and when registered shall have the same effect, as if the original document had been registered therein.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 28 is a single, self-contained registration rule: it permits registration of certified copies of corporate documents, sets the certification prerequisite, and states the resulting legal effect. One recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of notice of sale under mortgage
rows.groupTitle: Permissive registration of mortgage sale notices
rows.groupReason: One permissive registration right with its triggering conditions (mortgage power of sale on default with required notice, or Property Act notice) and venue (county registry office, at full length, subject to s. 30).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which a notice of sale under a mortgage may be registered, the required form (full length), the correct registry office, and the applicable section 30 condition.

evidenceText: any such notice given as provided in and by any such mortgage, or under the Property Act, may, subject to section 30, be registered at full length in the registry office for the county in which the property covered by the mortgage is situate.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 29 is a single permissive registration rule: it defines the conditions under which a mortgage sale notice may be registered and the venue, forming one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Proof of signature and notice
rows.groupTitle: Proof requirements for registering a notice of sale
rows.groupReason: All four subsections together state the complete proof procedure: signature acknowledged/proved, oath of giving/publishing, POA recording, corporate-seal sufficiency, and which official may take the proof.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two matters that must be proved before a notice of sale may be registered, the additional recording step where a power of attorney is used, the sufficient proof for corporate execution, and the flexibility as to before which official the proofs may be taken.

evidenceText: the signature of the person authorized under the provisions of the mortgage, or by the Property Act, to give or publish such notice shall be acknowledged or proved before a person authorized to take proofs or acknowledgments of deeds under this Act
Where the notice is given by an agent acting under power of attorney, the power of attorney also must be recorded.

proof of the corporate seal and that the same was affixed by an officer of the corporation thereunto authorized by the board of directors or other lawful authority, and of the signature of such officer, shall in all cases be sufficient.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 30 is one coherent procedural mechanism: the proof requirements that must be satisfied before a notice of sale under mortgage may be registered. Subsections 30(1)–(4) are interdependent conditions and variations of the same proof rule and do not warrant separate recall units.

rows.heading: Duty of registrar respecting notice of sale
rows.groupTitle: Registrar's duty and evidentiary effect for registered sale notices
rows.groupReason: Both subsections state the registrar's handling duty for a properly proved section 29 notice and the evidentiary consequences of registration, forming one recall unit on how sale notices are processed and proven.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the registrar's duty when a duly proved section 29 notice of sale is produced, the evidentiary effect of the registrar's certificate in courts, and the applicability of section 85 of the Evidence Act to notices registered under sections 29 and 30.

evidenceText: the registrar shall deal therewith in all respects as provided in section 51, and the certificate that the registrar shall put on any such notice and proof, as provided for in said section 51, shall be taken and allowed as evidence of the registry of such notice and proof thereon in all courts
The provisions of section 85 of the Evidence Act are applicable to any notice or proof thereof, registered under the provisions of sections 29 and 30

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 31 is a short, self-contained operative provision imposing a specific duty on the registrar to process a section 29 notice per section 51 and establishing the evidentiary effect of the resulting certificate; the two subsections address one coherent concept and form a single recall task.

rows.heading: Filing of notice of sale
rows.groupTitle: Filing of notice of sale in lieu of full registration
rows.groupReason: One coherent filing procedure with a single actor (the registrar) performing indexing, certification, and ordering steps as part of the alternative to full registration under sections 29–31.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the registrar must file (not register at full length) a notice of sale at the requester's direction, index the names of the giver and recipients, certify the day, hour, and minute of filing, and enter the notice in order of receipt with other instruments.

evidenceText: the registrar, at the request of the person offering such notice of sale, affidavits and other proof for registration, shall file the same in his office instead of registering the same at full length
enter in the index the name of the person giving the notice, and the names of the persons to whom such notice was given, and enter a certificate upon such notice of the day, hour and minute of filing

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 32 is a single procedural rule: at the request of the person offering a notice of sale, the registrar files rather than registers at full length, with specific indexing, certification, and ordering steps that all belong to that one filing act.

rows.heading: Registering lien or certificate under the Construction Remedies Act
rows.groupTitle: Registration of Construction Remedies Act liens and certificates
rows.groupReason: Both subsections state one coherent rule: the registration pathway differs from the Registry Act's but the legal effect is the same.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the registration procedure for a Construction Remedies Act lien or certificate and identify its legal effect relative to Registry Act registration.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 33 is a short, self-contained carve-out: Construction Remedies Act liens or certificates are registered per that Act (s.33(1)) and carry the same effect as Registry Act registration (s.33(2)). Both subsections are tightly interdependent and form one recallable rule about a specific registration pathway and its effect.

rows.heading: Effect of registration of conveyance
rows.groupTitle: Effect of registration of conveyance
rows.groupReason: One rule defining what registration accomplishes (transfer of land and possession) and what it dispenses with (livery of seisin or any other act).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the legal effect of registering a duly acknowledged or proved conveyance and identify the act that registration dispenses with.

evidenceText: shall be effectual for the transferring of the land therein described and the possession thereof, according to the intent of such conveyance without livery of seisin or any other act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 34 is a single, self-contained rule stating the legal effect of registering a conveyance: it transfers land and possession and dispenses with livery of seisin or any other act.

rows.heading: Registration of copy
rows.groupTitle: Registration of Certified Copy in Another Registry Office
rows.groupReason: One permission, its two conditions (registrar certification; acknowledgment taken before an authorized person in the destination office), and its legal effect are inseparably linked for recall.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which a certified copy of a duly registered instrument may be registered in another registry office and the effect that registration has.
rows.sourceMapReason: Single procedural rule on registering a certified copy in another registry office, with tightly linked conditions and effect forming one recall unit.

rows.heading: Affidavit of execution or acknowledgment
rows.groupTitle: Prohibitions on parties and witness requirement for affidavits of execution
rows.groupReason: Parties cannot witness or acknowledge another party's execution, and a witness must have subscribed their hand signature before proof is taken; both rules are interdependent parts of one execution-integrity concept.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two things a party to an instrument is prohibited from doing in the execution/acknowledgment process and the prerequisite a witness must satisfy before their affidavit or proof of execution may be taken.

evidenceText: No party to an instrument shall (a) witness the execution of the instrument by another party, or (b) take an affidavit or acknowledgment of the execution of the instrument.
No affidavit or proof of the execution of an instrument shall be taken from a witness unless the witness has subscribed his signature to the instrument by hand as a witness to its due execution.

rows.sourceMapReason: Short section with interdependent prohibitions on parties and a witness-subscription requirement forming one coherent execution-and-acknowledgment rule.

rows.heading: Proof of execution
rows.groupTitle: Forms of proof of execution by a subscribing witness and registrar acceptance
rows.groupReason: The provision sets one coherent rule: acceptable proof forms (oath, affidavit, affirmation, or declaration per the law of the proving country) and the registrar's power to accept without further proof when the foreign-law statement is included.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the permissible forms of proof of execution by a subscribing witness and the condition under which the registrar may receive an instrument without further proof of due execution.

evidenceText: such proof may be made either by oath or affidavit, or by affirmation or declaration when by the law of the country where such proof is made an affirmation or declaration is allowed instead of an oath or affidavit

the registrar may receive such instrument so proved without any other or further proof of the due execution, if it be stated in such proof that, by the law of the country where the same is made, proof by affirmation or declaration is allowed instead of by oath or affidavit

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 37 is a single, self-contained rule on the permissible forms of proof of execution by a subscribing witness and the registrar's corresponding acceptance standard; no internal split is warranted.

rows.heading: Sufficiency of name in affidavit
rows.groupTitle: Sufficiency of abbreviated witness names in affidavit
rows.groupReason: One independent registration permission: abbreviated Christian names in the affidavit do not bar registration.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the condition under which an instrument may still be registered when the subscribing witness's Christian names appear in the affidavit only by initial letters or abbreviation.

evidenceText: Any instrument may be registered under this Act notwithstanding the Christian names of the subscribing witness making the affidavit are only set forth in the affidavit by initial letters or by abbreviation and not in full.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single-sentence permission rule: an instrument may be registered when the subscribing witness's Christian names appear only by initials or abbreviation in the affidavit.

rows.heading: Error or omission in affidavit of execution
rows.groupTitle: Effect of affidavit errors on registration validity
rows.groupReason: One rule with two directly dependent limitations (registrar's proof duty preserved; prior court adjudication excluded) that together form a single recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify which affidavit errors do not void registration and state the two exceptions that preserve the registrar's duty and prior court decisions.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 39 states one interdependent rule: specified affidavit defects do not void registration, subject to the registrar's continuing proof duty and prior court adjudications. The three clauses are tightly coupled and fragment if recalled separately.

rows.heading: Compellability of witness
rows.groupTitle: Compellability of subscribing witness to prove execution
rows.groupReason: One provision, one rule: the witness, the court order mechanism, the exception for incompetent witnesses, and the registration purpose form a single recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State who may be compelled to prove execution of an instrument, by what court order, the exception for incompetent witnesses, and the purpose for which compellability applies under the Registry Act.

evidenceText: Every subscribing witness, except such as may be an incompetent witness by this Act, shall be compellable, when necessary by order of a judge of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick, to make affidavit or proof of the execution of any instrument for the purpose of registration under this Act.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 40 is a single short provision establishing one rule: a subscribing witness may be compelled by court order to prove execution of an instrument for registration. It forms one coherent recall concept with no internal split.

rows.heading: Certificate of proof of instrument
rows.groupTitle: Certificate of proof of instrument (unavailable witness)
rows.groupReason: Trigger conditions, the judicial proof procedure, the endorsed-and-sealed certificate requirement, and the registrar's duty to register all belong to one alternative proof mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions that trigger alternative proof of execution, the required judicial procedure and certificate form, and the registrar's registration duty when the subscribing witness is dead, of unsound mind, or without the Province with unknown residence.

evidenceText: Where the witness to an instrument is dead, or has become insane, idiotic, imbecile or of unsound mind or understanding

may make proof viva voce or by affidavit, as the judge may require, before a judge of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick, or a judge of any superior court of record in any other province of Canada
the registrar shall register such instrument and certificate, if the certificate is sealed with the seal of the court to which the judge belongs

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 41 is a single integrated procedure for proving execution when the subscribing witness is unavailable; trigger conditions, judicial proof method, certificate requirements, and the registrar's registration duty form one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Proof of signature or seal
rows.groupTitle: No separate verification of seal or signing officer required for registration
rows.groupReason: One recall task: identify when no separate seal or signature/office verification is needed, the sealing-and-certification condition, and the Act-specific exception.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the circumstances under which no proof verifying the seal or the signature and office of the person before whom an acknowledgment or affidavit is made is required for registration under the Registry Act.

evidenceText: It is not necessary for the purpose of registration that there be any proof verifying the seal affixed to any acknowledgment, affidavit or other proof except where it may be otherwise required by this Act

nor is it necessary, except as otherwise required by this Act, to verify the signature or office of any person before whom such acknowledgment or affidavit is made, if the same purports to be sealed and certified by the proper officer as required

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 42 is a short, self-contained procedural rule stating what evidentiary verification is not required for registration of acknowledgments and affidavits. The two clauses (seal verification, signature/office verification) share the same condition and exception, forming one recall task.

rows.heading: Seal of court of record, seal of corporation
rows.groupTitle: Sufficient evidence of due execution: court and corporate seals
rows.groupReason: Covers the evidentiary sufficiency rules for court and corporate seals in registration and the sheriff's-conveyance exception.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the evidentiary requirements for a court-sealed instrument (seal alone suffices) and a corporate-sealed instrument (seal, officer signature, and affidavit content) to constitute sufficient evidence of due execution for registration, and identify the sheriff's-conveyance carve-out.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 43 establishes parallel evidentiary rules for court-sealed and corporate-sealed instruments in registration, plus a narrow sheriff's-conveyance carve-out, forming one coherent evidence-of-execution concept.

rows.heading: Execution of instruments
rows.groupTitle: In-Province Instrument Execution, Authorized Persons, and Fees
rows.groupReason: The core two-method execution rule, the in-province authorized persons for acknowledgment and proof, and the in-province fee provision form one coherent domestic practice unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two methods of executing an instrument before registry, identify the persons authorized to take in-province acknowledgments and proofs, and note that the in-province fee is prescribed by regulation.

evidenceText: Before the registry of any instrument, the execution of the same shall either be acknowledged by the person executing the same, or be proved by the oath of a subscribing witness
if the execution of an instrument is acknowledged in this Province, the acknowledgment may be taken before and by

if the execution of an instrument is proved in the Province such proof may be taken before and by any of the persons enumerated in paragraph (a) or before and by a Commissioner for taking affidavits to be read in the Supreme Court
The fee for taking and certifying acknowledgments or proof, as the case may be, within the Province is that prescribed by regulation

rows.sourceMapReason: The section establishes one execution framework but applies it through materially different actor lists and certification requirements for in-province versus out-of-province scenarios, creating distinct recall tasks.

rows.heading: Execution of instruments
rows.groupTitle: Out-of-Province Instrument Execution and Certification
rows.groupReason: The out-of-province actor lists involve distinct inter-jurisdictional and international officials with separate certification and authentication requirements, forming an independently recallable unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the persons authorized to take out-of-province acknowledgments and proofs of instrument execution and the associated certification or authentication requirements for each category.

evidenceText: if the execution of an instrument is acknowledged out of the Province, the acknowledgment may be taken before and by
if the execution of an instrument is proved out of the Province such proof may be taken before and by

the handwriting and certificate of any such Judge or Lord of Session being authenticated under the seal of a notary public, and the taking of any such acknowledgment before such Minister, Ambassador, Consul, Vice-Consul, Acting Consul, Pro-Consul, Consular Agent or Governor being certified respectively under his hand and seal of office

rows.sourceMapReason: The section establishes one execution framework but applies it through materially different actor lists and certification requirements for in-province versus out-of-province scenarios, creating distinct recall tasks.

rows.heading: Registrar and deputy registrar ex officio commissioner of oaths
rows.groupTitle: Registrar and deputy registrar as ex officio commissioners
rows.groupReason: One short provision creating a specific official power; no internal structure to split.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify that every registrar and deputy registrar is ex officio a Commissioner for Taking Affidavits to be read in The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick.

evidenceText: Every registrar and deputy registrar is ex officio a Commissioner for Taking Affidavits to be read in The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single operative sentence granting every registrar and deputy registrar ex officio commissioner status for The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick; one self-contained recall task.

rows.heading: Certificate of development officer
rows.groupTitle: Development officer certification requirement and exceptions
rows.groupReason: The certification rule, plan extension, seven enumerated exceptions, and registrar uncertainty duty form one interdependent registration precondition a learner must recall as a complete rule set.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State when a development officer certification is required before registration of an instrument or annexed plan in a subdivision area, identify the seven exceptions, and describe the registrar's duty when certification status is uncertain.

evidenceText: No instrument that transfers an interest in land in an area to which a subdivision by-law or regulation applies shall be registered until it has been certified by a development officer pursuant to section 77 of the Community Planning Act.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the registration of
Where a registrar is uncertain whether an instrument that has not been certified as mentioned in subsection (1) is subject to that subsection, he shall not register it until it has been so certified.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 46 states the development officer certification requirement for subdivision-area instruments, extends it to annexed plans, lists seven exceptions, and imposes a registrar uncertainty duty — a coherent rule/exception/procedure structure best studied as one unit.

rows.heading: Persons before whom proof of execution made
rows.groupTitle: Persons Before Whom Out-of-Province Proof of Execution May Be Made (s. 47)
rows.groupReason: Cross-references s.44 persons for out-of-Province affidavits, oaths, declarations, or affirmations proving execution of powers of attorney, wills, or probates for registry.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the persons authorized under section 44 before whom an out-of-Province affidavit, oath, declaration, or affirmation proving execution of a power of attorney, will, or probate may be made for registry in New Brunswick.

evidenceText: Any affidavit, oath, declaration or affirmation made without the Province, proving the execution of any power of attorney, will or probate, copy or memorial thereof, for the purpose of registry in this Province, may be made before any person authorized by section 44 to take proof of conveyances without the Province.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single procedural rule extending the s.44 out-of-Province proof-of-execution authorization to powers of attorney, wills, and probates for registry; one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of Crown grant
rows.groupTitle: Registration of Crown Grants – Simplified Evidentiary Requirements
rows.groupReason: The fee-payment condition and the evidentiary exemptions form one interdependent recall task for Crown-grant registration.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the registration condition and the evidentiary exemptions that apply when registering a Crown grant from the Province of New Brunswick or Canada.

evidenceText: grants from the Crown as representing the Province of New Brunswick, and grants from the Crown as representing Canada may be registered without proof of the seal of the Province or of Canada or the signature, or official position, or authority of the persons purporting to act on behalf of the Crown

rows.sourceMapReason: One short provision stating a single permission: Crown grants are registrable without proof of seal, signature, position, or authority upon payment of fees.

rows.heading: Certificate of cancellation of Crown grant
rows.groupTitle: Certificate of cancellation of Crown grant
rows.groupReason: Both subsections describe one mechanism: the Minister's duty to record a legislative cancellation, the registration trigger for its effect, the legislative-override exception, and the no-proof-of-signature registration rule for the certificate.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister of Natural Resources' recording duty, the rule that a Crown grant cancellation has no effect until the certificate is registered in the appropriate county registry office (unless an Act provides otherwise), and that the certificate may be registered without proof of the Minister's signature or official position.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 49 states a coherent mechanism for Crown grant cancellation: the Minister's recording duty, the rule that cancellation has no effect until the certificate is registered (with a legislative-override exception), and a registration simplification for the certificate. All pieces are interdependent and form one recallable concept.

rows.heading: Registration of original instrument, annexed plan, instrument conveying parcel
rows.groupTitle: Production and form of instruments for registration
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1), (2), and (3) together state what must be produced, the multi-part endorsement procedure with evidentiary effect, and the full-length completeness requirement for registration.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the production requirement for original instruments (including multi-part instruments), the registrar's endorsement duty and evidentiary effect for additional original parts, and the full-length registration requirement.

evidenceText: all instruments that may be registered under this Act shall be registered upon the production to the registrar of the original instrument, when but one is executed; or, when such instrument is in two or more original parts, upon the production of one such part
every instrument shall be registered at full length, including every certificate of acknowledgment, or proof, and affidavit, required by this Act for the registry of the same

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 50 contains four distinct recall tasks: basic instrument production and form, the abbreviated judgment/decree mechanism, general annexed-plan filing, and subdivision-plan filing with the parcel-adding condition.

rows.heading: Registration of original instrument, annexed plan, instrument conveying parcel
rows.groupTitle: Abbreviated judgments and decrees
rows.groupReason: Subsection (3.1) creates a distinct registrar refusal power and specifies the content and certification requirements for an abbreviated judgment or decree.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the registrar may refuse a judgment or decree for registration and state the two requirements the abbreviated judgment or decree must meet.

evidenceText: the registrar may refuse to register the judgment or decree and require the person to present an abbreviated judgment or decree that (a) omits the provisions that do not affect an interest in or title to land or require the payment of money, and (b) is certified under the seal of the court that issued the judgment or decree

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 50 contains four distinct recall tasks: basic instrument production and form, the abbreviated judgment/decree mechanism, general annexed-plan filing, and subdivision-plan filing with the parcel-adding condition.

rows.heading: Registration of original instrument, annexed plan, instrument conveying parcel
rows.groupTitle: Filing of plans annexed to instruments
rows.groupReason: Subsections (4), (6), and (7) form a rule/exception/duty-source structure governing when and how copies of annexed plans must be delivered and numbered.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the plan-copy delivery and numbering requirement, the exception where the plan is already on file, and the obligation on the grantor to furnish plan copies.

evidenceText: no instrument tendered the registrar for registration, to which there is annexed any plan, shall be received by the registrar for registration unless there is delivered to the registrar to be filed by him, a copy of any and all plans annexed to such instrument
Where the reference in a deed is to a plan already on file in the registry office, it is not necessary to deliver to the registrar another copy of said plan
it shall be furnished by the grantor on delivery of the instrument to the grantee

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 50 contains four distinct recall tasks: basic instrument production and form, the abbreviated judgment/decree mechanism, general annexed-plan filing, and subdivision-plan filing with the parcel-adding condition.

rows.heading: Registration of original instrument, annexed plan, instrument conveying parcel
rows.groupTitle: Subdivision plan filing and parcel-adding condition
rows.groupReason: Subsections (5) and (8) set the approval prerequisites for filing subdivision plans and the specific condition applying when a parcel is created to be added to an adjoining parcel.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the approval stamps or certificates required before the registrar will file a subdivision plan, and the additional requirement where the plan shows a parcel created for addition to an adjoining parcel.

evidenceText: the registrar shall file any plan for the subdivision of land to which a subdivision by-law or regulation applies, whether annexed to an instrument or not, if it bears the stamp or certificate or approval of (a) a development officer under the Community Planning Act, and (b) the Director of Surveys if the land is in an integrated survey area constituted under the Surveys Act

the registrar shall not accept the plan for filing unless the plan is accompanied by an instrument accepted by the registrar for registration which conveys the parcel so created to the owner of the adjoining parcel as shown on the plan

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 50 contains four distinct recall tasks: basic instrument production and form, the abbreviated judgment/decree mechanism, general annexed-plan filing, and subdivision-plan filing with the parcel-adding condition.

rows.heading: Certificate of registrar
rows.groupTitle: Registrar's certificate: endorsement requirements and evidentiary effect
rows.groupReason: Covers the registrar's duty to endorse the registry number and time of receipt, the deeming rule that the instrument is registered as of that time, and the prima facie evidentiary effect in all courts including the no-proof rule for the registrar's signature or office.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the registrar must endorse on a registered instrument (registry number, date and time, prescribed form) and the legal effect of that endorsement: the instrument is deemed registered as of the stated time and the certificate is prima facie evidence of registry, time, and due execution, with no proof required of the registrar's signature or office.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 51(1) states the registrar's endorsement duty and the deeming and evidentiary effects of the certificate as one short, coherent certification mechanism suitable for a single study unit.

rows.heading: Court order respecting production of book or record
rows.groupTitle: Court Order Required for Production of Registrar's Books or Records
rows.groupReason: One coherent duty-limitation rule with two interdependent conditions (judicial order for special reasons; service of order copy with summons) that together define when registry records may be compelled to court.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two conditions that must be satisfied before a registrar is obliged to attend court with a book or record in the registrar's custody, and identify the standard the judge applies.

evidenceText: The registrar shall not be obliged to attend any court with any book or record in the registrar's custody unless the judge presiding, or appointed to preside, shall for special reasons appearing to him or her sufficient order the production of the book or record, nor unless a copy of such order is served with the summons to witness.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 53 is a single, self-contained procedural rule: the registrar is not obliged to produce custody books or records to a court unless a judge orders production for special reasons and a copy of the order is served with the summons. The two conditions are interdependent and answer one recall task.

rows.heading: Certificate of satisfaction of mortgage
rows.groupTitle: Discharge of Registered Mortgage by Certificate of Satisfaction
rows.groupReason: One tightly interdependent rule covering who signs, how the certificate is proved, and where it is registered to discharge a registered mortgage.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the signatory, proof, and registration requirements for discharging a registered mortgage by certificate of satisfaction under section 54 of the Registry Act.

evidenceText: A registered mortgage may be discharged by a certificate of the satisfaction thereof signed by the mortgagee, his representatives or assigns, and acknowledged or proved in the same manner as an instrument, and registered with the acknowledgment or proof in the proper registry book in the office where the mortgage is registered.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 54 states one self-contained rule for discharging a registered mortgage by certificate of satisfaction, specifying signatory, proof, and registration requirements as a single recallable mechanism.

rows.heading: Certificate of partial release of mortgage
rows.groupTitle: Partial release of mortgage: form, contents, and effect
rows.groupReason: The provision states in one passage who may execute a partial release, the required form, the mandatory descriptive and monetary contents, and the resulting legal effect, all interdependent parts of a single rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may execute a partial release of mortgage, the required form and mandatory contents of the certificate, and the effect it has upon registration.

evidenceText: he may do so by a deed or certificate duly acknowledged or proved in the same manner as an instrument may be acknowledged or proved under this Act

such deed or certificate shall contain as precise a description of the portion of lands or of the estate or interest so released or discharged as would be necessary to be contained in an instrument of conveyance for registration under this Act
said certificate when registered shall have the same effect as a release has under section 54

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 55 is a self-contained operative provision governing partial release of a mortgage, combining actor, form, content, and effect rules in one short section that forms a single coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Conveyance by married woman
rows.groupTitle: Content requirement for conveyance by married woman of pre-marriage property
rows.groupReason: One operative 'shall state' rule prescribing what a conveyance by a married woman of pre-marriage property must include.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State what a conveyance by a married woman of property acquired before marriage must include regarding the name under which the property was acquired.
rows.sourceMapReason: Single operative content requirement for a specific conveyance type; independently recallable as a registry practice rule.

rows.heading: Certificate of satisfaction of judgment
rows.groupTitle: Discharging a Registered Judgment or Memorial of Judgment
rows.groupReason: The actor, method, partial-discharge option, and releasing effect are interdependent parts of one discharge mechanism best recalled together.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may discharge a registered judgment, certificate, or memorial of judgment, the required form and registration method, and the effect of registration on the charged land or a specially mentioned portion.

evidenceText: A registered judgment or certificate or memorial of judgment may be discharged or partially discharged by the person entitled to discharge the same, by certificate executed and registered in the same manner as a certificate of discharge of mortgage

such certificate, when registered, shall have the effect of releasing the land charged by the registration of the judgment, certificate or memorial, or such portion thereof as may be specially mentioned in such discharge.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 57 states one coherent mechanism — who may discharge a registered judgment, certificate, or memorial of judgment, the required form and method, and the releasing effect on charged land — forming a single recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of Order for Partition or Sale
rows.groupTitle: Registration of Order for Partition or Sale
rows.groupReason: Endorsement prerequisite, registration venue, and operative effect (same as registered conveyance) form one interdependent registration rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the endorsement requirement, the registration venue, and the legal effect of registering a copy of an Order for Partition or Sale under the Registry Act.

evidenceText: A copy of an Order for Partition or Sale endorsed with the certificate of the clerk in accordance with the Rules of Court under the Judicature Act may be registered in the registry office for the county in which the lands are situate and shall have the same effect as any registered conveyance within the provisions of this Act.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single short provision establishing one registration pathway: endorsement requirement, venue, and legal effect are interdependent parts of one recallable rule.

rows.heading: Registration of certificate of pending litigation
rows.groupTitle: Notice to non-parties of pending land-title litigation
rows.groupReason: The trigger, the no-notice rule, and both registration conditions form one concept a learner must recall together.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions that must be met before instituting an action or proceeding questioning title to land is deemed notice to a non-party.

evidenceText: shall not be deemed notice of the action or proceeding to any person not being a party thereto until a certificate of pending litigation prescribed by the Rules of Court under the Judicature Act has been signed by the clerk of The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick in the judicial district wherein the action was instituted or the proceeding taken, and has been registered in the registry office for the county in which the land is situate.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 59 states one integrated rule: pending land-title litigation is not notice to non-parties until a certificate of pending litigation is both signed by the clerk and registered in the county registry office. The trigger, negative rule, and two conditions are interdependent parts of a single recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of power of attorney, conveyance under power of attorney
rows.groupTitle: Registration of power of attorney and validity of conveyance under it
rows.groupReason: Both subsections together state the mandatory county-registration prerequisite for a valid conveyance under a POA and the registration/proof procedure for instruments executed by the attorney.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the mandatory registration requirement for a power of attorney (or confirming instrument) in the county registry office before a conveyance under it is valid, and the acknowledgment or proof procedure for registering an instrument executed by the attorney.

evidenceText: the registry of any instrument of conveyance under such power or other instrument shall not be valid unless the power or some instrument confirming it shall be duly registered in the registry office of the county where the lands to which the same relates are situate

The execution of any instrument by an attorney named in such power of attorney shall be valid and effectual, and may be registered upon the acknowledgment of such attorney before any of the persons authorized by this Act to take acknowledgments

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 60 is a short, self-contained provision on POA registration and the validity conditions for conveyances executed under a power of attorney; both subsections form one coherent recall unit on the POA registration mechanism.

rows.heading: Summons to witness
rows.groupTitle: Summons to compel witness attendance or instrument production for registration
rows.groupReason: One procedural concept: which courts may issue the summons, its two purposes (witness attendance or instrument production for proof of registration), form, and the consequence of disobedience.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which courts may issue a summons under the Registry Act, the two purposes the summons may serve (compelling witness attendance or production of a conveyance or instrument for proof of registration), and that disobedience may be punished by the issuing court in the usual manner.

evidenceText: A summons to witness may be issued from The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick, or any other court having jurisdiction

to compel the attendance of any witness, or the production of any conveyance or instrument for the proof thereof, that the same may be registered agreeably to the provisions of this Act; disobedience to such summons may be punished by such court in the usual manner.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 61 is a short, self-contained procedural provision creating one coherent summons power with its purpose and disobedience consequence; no natural split point exists.

rows.heading: Orders of Provincial or Federal Cabinet
rows.groupTitle: Registration of Orders in Council
rows.groupReason: All elements—what may be registered, where, and the certification requirement—form a single permissive registration rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the conditions under which Orders of the Governor General in Council or the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may be registered in a county registry office, including the required certification.

evidenceText: Orders of the Governor General in Council or the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may be registered in the registry office for the county in which any land to which the Order in Council relates is situate, upon the deposit of a copy of the order certified by the clerk or assistant or acting clerk of the Council.

rows.sourceMapReason: A short, self-contained permissive registration rule for Orders in Council specifying location and certification requirement as one coherent recall task.

rows.heading: Registration of bond to Crown
rows.groupTitle: Recording requirement for a bond to the Crown
rows.groupReason: One self-contained rule tying the legal effect of a bond to the Crown (binding the land) to a specific registration prerequisite in the county registry office.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the condition under which a bond to the Crown binds the land of the person executing it and identify the required registry office for recording.

evidenceText: No bond to the Crown binds the land of any person executing the same unless and until it is recorded in the registry office for the county wherein the land is situate.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single operative rule: a bond to the Crown does not bind the land of the person executing it unless and until recorded in the county registry office.

rows.heading: Registration as notice
rows.groupTitle: Notice effect of registration and registrar's proof duty
rows.groupReason: Both the third-party notice rule (surviving proof defects) and the registrar's continuing proof duty form a single recall task on the legal effect of registration and its limits.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that registration of an instrument constitutes notice to all persons claiming an interest in the lands subsequent to registration even with defective proof, and that the registrar's duty to refuse registration without the proof required by the Act is not dispensed with.

evidenceText: The registration of any instrument under this Act constitutes notice of the instrument to all persons claiming any interest in the lands subsequent to such registration, notwithstanding any defect in the proof for registration, but nevertheless it shall continue to be the duty of every registrar not to register any instrument except on such proof as is required by this Act.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 64 states one coherent rule: registration gives constructive notice to subsequent claimants even with defective proof, while the registrar's duty to require proper proof is unaffected. The two clauses are interlocked by 'notwithstanding' and 'but nevertheless' and should be recalled together.

rows.heading: Payment of fees
rows.groupTitle: Fee payment as precondition to compulsory registration
rows.groupReason: One rule with one actor (the registrar), one modality (shall not be compelled), and one condition (fees first paid) forms a single recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the condition that must be satisfied before the registrar can be compelled to register an instrument under the Registry Act.

evidenceText: The registrar shall not be compelled to register any instrument unless the fees authorized by this Act are first paid thereon.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 65 states a single, self-contained prerequisite: the registrar shall not be compelled to register any instrument unless authorized fees are first paid. It has clear independent recall value as a core registration precondition.

rows.heading: Payment of fees of a digitally scanned image of an instrument
rows.groupTitle: Electronic payment for digitally scanned images
rows.groupReason: One rule tying the mandatory electronic payment modality to the Chief Registrar of Deeds' delegated manner and timing for fees and taxes on digitally scanned images.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the required payment method for fees and taxes on registration of a digitally scanned image of an instrument and identify who establishes the manner and timing.

evidenceText: Payment of any fees or taxes in respect of the registration of a digitally scanned image of an instrument shall be made by electronic means in such manner and at such time as is established by the Chief Registrar of Deeds.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single-sentence provision establishing a specific electronic-payment requirement for digitally scanned images, with manner and timing delegated to the Chief Registrar of Deeds. One focused recall task.

rows.heading: Offences and penalty respecting taking of fees by employees
rows.groupTitle: Retaining registry office fees and the dismissal penalty
rows.groupReason: Subsection (2) withholds from registry-office employees any right to keep fees received for work done or information furnished in connection with the registry office, and subsection (3) makes dismissal from office the penalty for any violation.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State who is barred from retaining registry office fees and the penalty for a violation.

evidenceText: No registrar, deputy registrar, or clerk in the registry office, is entitled to retain for his own use any fee received for work done or information furnished in connection with the registry office.
The penalty for any violation of this section shall be dismissal from office.

rows.sourceMapReason: Subsection 66(1) is repealed, but subsections 66(2) and 66(3) remain in force as one coherent rule: no registrar, deputy registrar or clerk in the registry office is entitled to retain for his or her own use any fee received for work done or information furnished in connection with the registry office, and the penalty for any violation is dismissal from office.

rows.heading: Liability of registrar, deputy registrar and clerk
rows.groupTitle: Immunity of registry office personnel acting in good faith
rows.groupReason: One rule: personal immunity for registry office staff whose acts or omissions were in good faith in pursuing statutory duties.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the personal immunity available to a registrar of deeds, deputy registrar of deeds, or clerk in a registry office and identify the good-faith and duties conditions that must be met.

evidenceText: No action lies against a registrar of deeds, a deputy registrar of deeds or a clerk in a registry office with respect to any act or omission by that person if he acted in good faith in pursuing his duties under this or any other Act or law.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 66.1 is a single, self-contained immunity rule for registry office personnel; no split or combine needed.

rows.heading: Proceedings against the Crown
rows.groupTitle: Proceedings Against the Crown for Registry Office Acts
rows.groupReason: Crown is the proper respondent for registry staff acts or omissions, notwithstanding personal immunity under s. 66.1 and PACA s. 4.

rows.heading: Regulations and amendments respecting Schedule of Fees

rows.heading: Statement of fees

rows.sourceMapReason: Three short subsections establish the legal identity of Service New Brunswick (corporate form, mandatory composition, head office) as one unified recall task; low independent priority but states a mandatory composition rule and specific corporate form beyond pure reference.

rows.heading: Objects and purposes
rows.groupTitle: Objects and Purposes of Service New Brunswick
