rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the six statutory objects and purposes of Service New Brunswick, including the Lieutenant-Governor in Council's residual direction power in item (f).

evidenceText: to provide services to public bodies, local government bodies, other governments, the public and other bodies or persons
to acquire and maintain the infrastructure needed to support the delivery of services
to carry out any other activities or duties that the Lieutenant-Governor in Council directs

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 3 is a single coherent mandate listing six objects and purposes of Service New Brunswick that all answer the same recall question; no materially distinct recall tasks warrant a split.

rows.heading: Powers and duties
rows.groupTitle: Service New Brunswick capacity, powers, and duties
rows.groupReason: Subsections 4(1)–4(3) together state the entity's legal capacity, its enumerated powers, and its duty to perform statutory obligations; recalling them separately would fragment one coherent standing provision.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall Service New Brunswick's natural-person capacity, its specific powers (property dealings, agreements, exercise of statutory powers, and incidental acts), and its duty to perform any duty imposed under an act or regulation.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 4 is a short, cohesive capacity-and-duties provision: a general capacity grant, enumerated powers without limiting that grant, and a single duty clause all define Service New Brunswick's legal standing as one concept.

rows.heading: Delegation by Service New Brunswick
rows.groupTitle: Delegation of Service New Brunswick powers and duties
rows.groupReason: The delegation power, permitted delegatees, conditions power, and delegate compliance duty form one coherent mechanism that a learner recalls as a single delegation rule set.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the persons to whom Service New Brunswick may delegate its powers or duties in writing, the ability to impose terms and conditions in the delegation, and the delegate's duty to comply with those terms.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 5 is a short, self-contained delegation provision creating a power to delegate in writing to specific persons, a power to impose terms and conditions, and a corresponding compliance duty on the delegate. The three subsections form one interdependent delegation mechanism suitable for a single study unit.

rows.heading: Agreements or arrangements to provide services
rows.groupTitle: Counterparties for Service New Brunswick service agreements

rows.sourceMapReason: All three subsections state one permissive power (Service New Brunswick may enter into service agreements) with three mutually exclusive counterparty categories that together define the full scope; they answer one recall question and should be studied as a unit.

rows.heading: Prescribed public bodies required to receive specified services

evidenceText: A public body prescribed by regulation shall receive from Service New Brunswick any service specified by regulation for that public body.

rows.sourceMapReason: Short mandatory-obligation provision creating a shall-duty distinct from the permissive agreements in s.6; one clearly recallable rule.

rows.heading: Service New Brunswick may engage a third party to provide a service on its behalf

provide for the protection of personal information against risks, including unauthorized access, use, disclosure or destruction

rows.heading: Service New Brunswick may engage a third party to provide a service on its behalf

rows.sourceMapReason: The section pairs Service New Brunswick's engagement authority and mandatory agreement contents (8(1)–(4)) with a separate third-party prohibition and a deemed RIPA-compliance effect (8(5)–(6)), creating two independently recallable study tasks with different actors and modalities.

rows.heading: Role of Board

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 10 contains two tightly interdependent subsections: a duty to administer with a sound-business-practices standard (10(1)) and an enabling power to exercise all powers of Service New Brunswick (10(2)). Together they answer one recall question about the Board's core role and form a single coherent concept.

rows.heading: Board composition

rows.heading: Terms of office and vacancies

rows.heading: Terms of office and vacancies

In the case of the temporary absence or inability to act of a member of the Board referred to in paragraph 11(1)(b), (c) or (d) the Minister may appoint a substitute for the member for the period of the temporary absence or inability to act.

rows.heading: Secretary

rows.heading: Meetings and quorum

rows.heading: Remuneration and expenses

rows.heading: Form and content of conveyances of land and agreements for sale or purchase of land, format of forms

evidenceText: The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing the form and content of conveyances of land by deed, lease, mortgage and debenture, and thereafter a conveyance drawn contrary to such regulation shall not be accepted for registration in a registry office, notwithstanding the Registry Act.
Notwithstanding subsection (1), the parties to a conveyance of land by deed, lease, mortgage or debenture made in a form prescribed hereunder may include in the conveyance any covenant or condition.

The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing the size, style of type, general format and other matters of like nature pertaining to standard forms of conveyances by deed, lease, mortgage or debenture and of agreements prescribed under the authority of this Act.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 2 contains three distinct recall tasks: (1) the scope of regulatory power over form, content, and format and the registration consequence of non-compliance; (2) the power to prescribe meaning and legal effect with mandatory court construction and retroactivity; and (3) savings for inter-party validity, pre-regulation documents, and deemed compliance.

rows.heading: Form and content of conveyances of land and agreements for sale or purchase of land, format of forms

evidenceText: In making regulations pursuant to subsection (1) the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may prescribe the meaning and legal effect of any language used in any form prescribed thereunder, and any conveyance made in a form prescribed by regulation shall be construed in all courts in accordance with the meaning and legal effect assigned to its language by the regulations.

Any regulation made pursuant to subsection (1) for the purposes of subsection (2) or (2.1) may be retroactive in its operation, and any regulation which is to be retroactive in its operation shall specify the date on which it shall be deemed to have come into force.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 2 contains three distinct recall tasks: (1) the scope of regulatory power over form, content, and format and the registration consequence of non-compliance; (2) the power to prescribe meaning and legal effect with mandatory court construction and retroactivity; and (3) savings for inter-party validity, pre-regulation documents, and deemed compliance.

rows.heading: Form and content of conveyances of land and agreements for sale or purchase of land, format of forms
rows.groupTitle: Savings for inter-party validity, pre-regulation documents, and deemed compliance

evidenceText: Nothing contained in this section affects (a) the validity or effect of any conveyance of land by deed, lease, mortgage or debenture or any agreement drawn contrary to any regulation made pursuant to this section, as regards the persons who are the parties thereto; or (b) the acceptance for registration in a registry office of a conveyance by deed, lease, mortgage or debenture or of an agreement which was drawn, executed and delivered prior to the promulgation of the regulations authorized under this section.

Notwithstanding subsection (1), a conveyance of land by deed, lease, mortgage or debenture drawn, executed and delivered after the coming into force of this Act and the regulations authorized under this section, shall, upon its registration in a registry office, be deemed to have been in compliance with this Act and the regulations.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 2 contains three distinct recall tasks: (1) the scope of regulatory power over form, content, and format and the registration consequence of non-compliance; (2) the power to prescribe meaning and legal effect with mandatory court construction and retroactivity; and (3) savings for inter-party validity, pre-regulation documents, and deemed compliance.

evidenceText: The New Brunswick Plane Rectangular Coordinate Projection is a stereographic double projection of the NAD83 (CSRS) geocentric ellipsoid, on a secant plane.

The coordinates shall be made to depend on (a) the values of the six New Brunswick Canadian Base Network stations set out in this schedule, or (b) the values of the densification of the Canadian Base Network carried out by Service New Brunswick for the purpose of establishing the New Brunswick High Precision Network.

rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the basis on which the Minister may issue a construction permit, the initial three-year term, the maximum renewal period, and the sources of conditions binding the permit.

evidenceText: Based upon consideration of the plans submitted and any alterations thereof, the Minister may issue a construction permit to the person applying.

A construction permit shall be for a term of three years, renewable for a maximum of two one-year periods at the discretion of the Minister and shall be subject to the terms and conditions prescribed by regulation and to any special conditions imposed by the Minister thereon.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13 contains two distinct recall tasks: the prohibition and application duties on persons and lease holders, and the Minister's issuance power with the resulting permit's term and conditions.

rows.heading: Construction permit – duties
rows.groupTitle: Duty of construction-permit holder to perform prescribed work
rows.groupReason: One operative duty: the permit holder must perform work requirements to the extent and value set by regulation.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the obligation imposed on the holder of a construction permit under section 14 and identify the source of the prescribed extent and value.

evidenceText: The holder of a construction permit shall perform the work requirements to the extent and value prescribed by regulation.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 14 imposes one clear, operative duty on the construction-permit holder (perform work requirements to the extent and value prescribed by regulation). It is a single recallable obligation distinct from the application and issuance rules in section 13.

rows.heading: Transference of licence, lease or permit
rows.groupTitle: Transference of underground storage instruments
rows.groupReason: Prohibition, prior-written-consent requirement, and conditions power are one interdependent rule a learner recalls as a unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that no underground storage exploration licence, storage lease, or construction permit may be surrendered, assigned, sublet, transferred, or abandoned without prior written consent of the Minister, who may prescribe special conditions.

evidenceText: No underground storage exploration licence, storage lease or construction permit shall be surrendered, assigned, sublet or otherwise transferred or abandoned without the prior written consent of the Minister upon any special conditions he may prescribe.

rows.sourceMapReason: A single prohibition with its consent condition and the Minister's conditions power forms one interdependent recall unit.

rows.heading: Revocation of licence, lease or permit
rows.groupTitle: Minister's revocation power for non-compliance
rows.groupReason: One provision, one power, one trigger — a compact standalone recall unit on the grounds and effect of revocation.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the trigger (non-compliance with the Act, regulations, or special conditions), the actor (the Minister), and the scope of the revocation power (any licence, lease, or permit under the Act).

evidenceText: the Minister may forthwith revoke any licence, lease or permit issued or granted to that person under this Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16 states a single, self-contained revocation power: the Minister may forthwith revoke a licence, lease, or permit on a trigger of non-compliance with the Act, regulations, or special conditions. One actor, one trigger, one power — a single recallable concept.

rows.heading: Security
rows.groupTitle: Requirements for security under the Underground Storage Act
rows.groupReason: All three security requirements (payable to Minister of Finance and Treasury Board, amount per regulations, form per Oil and Natural Gas Act) are interdependent conditions that must be recalled together.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the payee, the amount-setting mechanism, and the permitted forms for security required under the Underground Storage Act.

evidenceText: shall be made payable to the Minister of Finance and Treasury Board, shall be in the amount specified by the regulations and shall be in one of the forms specified in the Oil and Natural Gas Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 17 sets three tightly interdependent requirements for any security required under the Act (payee, amount, and form), answering a single recall question and forming one coherent unit.

rows.heading: Forfeiture of security
rows.groupTitle: Ministerial power to forfeit security
rows.groupReason: Covers the two alternative triggers (non-compliance with Act/regulations/special conditions, or damage from authorized operations), the Minister's forfeiture power over the responsible person's security, and the permitted uses of the forfeited sums.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two alternative triggers for forfeiture, identify the responsible person, and explain the two permitted purposes for expending the forfeited sums under section 18.

evidenceText: the Minister may declare forfeit any security provided under this Act by the person responsible for such failure or damage and may expend the sums so declared to rectify the effects of such failure or to compensate for or rectify such damage

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18 states a single coherent ministerial forfeiture power with its two alternative triggers and the permitted expenditure of forfeited sums; the elements are tightly interdependent and form one recallable concept.

rows.heading: Return or maintenance of security
rows.groupTitle: Return or maintenance of security (s. 19)
rows.groupReason: The provision states the default rule (security is returnable) and the depositor's option to maintain it for other activities, subject to forfeiture under s. 18. These are two sides of one disposition rule and should be recalled together.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the rule for disposition of security furnished under the Underground Storage Act, including the depositor's option to maintain security for other authorized activities and the qualifier in section 18.

evidenceText: Subject to section 18, any security furnished under this Act is returnable to the person who deposited the said security, or, at his option, may be maintained on deposit for other activities authorized by this Act or any other Act administered by the Minister.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19 is a short, coherent rule stating that security furnished under the Act is returnable to the depositor or, at the depositor's option, may be maintained for other authorized activities, subject to the forfeiture power in section 18. The return right and the option to roll over form one recall task: what happens to security when the original activity ends.

rows.heading: Reports and returns, entry and inspection
rows.groupTitle: Reporting and returns duty on holders
rows.groupReason: Standalone reporting obligation: identifies the actors (holders of storage leases, construction permits, or underground storage exploration licences) and the duty to produce reports and returns the Minister requires.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State who is subject to the reporting and returns duty under section 20(1) and to whom the reports are made.

evidenceText: Each holder of a storage lease, construction permit or underground storage exploration licence shall make such reports and returns as the Minister may require.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 20 contains two substantively distinct obligations: a general reporting/returns duty (20(1)) and a separate entry-and-inspection regime with its own conditions and corresponding holder duty (20(2)). A learner would recall these as separate prompts.

rows.heading: Reports and returns, entry and inspection
rows.groupTitle: Entry, inspection, and sampling power; holder duty to permit and facilitate
rows.groupReason: Cohesive entry-and-inspection regime: the Minister's authorized-person power (enter, inspect records/plants/equipment, sample, test), its conditions (reasonable time, identification card), and the holder's corresponding duty to permit and facilitate.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may exercise entry and inspection under section 20(2), the conditions attached (reasonable time, identification card), the specific powers granted, and the holder's duty to permit and facilitate access.

evidenceText: Persons authorized by the Minister to enforce the provisions of this Act and the regulations, at any reasonable time and upon the presentation of an identification card issued by the Minister may
and each holder of a storage lease, construction permit or underground storage exploration licence shall permit and facilitate such access and inspection.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 20 contains two substantively distinct obligations: a general reporting/returns duty (20(1)) and a separate entry-and-inspection regime with its own conditions and corresponding holder duty (20(2)). A learner would recall these as separate prompts.

rows.heading: Special conditions and orders
rows.groupTitle: Minister's special conditions and entry orders (s. 21)
rows.groupReason: Both subparagraphs express the Minister's supplementary discretionary authority; recalling them together captures the full scope of the special-conditions-and-orders power.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two specific powers section 21 gives the Minister in addition to other powers in the Act: prescribing special conditions on licences, leases, or permits, and making a special order for entry on private lands for exploration (subject to section 9).

evidenceText: prescribe special conditions for the issuance, renewal or transfer of an underground storage exploration licence, storage leases or construction permit
make a special order permitting, subject to section 9, entry upon private lands for the purpose of exploration to evaluate underground storage potential for fluids

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 21 grants the Minister two short, tightly related discretionary powers under one framing ('in addition to powers contained elsewhere in this Act'): prescribing special conditions on instruments and making entry orders on private lands. Both are independently meaningful but short enough to recall together as the Minister's special-condition and special-order authority.

rows.heading: Regulations
rows.groupTitle: Scope of Regulatory Power Under the Underground Storage Act
rows.groupReason: One enabling power with enumerated subject areas forming a single regulatory-scope recall task.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the areas in which the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations under the Underground Storage Act.

evidenceText: The Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations:
prescribing the amount of any fee, rental or security required by this Act
governing generally all matters considered advisable and convenient for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 22 grants the Lieutenant-Governor in Council a single regulatory power enumerated across subject areas (fees/security, fluid designation, application content, instrument terms and forms, work requirements, and a general catch-all). All items answer one recall question: what may be regulated under this Act.

rows.heading: Will defined
rows.groupTitle: Definition of "will" in the Wills Act
rows.groupReason: One definitional rule: what "will" includes for all purposes of the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that under the Wills Act, "will" includes a testament, a codicil, an appointment by will or by writing in the nature of a will in exercise of a power, and any other testamentary disposition.
rows.sourceMapReason: The section defines the scope of "will" for the entire Act, expanding it beyond a last will and testament to include codicils, appointments by will, and other testamentary dispositions.

rows.heading: Power of testator
rows.groupTitle: Scope of testamentary disposition power
rows.groupReason: The general rule and the three enumerated property-interest categories (estates pur autre vie, contingent/executory/future interests, rights of entry) form one recall task: what may a testator dispose of by will.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the full scope of property a testator may devise, bequeath, or dispose of by will under section 2, including the three categories of interests expressly included.

evidenceText: A person may by will devise, bequeath or dispose of all real and personal property, whether acquired before or after making his will, to which at the time of his death he is entitled either at law or in equity
estates pur autre vie, whether there is or is not a special occupant and whether they are corporeal or incorporeal hereditaments
contingent, executory or other future interest in real or personal property
rights of entry

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 2 states one coherent concept: the full scope of testamentary disposition, combining the general rule (all real and personal property at law or in equity) with three enumerated inclusions that remove doubt about unusual interests.

rows.heading: Necessity of writing
rows.groupTitle: Writing requirement for a will
rows.groupReason: One-sentence provision stating the writing condition for will validity; forms a single recall task on basic will formalities.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that under the Wills Act a will is valid only when it is in writing.

evidenceText: A will is valid only when it is in writing.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 3 states a single, foundational validity rule for wills (writing requirement) that is independently recallable and central to any study of will formalities.

rows.heading: Attestation clause
rows.groupTitle: Attestation requirements for a valid will
rows.groupReason: The three paragraphs are conjunctive conditions of one validity rule; recalling them separately would fragment the test.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the three execution requirements (signing by the testator or by another in the testator's presence, witness presence at signing or acknowledgment, and witness subscription in the testator's presence) that must all be met for a will to be valid under section 4.

evidenceText: at its end it is signed by the testator or signed in his name by some other person in his presence and by his direction
the testator makes or acknowledges the signature in the presence of two or more attesting witnesses present at the time
two or more of the attesting witnesses subscribe the will in the presence of the testator

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 4 states one conjunctive validity test with three interdependent execution requirements (signing, witness presence, witness subscription) that form a single recall unit.

rows.heading: Attestation clause when using an electronic means of communication
rows.groupTitle: Counterpart execution of electronic wills
rows.groupReason: The counterpart-signing permission, the rule that counterparts together constitute the will, and the deemed-identity rule form a separate mechanism distinct from the attestation-presence requirements.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain that a will executed electronically may be signed or subscribed in counterpart, that counterparts together constitute the will, and that minor non-substantive format or layout differences do not defeat identity.

evidenceText: the requirements that a will be signed or subscribed may be satisfied by signing or subscribing the will in counterpart
counterparts of a will shall together constitute the will
counterparts of a will are deemed to be identical even if there are minor, non-substantive differences in format or layout of the counterparts

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 4.1 contains two distinct mechanisms: (a) how electronic means of communication satisfies the three attestation requirements with a lawyer-witness condition, plus a mandatory statement; and (b) the separate counterpart-execution mechanism with its own rules on identity and constitution of the will.

rows.heading: Attestation clause when using an electronic means of communication
rows.groupTitle: Electronic attestation requirements and mandatory statement
rows.groupReason: The definition, the three parallel electronic-attestation permissions, the lawyer-witness condition, and the mandatory statement form one coherent recall task: how electronic attestation works under section 4.1.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the definition of electronic means of communication, identify which section 4 attestation requirements it may satisfy, the requirement that at least one witness be a practising member of the Law Society of New Brunswick, and the mandatory statement in the will.

evidenceText: "electronic means of communication" means an electronic means of communication in which all persons are able to see, hear and communicate with one another in real time, to the same extent as if the persons were communicating in person in the same location.
provided that at least one witness is a lawyer who is a practising member of the Law Society of New Brunswick
A will made in accordance with this section shall include a statement that it was signed and witnessed in accordance with this section.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 4.1 contains two distinct mechanisms: (a) how electronic means of communication satisfies the three attestation requirements with a lawyer-witness condition, plus a mandatory statement; and (b) the separate counterpart-execution mechanism with its own rules on identity and constitution of the will.

rows.heading: Will of member of Canadian Forces
rows.groupTitle: Simplified will for military and maritime personnel – form and proof of active service
rows.groupReason: Subsections 5(1)–(3) form one permission with its evidentiary fallback; separating the proof rules would fragment the eligibility mechanism.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the form requirements for a will made by a member of the Canadian Forces, another force on active service, or a mariner at sea, and identify the certificate and deeming provisions that prove active service.

evidenceText: may make a will by a writing signed by him or by some other person in his presence and by his direction without any further formality or any requirement of the presence of or attestation of signature by a witness

a certificate signed by or on behalf of an officer purporting to have custody of the records of the force in which a person was serving at the time the will was made setting out that the person was on active service at that time, is sufficient proof of that fact

a member of a naval, land or air force is deemed to be on active service after he has taken steps under the orders of a superior officer preparatory to serving with or being attached to or seconded to a component of such a force that has been placed on active service

rows.sourceMapReason: The section creates a self-contained permission for military and maritime personnel to make a simplified will, supported by two tightly interdependent proof-of-service subsections; all three form one coherent mechanism.

rows.heading: Holograph will
rows.groupTitle: Holograph will
rows.groupReason: One operative permission defining the sole requirements (own handwriting, own signature) and the formalities dispensed with (no formality, no witnesses) for a holographic will.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the two requirements for a valid holographic will under section 6 and identify the formalities it expressly dispenses with.

evidenceText: A testator may make a valid will wholly by his own handwriting and signature, without formality, and without the presence, attestation or signature of a witness.

rows.sourceMapReason: Single self-contained rule establishing the requirements and exemptions for a valid holographic will; forms one coherent recall task with no internal sub-concepts to separate.

rows.heading: Signature to will
rows.groupTitle: Effect of a conforming signature on post-signature dispositions
rows.groupReason: Subsection (3) states an independent substantive limitation on what a conforming signature can effect, distinct from the position-validity rule in subsections (1) and (2).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain that a signature conforming to sections 4, 5, 6, or 7 does not give effect to a disposition or direction underneath or following the signature or inserted after the signature was made.

evidenceText: a signature in conformity with section 4, 5 or 6 or this section does not give effect to a disposition or direction that is underneath the signature or that follows the signature or to a disposition or direction inserted after the signature was made

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 7 contains two distinct recall tasks: the general signature-position validity rule with its non-invalidating illustrations (ss. 7(1)–(2)) and a separate substantive rule limiting a signature's effect to text preceding it (s. 7(3)).

rows.heading: Signature to will
rows.groupTitle: Signature position validity and non-invalidating circumstances
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1) and (2) are tightly interdependent; the enumerated circumstances in (2) illustrate the breadth of the general position rule in (1).
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State where a testator's signature must be placed for a will to be valid and identify the specific position circumstances listed in subsection (2) that do not render a will invalid.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 7 contains two distinct recall tasks: the general signature-position validity rule with its non-invalidating illustrations (ss. 7(1)–(2)) and a separate substantive rule limiting a signature's effect to text preceding it (s. 7(3)).

rows.heading: Persons under 19 years
rows.groupTitle: Validity and Revocation of Wills by Persons Under 19
rows.groupReason: All three subsections address one rule: when a will by a person under 19 is valid, how military status is proved, and the corollary revocation right while still under 19.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the three conditions under which a will made by a person under 19 is valid, identify the evidentiary role of a military records officer's certificate, and confirm the power to revoke such a will while still under 19.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 8 is a short, coherent provision on validity and revocation of wills by persons under 19; the three subsections form one interdependent rule (validity conditions, supporting evidentiary proof, and the corollary revocation power).

rows.heading: Validity of power of appointment
rows.groupTitle: Wills Act form prevails over power-of-appointment form requirement
rows.groupReason: Single operative rule on form validity for powers of appointment; no internal sub-parts to separate.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the rule in section 9: a will made in accordance with the Wills Act is a valid execution of a power of appointment by will even if the power required a different form.

evidenceText: A will made in accordance with this Act is as to form a valid execution of a power of appointment by will notwithstanding that it has been expressly required that a will in exercise of the power be made in some form other than that in which it is made.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 9 states a single, self-contained validity rule: a will made under the Act satisfies any power-of-appointment form requirement, even if the power prescribed a different form. One recall task, no split or combine needed.

rows.heading: Publication of will
rows.groupTitle: No publication required for will validity
rows.groupReason: One rule answering whether publication is a validity requirement for a will made under the Act.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State that a will made in accordance with the Wills Act is valid without other publication.

evidenceText: A will made in accordance with this Act is valid without other publication.

rows.sourceMapReason: A single-sentence validity rule confirming that publication is not required for a will made in accordance with the Act; one self-contained recall task with no sub-parts to split.

rows.heading: Effect of incompetency of attesting witness
rows.groupTitle: Effect of incompetency of attesting witness on will validity
rows.groupReason: Single operative rule: witness incompetence (at execution or afterward) does not render the will invalid.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State whether and how the will's validity is affected when an attesting witness is or becomes incompetent to prove execution.

evidenceText: Where a person who attested a will was at the time of its execution or afterward has become incompetent as a witness to prove its execution, the will is not on that account invalid.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 11 states one clear operative rule: an attesting witness's incompetence does not invalidate the will. It is a self-contained protection distinct from Section 12's conflict-of-interest rule.

rows.heading: Conflict of interest of attesting witness
rows.groupTitle: Effect of conflict of interest in attesting witness
rows.groupReason: The voiding rule, debt-charge exclusion, competence carve-out, and two-witness saving condition form one interdependent recall task on when a gift to an attesting witness is or is not void.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State when a devise, bequest, or other disposition to an attesting witness (or spouse or claimant) is void, note the exclusion for charges and directions for payment of debt, and identify the condition under subsection (2) that prevents the gift from being void.

evidenceText: the devise, bequest or other disposition or appointment is void so far only as it concerns the person so attesting, or his or her spouse or a person claiming under any of them; but the person so attesting is a competent witness to prove the execution of the will or its validity or invalidity.

Where a will is attested by at least two persons who are not within subsection (1) or where no attestation is necessary, the devise, bequest or other disposition or appointment is not void under that subsection.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 12 states one coherent rule on the effect of a conflict of interest in attesting witnesses: the voiding rule, the debt-charge exclusion, the competence point, and the two-witness saving condition all answer the same recall question.

rows.heading: Power of creditor to attest will
rows.groupTitle: Creditor competency to attest a will charging their debt
rows.groupReason: One rule with one trigger (debt charged by will) and one effect (creditor or spouse remains competent witness), forming a single recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State when a creditor or the spouse of a creditor whose debt is charged on real or personal property by a will remains a competent witness to prove the execution or validity of that will.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 13 states one coherent rule: a creditor or creditor's spouse whose debt is charged on property by a will remains a competent attesting witness. It is a single recall task distinct from s.12 (beneficial dispositions) and s.14 (executors).

rows.heading: Power of executor to attest will
rows.groupTitle: Executor witness competency
rows.groupReason: Single operative rule establishing that executor status is not a ground of witness incompetency in will proceedings.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the rule that a person is not incompetent as a witness to prove a will's execution or validity/invalidity solely by virtue of being an executor.

evidenceText: A person is not incompetent as a witness to prove the execution of a will, or its validity or invalidity solely because he is an executor.

rows.sourceMapReason: One-sentence competency rule: executor status alone does not disqualify a person from witnessing a will; self-contained and independently recallable.

rows.heading: Revocation of will
rows.groupTitle: Exclusive grounds for revocation of a will
rows.groupReason: The three operative methods (compliant will, compliant written declaration, physical destruction with intent) are tied by the exclusive 'only by' framing and answer one recall question.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the only three methods by which a will or part of a will may be revoked, including the specific requirements for each documentary method and the physical-destruction method (actor, presence/direction, and intention).

evidenceText: another will made in accordance with the provisions of this Act,
a writing declaring an intention to revoke and made in accordance with the provisions of this Act governing making of a will
burning, tearing or otherwise destroying it by the testator or by some person in his presence and by his direction with the intention of revoking it

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 15 sets out the exclusive grounds for revoking a will—three methods unified by the limiting phrase 'revoked only by'—forming one coherent recall task for a learner.

rows.heading: Effect of subsequent marriage on will
rows.groupTitle: Deemed intestacy on subsequent marriage
rows.groupReason: Subsections (1)–(2) state the triggering rule: the conditions (marriage while alive or surviving issue of a subsequent marriage) under which the will is treated as revoked by operation of law.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the two conditions under which a person who made a will and subsequently marries is deemed to have died intestate, and the Court to which the section applies.

evidenceText: A person who has made a will and who subsequently marries and dies shall be deemed to have died intestate if the person dies
while married, or
while any issue of a marriage of the testator subsequent to the will is still alive.

rows.sourceMapReason: The section contains two distinct recall tasks: the substantive rule creating deemed intestacy on subsequent marriage, and the separate application-and-decision mechanism (actors, time limit, undue-detriment standard, extension power) that allows partial restoration of the will.

rows.heading: Effect of subsequent marriage on will
rows.groupTitle: Application and Court decision to restore a devise or bequest
rows.groupReason: Subsections (3)–(6) set out the applicant, the four-month limit, the undue-detriment standard with its safe-harbour, and the Court's power to extend time — a distinct procedural-and-decision recall task separate from the triggering rule.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State who may apply, the time limit, the undue-detriment standard the Court applies, the safe-harbour rule, and the Court's power to extend the period for undistributed estate.

evidenceText: a person who is a beneficiary under the will but who will take no part of the deceased's estate on intestacy may apply to the Court within four months after the deceased's death for effect to be given to the devise or bequest in the will
the Court may order that effect be given to any devise or bequest, or any part of it, contained in the will if such an order can be made without undue detriment

Without limiting the generality of subsection (4), the Court may consider that a detriment to a person who is entitled to part of the deceased's estate on intestacy and who is a beneficiary under the will is not an undue detriment if that person will receive, as a result of an order made under subsection (4), no less than the person would have been entitled to under the will.

Notwithstanding subsection (3), the Court may, after the expiration of the period referred to in that subsection, if the Court considers it just, allow an application to be made under that subsection in respect of any portion of the deceased's estate remaining undistributed at the date of the application.

rows.sourceMapReason: The section contains two distinct recall tasks: the substantive rule creating deemed intestacy on subsequent marriage, and the separate application-and-decision mechanism (actors, time limit, undue-detriment standard, extension power) that allows partial restoration of the will.

rows.heading: Circumstances where section 15.1 does not apply
rows.groupTitle: Exceptions to the Effect of Subsequent Marriage on a Will (s. 16)
rows.groupReason: The two exceptions—contemplation-of-marriage declaration and power-of-appointment wills—are jointly needed to know the full scope of when s. 15.1 is excluded.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the two circumstances in which section 15.1 (deeming a testator to have died intestate after subsequent marriage) does not apply: a will declaring it was made in contemplation of the marriage, and a will made in exercise of a power of appointment over property that would not pass to the testator's heir, executor, administrator, or intestate successors.

evidenceText: Section 15.1 does not apply where (a) there is a declaration in the will that it is made in contemplation of the marriage, or (b) the will is made in exercise of a power of appointment of real or personal property that would not in default of the appointment pass to the heir, executor or administrator of the testator or to the persons entitled to the estate of the testator if the testator died intestate.

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 16 lists two short exceptions to section 15.1's operation; both answer the same recall question (when the marriage-revocation rule does not apply) and form one coherent concept.

rows.heading: Presumption of intention to revoke
rows.groupTitle: Revocation by Presumption of Changed Intention
rows.groupReason: Single operative rule: a will is not revoked by presuming an intention to revoke on the ground of a change in circumstances.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the rule that a will is not revoked by presumption of an intention to revoke on the ground of a change in circumstances.

evidenceText: A will is not revoked by presumption of an intention to revoke it on the ground of a change in circumstances.

rows.sourceMapReason: Short operative rule prohibiting revocation of a will by presumption of changed intention based on altered circumstances; independently recallable substantive protection.

rows.heading: Alterations
rows.groupTitle: Effect of and requirements for alterations to a will
rows.groupReason: Subsections 18(1) and 18(2) form one interdependent rule: the default consequence of a non-compliant alteration and the compliant signing, attestation, and placement path, including the section 5 and section 6 exception.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the effect of a will alteration not made in accordance with the Act and the signing, attestation, and placement requirements for a valid alteration, including the testator-signature-only rule for wills made under section 5 or section 6.
rows.sourceMapReason: Section 18 states one coherent rule on will alterations: the default consequence of a non-compliant alteration and the specific signing and placement requirements for a valid alteration.

rows.heading: Revival of revocation
rows.groupTitle: Revival of revoked wills
rows.groupReason: General revival mechanism (conforming will or codicil showing intention) and the partial-then-total revocation limitation form one inseparable recall unit.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the only two instruments by which a revoked will or part may be revived and explain that reviving a wholly revoked will does not extend to a portion revoked before the total revocation absent contrary intention.

evidenceText: is revived only
the revival does not extend to the part that was revoked before the revocation of the whole

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 19 states one coherent rule: the exclusive methods for reviving a revoked will (19(1)) and the limitation on revival where partial revocation preceded total revocation (19(2)). Both subsections are tightly interdependent and answer a single recall task.

rows.heading: Subsequent conveyance, ademption
rows.groupTitle: Post-will conveyance does not prevent will operation
rows.groupReason: Standalone anti-ademption rule: a post-will conveyance or act does not defeat the will as to any estate the testator could still dispose of at death.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: State the rule in s. 20(1) that a conveyance or act made after the will does not prevent the will's operation over property the testator still had power to dispose of by will at death.

evidenceText: does not prevent operation of the will with respect to any estate or interest in the property that the testator had power to dispose of by will at the time of his death

rows.sourceMapReason: The three subsections address distinct triggers and legal effects: post-will conveyance defeating the will, the devisee's interest when only a contractual right remains at death, and anti-ademption of commingled sale proceeds. Each is independently recallable.

rows.heading: Subsequent conveyance, ademption
rows.groupTitle: Devisee takes contractual or equitable interest at death
rows.groupReason: Distinct rule for when the testator holds only a contractual right or equitable interest created by a post-will contract: the devisee steps into that interest rather than the property itself.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Explain under s. 20(2) what the devisee or donee takes when, at death, the testator holds only a right or chose in action or equitable estate or interest arising from a post-will contract, subject to any contrary intention in the will.

rows.sourceMapReason: The three subsections address distinct triggers and legal effects: post-will conveyance defeating the will, the devisee's interest when only a contractual right remains at death, and anti-ademption of commingled sale proceeds. Each is independently recallable.

rows.heading: Effect of failure of inter-vivos gift

rows.heading: Devise includes leasehold and freehold estates

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 23 states one coherent rule of construction: a devise of land includes leasehold as well as freehold estates, subject to contrary intention, across four descriptive scenarios that all reach the same inclusion result. This is a single recallable legal concept.

rows.heading: Devise or bequest includes property that testator has power to appoint

rows.heading: Devise passes whole of estate

rows.heading: Devise or bequest to the “heir” of the testator

rows.sourceMapReason: Section 26 is a short, self-contained interpretive rule defining 'heir' in wills by reference to intestacy distribution and clarifying the inclusion of adopted persons; its parts are tightly interdependent and form one recallable concept.

rows.groupTitle: Arbitration and Non-Waiver Provisions
rows.groupReason: Clauses 40 and 41 establish the three-arbitrator dispute-resolution mechanism with Court of King's Bench appointment as fallback, and the non-waiver rule preserving the lessor's rights despite any prior condonation of default.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the arbitration procedure (mutual appointment, joint third appointment, two-of-three majority binding, Court of King's Bench appointment on default) and the rule that condoning a default does not constitute a waiver of the lessor's rights for continuing or subsequent breaches.

evidenceText: either party hereto shall be entitled to give to the other party notice of such dispute and demand arbitration thereof and, after giving notice and demand, each party shall at once appoint an arbitrator and such appointees shall jointly appoint a third; the decision of any two of the three arbitrators so appointed shall be final and binding

Any condoning, excusing or overlooking by the lessor of any default, breach or non-observance by the lessee at any time or times in respect of any covenant, proviso or condition herein contained shall not operate as a waiver of the lessor's rights hereunder

rows.groupTitle: Casualty, Holdover, and Operational Premises Provisions
rows.groupReason: Clauses 34–39 cover casualty abatement and termination, holdover as a monthly tenancy, the lessor's right to modify pipes and conduits, common-area use, the lessor's non-liability except for negligence, and lessee signage rights.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the proportional rent abatement for partial casualty and termination for total casualty, the holdover monthly-tenancy rule with one month's notice, the lessor's pipe-and-conduit modification right with a non-interference limit, common-area use rights, the lessor's non-liability except for negligence, and the lessee's signage installation and removal rights.

evidenceText: If the demised premises are rendered partially unfit for the lessee by fire, lightning, tempest or other insurable casualty, the rent hereby reserved shall abate in part only in the proportion that the part of the demised premises rendered unfit for the lessee bears to the whole of the demised premises, or if the demised premises are rendered wholly unfit for the lessee, this lease shall be terminated

In the event that the lessee holds over beyond the duration of this lease or the renewal thereof with or without the consent of the lessor and without any further written agreement, the tenancy resulting shall be a monthly tenancy only

The lessor shall have the right to make changes or additions to the pipes, conduits and ducts in the demised premises where necessary to serve adjoining premises but not in a way to interfere materially with the use and enjoyment of the demised premises

rows.groupTitle: Payment Default, Forfeiture, and Bankruptcy Triggers
rows.groupReason: Clauses 26 and 27 establish the lessor's pay-and-recover remedy for payment default and the acceleration, forfeiture, and re-entry consequences triggered by execution, assignment for creditors, bankruptcy, or insolvency.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the lessor's right to pay a defaulted amount and recover it as rent with incidental remedies, and the triggers (execution, assignment for creditors, bankruptcy, insolvency) that accelerate four months' rent and give the lessor the option to forfeit and re-enter.

evidenceText: In the event that the lessee is in default of payment of any amount required by this lease to be paid by him, the lessor may pay such amount on his behalf and recover that amount together with his reasonable expenses from the lessee as rent, with all remedies incidental thereto

In the event that the rights of the lessee under this lease are at any time seized or taken in execution or attachment by any creditor of the lessee, or the lessee makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, becomes bankrupt or insolvent, or takes the benefit of any statute that may be in force for bankrupt or insolvent debtors, then the current month's rent, including additional rent, and the next three month's rent, including additional rent, immediately become due and payable

rows.groupTitle: Lessee's Insurance Obligation, Subrogation Waiver, and Insurable Interest
rows.groupReason: Clauses 23, 33, and 42 together define the lessee's obligation to maintain public liability and property damage insurance, the lessee's insurable interest in improvements, and the mandatory waiver of subrogation and release of claims against the lessor for insured perils.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the lessee's insurance obligation (coverage type, named parties, at lessee's expense), the lessee's insurable interest in alterations and improvements, and the mandatory subrogation waiver releasing all claims against the lessor arising from insured perils.

evidenceText: the lessee shall at his own expense take out and keep in force public liability and property damage insurance in the names of the lessor and the lessee for injury, death or property damage occurring in, or arising in connection with the operation of, the demised premises, with all inclusive coverage

the lessee has an insurable interest in any alterations, additions and improvements that may be made by the lessee in and to the demised premises, and the lessee is entitled to insure such alterations, additions and improvements up to their full insurable value

All policies of insurance placed by the lessee shall contain a waiver or waivers of subrogation against the lessor and the lessee waives, releases and discharges all rights, claims and demands whatsoever which the lessee might have or acquire against the lessor

rows.groupTitle: Lessor's Covenants and Rights
rows.groupReason: Clauses 28–31 set out the lessor's reciprocal obligations: quiet enjoyment, building-level insurance including mortgagee-required risks, payment of property taxes with stated exclusions, and the right to assign the lease as collateral security with a consent requirement for modification.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the lessor's covenant of quiet enjoyment, the scope of the lessor's building insurance obligation, the lessor's tax-payment duty and its exclusions, and the effect of the lessor's collateral assignment requiring assignee consent for lease modification.

evidenceText: the lessee, paying the rent hereby reserved and performing the covenants on his part to be performed, shall and may peaceably possess and enjoy the demised premises for the duration of this lease without any interruption or disturbance from the lessor or any person lawfully claiming under him

the lessor shall effect fire and extended coverage insurance and insurance against all other risks required to be insured against by a mortgagee, if any, as well as boiler and pressure vessel insurance

the lessor shall pay all taxes and rates, including local improvement rates, local government, provincial, federal or otherwise, assessed against the demised premises or the lessor or lessee on account thereof, save and except any business taxes and taxes upon the personal property and income of the lessee
The lessor may assign his rights under this lease as collateral security for a loan

rows.groupReason: Clauses 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 21, and 25 establish the lessee's ongoing obligations regarding repair, entry for inspection, restrictions on alterations, permitted use, statutory compliance, insurance-affecting activities, and reputable business conduct.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the lessee's maintenance duty with its exceptions, the consent requirement for alterations or improvements, the use restriction, the statutory-compliance duty, the prohibition on insurance-affecting activities, the lessor's right of entry for repair inspection, and the reputable-conduct obligation.

evidenceText: maintain the demised premises in good and sufficient order and repair to the satisfaction of the lessor, reasonable wear and tear and damage by fire, lightning, tempest and the like excepted

the lessee shall not, without the prior written consent of the lessor, place any building, erection, addition or improvement, other than trade fixtures, upon the demised premises, or alter the interior
the lessee shall use the demised premises only for the purpose or purposes agreed upon by the lessor and lessee
the lessee shall promptly comply with and conform to the requirements of every federal and provincial statute, rule, regulation and ordinance, and every local government by-law

rows.groupTitle: Lessee's Rent and Financial Payment Obligations
rows.groupReason: Clauses 11, 20, 22, and 24 collectively define what the lessee must pay: base rent without deduction, public utilities, premises taxes and levies, and additional rent for common-area and building costs.
rows.approximateLearningGoal: Identify each category of payment the lessee owes under the statutory lease covenants and the conditions attached to each, including no-deduction rent, utilities as they become due, premises taxes, and proportion-based common-area and building insurance/heating costs.

evidenceText: the lessee shall for the duration of this lease pay to the lessor the rent hereby reserved on the days and in the manner herein set out without any deduction whatsoever
the lessee shall pay to the lessor as additional rent in each year of the term hereby demised his proportion of (a) the total annual cost of operating and maintaining the common area
the lessee shall pay as they become due all charges for public utilities including electricity, gas, water, telephone
the lessee shall pay for the duration of this lease all taxes, rates, levies and assessments charged against the demised premises

rows.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the consent requirement (not to be unreasonably withheld) for assignment or subletting, the vacant-possession obligation, the lessor's right of entry to show premises to prospective tenants and purchasers, and the lessee's right to remove trade fixtures while making good any damage.

evidenceText: the lessee shall not, without the written consent of the lessor, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, assign, transfer, set over, sublet or otherwise by any act or deed cause or permit the demised premises or any part thereof to be assigned, transferred, sublet or set over

the lessee shall upon the expiration or other sooner determination of this lease peaceably deliver to the lessor vacant possession of the demised premises in the condition in which the lessee is by this lease required to maintain the demised premises

the lessee may at or prior to the termination of this lease, take, remove and carry away from the demised premises all fixtures, fittings, plant, machinery, utensils, shelving, counters, safes or other articles placed in or on the premises in the nature of trade or tenants' fixtures
